items.title: Welcome Muse Spark Open: open-weight frontier multimodal mixture-of-experts model from Meta
items.body:
Following Muse Glimmer, Muse Spark Open introduces a mixture-of-experts architecture at a much larger scale, and the most capable US open-weights model to date.

Meta trained Muse Spark Open for agentic coding: reading a codebase, writing and debugging code, and calling tools. It also takes images, audio, and video as input, so the same model can read a screenshot, listen to a voice note, or watch a screen recording while it works on your code. This post shows you how to run it, how to fine-tune it, and what we built with it. Find all the models here.

Overall Capabilities and Architecture

Meta describes Muse Spark Open as a coding-optimized model trained on real developer workflows such as multi-file refactors and long debugging sessions. Muse Spark Open is an agentic focused model that plans, acts, observes, and self-corrects over long tasks, including browsing the web with images.

The checkpoint repositories are Muse-Spark-Open-816B-A42B and Muse-Spark-Open-816B-A42B-NVFP4.

Muse Spark Open is the full-size model of the Muse series of models. Muse Glimmer, which Meta released in August, is a small dense model from the same series, ideal for running locally. Both models use the same tokenizer and vocabulary. The chat template follows the Muse Glimmer template, with additions for the new modalities. In Muse Spark Open the input embedding and the output layer are separate matrices of about 1.66B parameters each.

The language model has 62 layers and a hidden dimension of 8192. Each layer has 128 query heads and 16 key-value heads (grouped-query attention). Each head has 64 dimensions. The attention block has an output gate and an output normalization layer. The model also applies normalization to the queries and the keys (QK-norm). Each block combines its input and its output through a learned residual gate, not through a plain sum.

Muse Glimmer uses one dense feed-forward network in each layer. Muse Spark Open replaces this dense network with a Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) block. Each MoE block has 256 experts, and a router selects 8 experts for each token. Each expert is a feed-forward network that projects from 8192 to 4096 dimensions and back to 8192, then applies its own normalization to its output. The experts hold ~97% of the total model parameters.

Only 8 experts run per token, so the model computes each token with about 42B parameters. All 256 experts stay in memory, so deployment needs the memory of an 816B-parameter model, but runs at the much faster speed of a 42B model. The BF16 checkpoint is about 1.5 TB in safetensors format. The NVFP4 checkpoint stores the parameters in 4-bit precision with negligible loss in accuracy, specifically for NVIDIA Blackwell GPUs. In transformers, the BF16 checkpoint runs across 4 nodes of 8 H200 GPUs with tensor parallelism (TP=32) and the NVFP4 runs on a single B200 node. If you want to deploy Muse Spark Open, check out the llama.cpp, vLLM, and SGLang recipes below.

A perception encoder converts images and video frames into tokens for the language model, just like Muse Glimmer. The encoder has 1.8B parameters, 50 layers, a hidden dimension of 1536, and 16 attention heads. It splits each image into 14×14 patches and produces features with 4096 dimensions. Position information comes from learned absolute embeddings and 2D RoPE. The feed-forward network in each layer uses LayerNorm and GELU. Every fourth layer and the last layer use full attention, and the other layers use sparse attention.

Muse Glimmer 30B uses an encoder with the same architecture. The design follows the Perception Encoder work from Meta. Video input goes through the same encoder as images.

Muse Spark Open accepts audio as input through its audio encoder. An audio tokenizer converts the audio into tokens, and the chat template marks the audio position with <|audio|> tokens. The encoder emits one audio token every 80 ms, which yields 12.5 tokens per second. So let’s say, you have an audio of 10 seconds, the number of input audio tokens would be 125. The encoder itself is a convolutional pyramid where each stage consists of a patch embedder of different patch sizes and 2 convolutional blocks of 1d kernels of size 7 with stride of 1. These stages are repeated for patch sizes of [16, 6, 5, 4]. At the end of the final stage, the temporal frames are fed to a final block of RMSNorm → linear projection → RMSNorm.

The context window is 1M tokens at inference. The configuration sets max_position_embeddings to 1,048,576. This includes image, video, and audio tokens in the same window as text.

Grouped-query attention keeps the KV cache small for a model of this size. Each token adds 2 × 16 heads × 64 dimensions × 62 layers = 126,976 values to the cache. In BF16, this is about 250 KB per token and about 266 GB for a full 1M-token context.

The Muse Spark Open implementation provides MuseSparkForConditionalGeneration for text generation from multimodal inputs and MuseSparkProcessor for preparing conversations. The processor combines the tokenizer, image and video processors, audio feature extractor, and chat template.

Use a DistributedConfig to configure the parallelism settings. tp_size is the number of devices across which the dense layers are sharded, and ep_size is the number of devices across which the experts are distributed.

You can initialize the model and processor as follows.

import os from transformers import AutoModelForMultimodalLM, AutoTokenizer, DistributedConfig distributed_config = DistributedConfig( tp_size=int(os.environ["WORLD_SIZE"]), ep_size=int(os.environ["WORLD_SIZE"]), ) tokenizer = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained("meta-models/Muse-Spark-Open-816B-A42B ") model = AutoModelForMultimodalLM.from_pretrained( "meta-models/Muse-Spark-Open-816B-A42B", distributed_config=distributed_config, ) messages = [ {"role": "user", "content": "Explain in one sentence why the sky is usually blue."}, ] inputs = tokenizer.apply_chat_template( messages, reasoning_effort="medium", # default: xhigh, options: low/medium/high/xhigh add_generation_prompt=True, tokenize=True, return_dict=True, return_tensors="pt", ).to(model.device).to(model.dtype) input_len = inputs["input_ids"].shape[-1] outputs = model.generate(**inputs, max_new_tokens=2000)

Prepare the conversation, then pass the messages to processor.apply_chat_template, enabling add_generation_prompt=True, tokenize=True, return_dict=True, and return_tensors="pt". Pass the processor output to model.generate and decode the newly generated tokens, excluding the input prefix. The processor has a lever for the reasoning effort, mapping symbolic levels (low/medium/high/xhigh) to the integers the model itself accepts (16, 64, 256, 512). Note that turning off reasoning is not possible with Muse Spark Open, so keep the model reasoning at “low” if you want to consume less tokens to solve an easier task. You can also set a numeric effort by including a line like Reasoning strength: 1 in the system prompt.

messages = [ {"role": "system", "content": "You should only answer with a number."}, {"role": "user", "content": "What is 17 * 23?"}, ] inputs = processor.apply_chat_template( messages, add_generation_prompt=True, tokenize=True, return_dict=True, return_tensors="pt", reasoning_effort="high", # options:low/medium/high/xhigh ).to(model.device).to(model.dtype) output = model.generate(**inputs, max_new_tokens=2000) generated_tokens = output[0][inputs["input_ids"].shape[1] :] print(processor.decode(generated_tokens, skip_special_tokens=False))

The Muse Spark Open processor expands each image marker into the number of patch tokens required by the processed image, surrounded by image boundary tokens. This expansion keeps the text positions aligned with the visual features passed to the model. The processor also handles multiple images within a single prompt.

items.body_ko:
Muse Glimmer에 이어, Muse Spark Open은 훨씬 더 큰 규모의 전문가 혼합(Mixture-of-Experts) 아키텍처를 도입했으며, 현재까지 미국에서 가장 유능한 오픈 가중치 모델입니다.

Meta는 Muse Spark Open을 에이전트 코딩(코드를 읽고, 코드를 작성 및 디버깅하며, 도구를 호출하는 작업)을 위해 훈련했습니다. 또한 이미지, 오디오, 비디오를 입력으로 받아, 동일한 모델이 코드를 작업하는 동안 스크린샷을 읽거나, 음성 메모를 듣거나, 화면 녹화를 시청할 수 있습니다. 이 게시물에서는 모델 실행 방법, 미세 조정 방법, 그리고 이 모델로 무엇을 만들었는지 보여줍니다. 모든 모델은 여기에서 찾을 수 있습니다.

전반적인 기능 및 아키텍처

Meta는 Muse Spark Open을 다중 파일 리팩터링 및 장기 디버깅 세션과 같은 실제 개발자 워크플로에 최적화된 코딩 모델로 설명합니다. Muse Spark Open은 이미지를 사용하여 웹을 탐색하는 것을 포함하여 긴 작업에 걸쳐 계획하고, 행동하고, 관찰하고, 자체 수정하는 에이전트 중심 모델입니다.

체크포인트 저장소는 Muse-Spark-Open-816B-A42B 및 Muse-Spark-Open-816B-A42B-NVFP4입니다.

Muse Spark Open은 Muse 모델 시리즈의 전체 크기 모델입니다. Meta가 8월에 출시한 Muse Glimmer는 동일 시리즈의 작은 밀집 모델로, 로컬에서 실행하기에 이상적입니다. 두 모델 모두 동일한 토크나이저와 어휘를 사용합니다. 채팅 템플릿은 새로운 모달리티를 위한 추가 기능을 포함하여 Muse Glimmer 템플릿을 따릅니다. Muse Spark Open에서 입력 임베딩과 출력 레이어는 각각 약 1.66B 매개변수의 별도 행렬입니다.

언어 모델은 62개의 레이어와 8192의 숨겨진 차원을 가집니다. 각 레이어에는 128개의 쿼리 헤드와 16개의 키-값 헤드(그룹 쿼리 어텐션)가 있습니다. 각 헤드는 64개의 차원을 가집니다. 어텐션 블록에는 출력 게이트와 출력 정규화 레이어가 있습니다. 모델은 또한 쿼리와 키에 정규화(QK-norm)를 적용합니다. 각 블록은 학습된 잔차 게이트를 통해 입력과 출력을 결합하며, 단순 합이 아닙니다.

Muse Glimmer는 각 레이어에 하나의 밀집 피드 포워드 네트워크를 사용합니다. Muse Spark Open은 이 밀집 네트워크를 전문가 혼합(MoE) 블록으로 대체합니다. 각 MoE 블록은 256개의 전문가를 가지며, 라우터는 각 토큰에 대해 8개의 전문가를 선택합니다. 각 전문가는 8192에서 4096 차원으로 투영하고 다시 8192로 투영하는 피드 포워드 네트워크이며, 자체 출력에 자체 정규화를 적용합니다. 전문가들은 전체 모델 매개변수의 약 97%를 차지합니다.

토큰당 8개의 전문가만 실행되므로, 모델은 약 42B 매개변수로 각 토큰을 계산합니다. 256개의 모든 전문가가 메모리에 유지되므로 배포에는 816B 매개변수 모델의 메모리가 필요하지만, 42B 모델보다 훨씬 빠른 속도로 실행됩니다. BF16 체크포인트는 safetensors 형식으로 약 1.5 TB입니다. NVFP4 체크포인트는 특히 NVIDIA Blackwell GPU를 위해 정확도 손실이 거의 없이 4비트 정밀도로 매개변수를 저장합니다. 트랜스포머에서 BF16 체크포인트는 8개의 H200 GPU를 가진 4개의 노드에 걸쳐 텐서 병렬 처리(TP=32)로 실행되며, NVFP4는 단일 B200 노드에서 실행됩니다. Muse Spark Open을 배포하려면 아래 llama.cpp, vLLM, SGLang 레시피를 확인하십시오.

인지 인코더는 Muse Glimmer와 마찬가지로 이미지와 비디오 프레임을 언어 모델용 토큰으로 변환합니다. 인코더는 1.8B 매개변수, 50개 레이어, 1536의 숨겨진 차원, 그리고 16개의 어텐션 헤드를 가집니다. 각 이미지를 14x14 패치로 분할하고 4096 차원의 특징을 생성합니다. 위치 정보는 학습된 절대 임베딩과 2D RoPE에서 나옵니다. 각 레이어의 피드 포워드 네트워크는 LayerNorm과 GELU를 사용합니다. 네 번째 레이어마다 그리고 마지막 레이어는 전체 어텐션을 사용하며, 다른 레이어는 희소 어텐션을 사용합니다.

Muse Glimmer 30B는 동일한 아키텍처를 가진 인코더를 사용합니다. 이 디자인은 Meta의 Perception Encoder 작업을 따릅니다. 비디오 입력은 이미지와 동일한 인코더를 통과합니다.

Muse Spark Open은 오디오 인코더를 통해 오디오를 입력으로 받습니다. 오디오 토크나이저는 오디오를 토큰으로 변환하고, 채팅 템플릿은 <|audio|> 토큰으로 오디오 위치를 표시합니다. 인코더는 80ms마다 하나의 오디오 토큰을 방출하며, 이는 초당 12.5 토큰에 해당합니다. 따라서 10초 길이의 오디오가 있다면, 입력 오디오 토큰 수는 125개가 됩니다. 인코더 자체는 각 단계가 다른 패치 크기의 패치 임베더와 1의 보폭을 가진 크기 7의 1d 커널 2개의 컨볼루션 블록으로 구성된 컨볼루션 피라미드입니다. 이러한 단계는 [16, 6, 5, 4] 패치 크기에 대해 반복됩니다. 최종 단계가 끝날 때, 시간 프레임은 RMSNorm → 선형 투영 → RMSNorm의 최종 블록으로 공급됩니다.

추론 시 컨텍스트 창은 1M 토큰입니다. 구성은 max_position_embeddings를 1,048,576으로 설정합니다. 여기에는 텍스트와 동일한 창에 이미지, 비디오, 오디오 토큰이 포함됩니다.

그룹 쿼리 어텐션은 이 크기의 모델에 대해 KV 캐시를 작게 유지합니다. 각 토큰은 캐시에 2 × 16 헤드 × 64 차원 × 62 레이어 = 126,976개의 값을 추가합니다. BF16에서 이는 토큰당 약 250KB이고, 전체 1M 토큰 컨텍스트의 경우 약 266GB입니다.

Muse Spark Open 구현은 멀티모달 입력에서 텍스트 생성을 위한 MuseSparkForConditionalGeneration과 대화 준비를 위한 MuseSparkProcessor를 제공합니다. 프로세서는 토크나이저, 이미지 및 비디오 프로세서, 오디오 특징 추출기, 채팅 템플릿을 결합합니다.

DistributedConfig를 사용하여 병렬 처리 설정을 구성하십시오. tp_size는 밀집 레이어가 분할되는 장치 수이고, ep_size는 전문가가 분산되는 장치 수입니다.

다음과 같이 모델과 프로세서를 초기화할 수 있습니다.

items.title: Muse Spark Open
items.body:
Muse Spark Open is available today and brings leading agentic capabilities to your desktop for the first time on Apple M5 Ultra Mac Studios.

Today, we’re releasing the weights for Muse Spark Open, the most capable US open-weight model to date. Muse Spark Open is a natively multimodal model with 816B total parameters (42B active) and a 1M-token context window. Built for coding and agentic work, it excels at long-horizon tasks, complex software engineering, and multi-step reasoning.

We believe the future is for everyone, and that includes the freedom to run advanced models wherever, including at home. Muse Spark Open is the first model in its class to run on your desktop using two Apple M5 Ultra Mac Studios with the latest MLX framework.

Muse Spark Open is available today through API platforms at Baseten, Fireworks AI, Groq, Modal, Nebius, OpenRouter and Together AI. Model weights are available for download on Amazon SageMaker AI, Google Cloud Model Garden, Hugging Face, and Microsoft Foundry Models.

It runs on leading inference engines like SGLang, vLLM, TensorRT-LLM, Hugging Face Transformers, Apple MLX, llama.cpp, and Unsloth with optimizations for AMD, Apple, Intel, and NVIDIA silicon. Developers can easily further customize the model using the PyTorch framework.

For more details about our evaluations, see the evaluation methodology report.

Leveraging the latest version of MLX, Muse Spark Open was optimized to run on Mac Studio with M5 Ultra, and together they’re the best way to run a powerful model on your own desktop.

Apple’s unified memory architecture lets the M5 Ultra's integrated GPU use up to 512 GB per Mac Studio, so two machines can hold an entire model. And the chip’s 1.2 TB/s of memory bandwidth is fast enough to read the small slice each token needs. The result is two Mac Studios behave like one supercomputer with a terabyte of unified memory.

We tested a range of agentic workflows running entirely on-device, using Muse Code powered by Muse Spark Open, including shipping real iOS changes to Ice Cubes (an open-source Mastodon client) — bug fixes, new features, full build — and driving DaVinci Resolve end to end, with the model reviewing footage frame by frame to find the strongest moments and crop them vertically.

We’re sharing this work because we want everyone to have access to the best models. The open-weight version of Muse Spark ships with custom, auto-tunable Helion GPU kernels in SGLang, delivering 1.03-3.95× kernel-level speedups on NVIDIA and AMD GPUs, and a 3% end-to-end speedup on AMD MI350.

Releasing open-weight models is part of how we bring the benefits of personal superintelligence to everyone, and part of how safety work advances across the field.

Open weights also carry their own considerations, and Muse Spark Open has additional safety post-training for that reason. The results demonstrate strong safeguards across risk categories measured.

We evaluated the model in line with our Meta Superintelligence Scaling Framework, covering the most severe risks, and it met the thresholds our framework requires for release. Detailed results are in the Muse Spark Open model card, with a full evaluation report available soon.

We’re releasing the weights under the Muse Model License with limited commercial terms, which allow many developers to use the model for free.

You can customize Muse Spark Open for your use case by leveraging PyTorch’s TorchTitan to further tune the model. To run it on Apple silicon, use MLX, which pulls the weights directly from Hugging Face.

Muse Spark Open is available now through Hugging Face: https://huggingface.co/collections/meta-models/muse-spark-open

MLX Adapter for running Muse Spark Open on Mac Studio.

Hosted Inference Partners: Together AI, Fireworks, Baseten, Modal, Groq, Nebius, and OpenRouter.

Built or published something with Muse Spark Open? Share with us on the Hugging Face Forums — we’d love to see what you create.
items.body_ko:
Muse Spark Open은 오늘 출시되며, Apple M5 Ultra Mac Studio에서 처음으로 데스크톱에 선도적인 에이전트 기능을 제공합니다.

오늘, 우리는 현재까지 미국에서 가장 유능한 오픈 가중치 모델인 Muse Spark Open의 가중치를 공개합니다. Muse Spark Open은 총 816B 매개변수(활성 42B)와 1M 토큰 컨텍스트 창을 가진 네이티브 멀티모달 모델입니다. 코딩 및 에이전트 작업을 위해 구축되었으며, 장기적인 작업, 복잡한 소프트웨어 엔지니어링 및 다단계 추론에 탁월합니다.

우리는 미래가 모두를 위한 것이며, 여기에는 집을 포함하여 어디에서든 고급 모델을 실행할 자유가 포함된다고 믿습니다. Muse Spark Open은 최신 MLX 프레임워크를 사용하여 두 대의 Apple M5 Ultra Mac Studio에서 데스크톱으로 실행되는 동급 최초의 모델입니다.

Muse Spark Open은 Baseten, Fireworks AI, Groq, Modal, Nebius, OpenRouter 및 Together AI의 API 플랫폼을 통해 오늘부터 사용할 수 있습니다. 모델 가중치는 Amazon SageMaker AI, Google Cloud Model Garden, Hugging Face 및 Microsoft Foundry Models에서 다운로드할 수 있습니다.

이 모델은 SGLang, vLLM, TensorRT-LLM, Hugging Face Transformers, Apple MLX, llama.cpp 및 Unsloth와 같은 선도적인 추론 엔진에서 실행되며, AMD, Apple, Intel 및 NVIDIA 실리콘에 최적화되어 있습니다. 개발자는 PyTorch 프레임워크를 사용하여 모델을 쉽게 더 커스터마이징할 수 있습니다.

평가에 대한 자세한 내용은 평가 방법론 보고서를 참조하십시오.

MLX의 최신 버전을 활용하여 Muse Spark Open은 M5 Ultra가 장착된 Mac Studio에서 실행되도록 최적화되었으며, 이 둘은 자체 데스크톱에서 강력한 모델을 실행하는 가장 좋은 방법입니다.

Apple의 통합 메모리 아키텍처는 M5 Ultra의 통합 GPU가 Mac Studio당 최대 512GB를 사용할 수 있도록 하여, 두 대의 머신이 전체 모델을 담을 수 있게 합니다. 그리고 칩의 1.2TB/s 메모리 대역폭은 각 토큰에 필요한 작은 조각을 읽을 만큼 충분히 빠릅니다. 그 결과 두 대의 Mac Studio는 1테라바이트의 통합 메모리를 가진 하나의 슈퍼컴퓨터처럼 작동합니다.

Muse Spark Open으로 구동되는 Muse Code를 사용하여 Ice Cubes(오픈 소스 Mastodon 클라이언트)에 실제 iOS 변경 사항을 배포하는 것(버그 수정, 새 기능, 전체 빌드 포함)과 DaVinci Resolve를 처음부터 끝까지 구동하는 것(모델이 프레임별로 영상을 검토하여 가장 강력한 순간을 찾아 세로로 자르는 것)을 포함하여 완전히 온디바이스에서 실행되는 다양한 에이전트 워크플로를 테스트했습니다.

우리는 모든 사람이 최고의 모델에 접근할 수 있도록 이 작업을 공유합니다. Muse Spark의 오픈 가중치 버전은 SGLang에 커스텀 자동 튜닝 가능한 Helion GPU 커널과 함께 제공되며, NVIDIA 및 AMD GPU에서 1.03-3.95배의 커널 수준 속도 향상을 제공하고, AMD MI350에서 3%의 종단간 속도 향상을 제공합니다.

오픈 가중치 모델을 출시하는 것은 개인용 슈퍼 인텔리전스의 이점을 모든 사람에게 제공하는 방법이자, 이 분야에서 안전 작업이 발전하는 방법의 일부입니다.

오픈 가중치 역시 자체적인 고려 사항을 가지고 있으며, Muse Spark Open은 그러한 이유로 추가적인 안전 사후 훈련을 받았습니다. 결과는 측정된 위험 범주 전반에 걸쳐 강력한 안전 장치를 보여줍니다.

우리는 Meta Superintelligence Scaling Framework에 따라 가장 심각한 위험을 다루는 모델을 평가했으며, 이 모델은 출시를 위해 프레임워크가 요구하는 임계값을 충족했습니다. 자세한 결과는 Muse Spark Open 모델 카드에 있으며, 전체 평가 보고서는 곧 제공될 예정입니다.

많은 개발자가 모델을 무료로 사용할 수 있도록 제한된 상업적 조건이 포함된 Muse Model License 하에 가중치를 출시합니다.

PyTorch의 TorchTitan을 활용하여 모델을 추가로 튜닝하여 사용 사례에 맞게 Muse Spark Open을 커스터마이징할 수 있습니다. Apple silicon에서 실행하려면 Hugging Face에서 직접 가중치를 가져오는 MLX를 사용하십시오.

Muse Spark Open은 Hugging Face를 통해 지금 사용할 수 있습니다: https://huggingface.co/collections/meta-models/muse-spark-open

Mac Studio에서 Muse Spark Open을 실행하기 위한 MLX 어댑터.

호스팅된 추론 파트너: Together AI, Fireworks, Baseten, Modal, Groq, Nebius 및 OpenRouter.

Muse Spark Open으로 무언가를 만들거나 게시했습니까? Hugging Face 포럼에서 저희와 공유해 주세요. 여러분이 만든 것을 보고 싶습니다.

items.title: Modeling and Understanding Neural Weights of Humanoid Policies with Diffusion
items.body: Recent advances in robot learning have driven rapid progress in humanoid control, enabling increasingly agile behaviors in the real world. However, humanoid control networks are typically obtained through conventional training procedures, while comparatively little attention has been given to directly modeling the distribution of their learned weights and generating functional networks in weight space. In this work, we investigate whether high-performing humanoid control networks can be generatively modeled directly through their weights. We adopt a latent diffusion framework that couples a linear autoencoder with a Diffusion Transformer. The autoencoder compresses actor network parameters into a compact latent space, and the Diffusion Transformer models the distribution of these latents. Trained on networks collected from reinforcement learning for the Unitree G1 robot, our approach generates deployable networks that perform various motions in the real world, including walking, dancing, and spin kick. Beyond generation, we further study the learned weight space to better understand the structure captured by these humanoid control networks. We identify a structural principle in the first-layer weights that consistently reflects the robot's kinematic prior. Notably, this kinematic prior emerges under both Reinforcement Learning (RL) and Imitation Learning (IL) training, suggesting that it is not specific to a particular optimization process but may instead reflect common knowledge associated with humanoid embodiment. Together, these results demonstrate the feasibility of generative modeling in humanoid network weight space, while providing initial insights into the information encoded by their learned weights. Additional results are available on our project website: https://humanoid-weight-diffusion.github.io/

items.title: Hierarchical Residual Policy Learning for Real-World Mobile Manipulation with Sparse Human Guidance
items.body: Mobile Manipulation (MoMa) is a cornerstone of autonomous robotic systems, yet real-world fine-tuning remains a formidable challenge because of high-dimensional action spaces and intricate coupling between heterogeneous modules. In this paper, we propose HiRe-MoMa (Hierarchical Residual Mobile Manipulation), a systematic framework for stable and sample-efficient real-world fine-tuning of complex MoMa systems. At its core, HiRe-MoMa adopts a Hierarchical Residual Architecture that fine-tunes a frozen base policy. A Policy-Agnostic Residual learns additive corrections atop the base policy, while Hierarchical Decoupling splits the residual into mobile-base and manipulator-arm heads with unidirectional conditioning, mitigating gradient interference and aligning corrections with the platform's physical hierarchy. To improve sample efficiency in data-expensive real-world settings, we propose Expert-Guided Value Alignment, which leverages sparse human interventions with under 20% training coverage to reshape the critic's value landscape, effectively guiding autonomous exploration through expert priors. Extensive real-world experiments on the TIAGo++ platform demonstrate that HiRe-MoMa consistently enhances task performance with only around 30 minutes of online interaction, regardless of the base policy architecture. To our knowledge, this is among the first frameworks to enable efficient on-robot fine-tuning for mobile manipulation in the real world, providing a practical paradigm for deploying complex robotic systems in dynamic, human-centric environments. Further details can be found on our project website: https://hire-moma.github.io/

items.title: Co-Evolving Acting and Forecasting for Language Agents
items.body:
Training language agents is bottlenecked by the high cost of long-horizon rollouts, yet standard agentic reinforcement learning (RL) learns only from a terminal scalar reward, leaving the supervision in intermediate steps largely unused. Prior work exploits this supervision through value targets that estimate per-step success probabilities or observation targets that fit environment response. Both are hard to construct well: (1) value targets come from the same single scalar signal for each step in the trajectory, and (2) observation targets, such as web pages and terminal logs, are long and noisy and reach only one step ahead. We propose 
ame, which adds a third kind of multi-step action targets. On successful on-policy trajectories, 
ame trains the policy backbone to generate the action sequences that follows each history. Each action is also supervised when forecast from the preceding histories, forming a temporal ensemble that the shared backbone absorbs during training, and this enables acting and forecasting to co-evolve. The policy still acts one step at a time at inference, with no overhead. Across five benchmarks (ALFWorld, ScienceWorld, WebShop, $τ^2$-bench, and AppWorld), 
ame (1) achieves stronger aggregate performance than GRPO and RL baselines with predictive auxiliary targets across simulated environments, while improving overall performance on both realistic applications; (2) delivers up to $1.9	imes$ and $2.0	imes$ higher sample efficiency than ECHO and GRPO, respectively, on ScienceWorld; and (3) achieves these gains with a single policy backbone, without additional models, separate pretraining, or inference overhead. The codebase is available at https://github.com/ulab-uiuc/CoPE.

items.title: Your Transformer Is Secretly Elastic
items.body: Scaling up transformers has produced models with broad capabilities, deployed across heterogeneous hardware and fluctuating workloads. Yet, model families offer only a few fixed sizes (e.g., S, B, L), forcing users to commit to a model based on hardware and latency constraints. This rigidity is often suboptimal under varying query loads. We introduce a retraining-free method that elastifies pre-trained transformers into a single model that adapts on-the-fly across a continuum of computational budgets. Our key contribution is a differentiable relaxation of the functional unit-ranking problem: unlike prior work, which optimizes a single importance weight per MLP block or attention head, we rank every individual MLP neuron and attention head jointly, on a common scale, by minimizing the model's loss under soft pruning across many sparsity targets, all at once. Across 27 vision and text transformer encoders ranging from 22M to 8B parameters, our method yields smooth degradation up to 60% sparsity and outperforms one-shot baselines under deep pruning. For example, pruning DINOv3 ViT-H+/16 to 50% sparsity removes 427M parameters while reducing ImageNet-1k linear-probing accuracy by only 0.8%, without the need for weight correction or retraining. At 60% sparsity, a pruned AugReg ViT-B/16 model achieves up to $1.80\times$ higher throughput and $1.26\times$ lower single-query latency on an A100 GPU. Elastic models are produced in minutes, with construction time scaling sub-linearly with parameter count.
items.body_ko: 트랜스포머를 확장하면 이종 하드웨어와 변동하는 워크로드에 걸쳐 배포되는 광범위한 기능을 가진 모델이 생성됩니다. 그러나 모델 제품군은 몇 가지 고정된 크기(예: S, B, L)만 제공하므로 사용자는 하드웨어 및 지연 시간 제약 조건에 따라 모델을 선택해야 합니다. 이러한 경직성은 다양한 쿼리 부하에서 종종 최적화되지 않습니다. 우리는 사전 훈련된 트랜스포머를 컴퓨팅 예산의 연속체에 걸쳐 즉석에서 적응하는 단일 모델로 유연화하는 재훈련 없는 방법을 소개합니다. 우리의 주요 기여는 기능 단위 순위 문제의 미분 가능한 완화입니다. 즉, 이전 작업이 MLP 블록 또는 어텐션 헤드당 단일 중요도 가중치를 최적화하는 것과 달리, 우리는 많은 스파스성 목표에 걸쳐 소프트 가지치기 하에서 모델의 손실을 한 번에 최소화함으로써 모든 개별 MLP 뉴런과 어텐션 헤드를 공통된 척도로 함께 순위를 매깁니다. 22M에서 8B 매개변수에 이르는 27개의 비전 및 텍스트 트랜스포머 인코더에서 우리의 방법은 최대 60%의 스파스성까지 부드러운 성능 저하를 나타내며 깊은 가지치기에서 원샷 기준선을 능가합니다. 예를 들어, DINOv3 ViT-H+/16을 50% 스파스성으로 가지치기하면 427M 매개변수가 제거되지만 ImageNet-1k 선형 프로빙 정확도는 0.8%만 감소하며, 가중치 수정이나 재훈련이 필요하지 않습니다. 60% 스파스성에서 가지치기된 AugReg ViT-B/16 모델은 A100 GPU에서 최대 1.80배 더 높은 처리량과 1.26배 더 낮은 단일 쿼리 지연 시간을 달성합니다. 탄력적인 모델은 몇 분 안에 생성되며, 구성 시간은 매개변수 수에 따라 준선형적으로 증가합니다.

items.title: Price of Anarchy of First-Price Auctions in Agentic Markets
items.body: An agentic market is a decentralized serving-time market where AI agents bid to claim each user prompt. An agent's bid is based on its expected value for the prompt, which is the expectation of the reward for its response minus its inference costs. First-price auctions (FPAs), in which the highest bidder pays its bid and receives the prompt, are a natural way to allocate prompts in such a market, since they are simple and transparent to run, and do not require central knowledge of private capabilities and costs. However, FPAs are not truthful: participants may bid less than their true value in the hope of a larger profit, and the prompt may then be allocated to someone other than the bidder who values it the most. This welfare loss is quantified by the $\textit{price-of-anarchy}$ (PoA). In this paper, we argue that agentic markets are likely to possess features that reduce the price-of-anarchy. The first is a $\textit{competitive floor}$, which occurs when multiple bidders usually value the prompt above some baseline share of the optimal welfare (e.g., because the best models are often distilled into cheaper alternatives, which perform similarly). We show that competition among them then limits the welfare loss, which can be driven to zero as the floor rises. The second feature is $\textit{near-independence}$ of values after conditioning on the prompt, which occurs when most of the predictable variation in the expected value is determined by the difficulty of the prompt. As the value distribution approaches conditional independence, we can derive an efficiency guarantee that approaches a factor of $1 - 1/e^2$ of the optimal welfare. Thus, both features give rise to welfare lower bounds that are significantly better than the well-known general case of $1 - 1/e$. We validate these results empirically using auctions with strategic bidders simulated on the EmbedLLM prompt routing dataset.

items.title: Continuum Attention
items.body: We introduce Continuum Attention (CA), a causal Transformer attention operator that replaces discrete key and value lookup with integration over a continuous, piecewise linear memory curve. Each query induces an exponential relevance density along the curve. Integrating the density and interpolated values yields exact normalized attention from closed form exponential moments, including half token boundary contributions. The gradients follow analytically from moments of order at most two, enabling parallel GPU implementations while retaining quadratic sequence complexity and the standard Transformer decoder. Compared with ordinary softmax and focal attention, CA reduces mean validation negative log likelihood by 0.0200 and 0.0480 nats per byte, respectively, winning all paired comparisons. An additional disjoint validation slice yields a 0.0457 nats per byte advantage over the strongest selected softmax baseline, with a paired 95% confidence interval. These findings motivate continuous integration as a promising attention alternative while leaving larger scale generalization open.

items.title: Learnable Hodge-Laplacian Driven Mixture of Experts for Steady-PDE Surrogates on Coarse Unstructured Meshes
items.body: Current approaches for steady partial differential equations surrogate models on unstructured meshes apply a single mixing mechanism to the whole solution. This paper proposes an architecture that partitions the solution among vanilla transformer experts, each focused on a different spectral scale. The partition is built from a discrete Hodge Laplacian $L_0=\star_0^{-1} d_0^{\top}\star_1 d_0$, that serves as a fitting layer measuring high-frequency content. A gating mechanism takes the mesh as input and produces the per-vertex weights that recombine the expert outputs. AirFRANS is a steady Reynolds-averaged Navier--Stokes (RANS) airfoil benchmark. We evaluate our approach in a reduced remeshed version of the benchmark with each unstructured mesh counting 9.6K faces and 4.9K vertices. We compare our approach with the Transolver on the same dataset and dataset slit. Our approach reduces relative $L_2$ error by 31\% and interior mean squared error by 47\%.

items.title: Player-1: Learning to Play from Synthetic Experience
items.body: Computer-use agents have demonstrated strong capabilities in interpreting screens and executing keyboard and mouse actions. However, games, with their visually rich worlds and diverse mechanics, remain challenging and offer a demanding next step toward general digital control. Current game-agent learning pipelines often rely on large-scale demonstrations with limited coverage of dynamic game states, while scalable environments for interactive training remain difficult to obtain. We introduce Player-1, a post-training framework for learning game control beyond demonstrations through synthetic experience. We extend the computer-use action space with relative pointer motion, sustained inputs, and composite actions. For supervised initialization, we fine-tune computer-use models on 6,044 curated gameplay trajectories that pair recorded actions with task instructions and visual reasoning. We construct Player-1-Gym, sixteen synthetic 2D and 3D environments designed around control demands shared across games. Programmatically verifiable rewards and randomized observations and control dynamics support multi-environment reinforcement learning with PPO. The resulting Player-1-9B and Player-1-35B-A3B improve MineDojo-300 success over their SFT policies by 27.8 and 17.7 percentage points, respectively. Player-1-9B reaches 38.33% success compared with 12.63% for the strongest evaluated baseline, with further gains over SFT on ViZDoom-10 and GameWorld. Further analyses show that broader synthetic environment coverage improves transfer, while the use of composite actions that combine multiple keyboard and mouse inputs increases during RL. We demonstrate that learning from synthetic experience substantially improves game control beyond supervised initialization, with gains that generalize beyond the RL training suite.
items.title_ko: Player-1: 합성 경험을 통한 게임 플레이 학습 에이전트
items.summary_ko: 컴퓨터 사용 에이전트는 화면 해석과 키보드/마우스 액션 실행에서 강력한 능력을 보여주지만, 게임은 여전히 어렵다. 이 연구는 동적으로 풍부한 게임 상태에 대한 대규모 데모 데이터의 한계를 극복하기 위해 합성 경험으로부터 게임 플레이를 학습하는 'Player-1'을 소개한다.
items.why_ko: AI가 복잡한 게임 환경에서 학습하고 행동하는 능력을 향상시키는 새로운 접근법을 제시하며, 이는 일반 디지털 제어 및 실제 환경에서의 로봇 학습에도 영감을 줄 수 있다.

items.title: Latent Compaction with Test-Time Training
items.body: Long contexts enlarge key--value (KV) caches, increasing memory use and attention costs during generation. Compressing these caches must preserve information for unseen questions. We introduce **Latent Compaction**, which learns a compact document-specific cache through test-time training. We initialize cache entries using reconstruction importance, teacher attention, and key-space diversity. Training first fits attention outputs and log-normalizers to those of the full cache, with reconstruction-selected entries held fixed. It then jointly optimizes the entire cache through end-to-end distillation from the full-cache model. Model weights remain frozen throughout, and training uses only generic prompts about the document, without access to downstream questions or answers. Experiments on RULER, LongBench, and Phonebook Lookup demonstrate substantial gains over budget-matched compression baselines. On a RULER, for example, our method achieves 96.7% accuracy at 32$\times$ compression, compared with 40.0% for KVZip+. The method also transfers across model scales and families, with retrieval gains on both Qwen3 and MiniCPM5. These results show that treating the KV cache as a neural network and optimizing it with test-time training can preserve retrieval accuracy under aggressive compression. The code is released at https://www.github.com/THUNLP/latent-compaction
items.title_ko: 테스트 시간 훈련을 통한 잠재 공간 압축으로 장기 컨텍스트 처리 효율 개선
items.summary_ko: 긴 컨텍스트는 KV(Key-Value) 캐시를 늘려 생성 중 메모리 사용과 어텐션 비용을 증가시킨다. Latent Compaction은 테스트 시간 훈련을 통해 문서별 압축 캐시를 학습하여 이 문제를 해결한다.
items.why_ko: LLM의 긴 컨텍스트 처리 시 발생하는 메모리 및 계산 비용 문제를 효율적으로 해결하는 방법으로, 이는 모델의 확장성과 실제 적용 가능성을 크게 높일 수 있다.

items.title: One Task, Many Interfaces: Simple Cross-Interface Consistency Training Improves LLM Agent Robustness
items.body: Post-training binds the competence of an LLM agent to the interface it was trained on. Semantics-preserving perturbations of that interface, such as renaming an action or changing the notation, leave the underlying task unchanged yet make the agent worse at it. Scoring each sample independently means interface randomization only broadens this dependence from a single interface to the training interface distribution, so out-of-distribution perturbations still degrade the agent. We propose Cross-Interface Policy Regularization (CIPR), a self-supervised objective that replaces action names with uninformative identifiers and presents each training sample under two interfaces in which equivalent actions are identified by construction. CIPR penalizes the KL divergence between the action distributions induced under the two interfaces, so the policy behaves consistently across them. We evaluate CIPR in both supervised and reinforcement-learning post-training, where it improves robustness. On agentic function calling, held-out interface perturbations reduce the accuracy of a post-trained agent by nearly 25%, and CIPR recovers 10.5% while leaving accuracy on the unchanged interface intact.
items.title_ko: 단일 작업, 다양한 인터페이스: 교차 인터페이스 일관성 훈련으로 LLM 에이전트 강건성 향상
items.summary_ko: LLM 에이전트의 능력은 훈련된 인터페이스에 강하게 의존한다. 이 연구는 의미론적으로 동일하지만 표현이 다른 인터페이스 간의 일관성 훈련을 통해 LLM 에이전트의 강건성을 향상시키는 방법을 제안한다.
items.why_ko: 다양한 사용자 인터페이스와 상호작용해야 하는 LLM 에이전트의 실용성을 크게 높여주며, 인터페이스 변화에 덜 민감한 견고한 에이전트 개발에 기여한다.

items.title: Beyond LLM Judge: Mechanical Verification for Agentic Autoformalization
items.body: We introduce a novel method for verifying Lean formalizations that goes beyond LLM-judged faithfulness. Unlike most verification methods, which rely on LLMs or trained models, our method combines LLM-based semantic review with mechanical numerical and vacuity checks, providing checkable feedback and detecting errors missed by LLM judges. We apply this method, along with our Extract-Verify-Proof autoformalization pipeline, to construct the Formalized Library of Mathematical Functions (FLMF), a partial formalization of the NIST Digital Library of Mathematical Functions (DLMF). On three labeled datasets, our method achieves the lowest accepted-error rate among the evaluated methods, measured as the fraction of incorrect statements accepted by the verification method. Expert review of the results also identifies translation and source defects in existing datasets. Code available at https://github.com/annamei1/FLMF-Ch7ErrFunc-Release.git.
items.title_ko: LLM 심사관을 넘어: 에이전트 자동 형식화의 기계적 검증
items.summary_ko: 이 연구는 LLM 기반의 의미론적 검토와 기계적 수치 및 공허 검사를 결합하여 Lean 형식화의 검증 방법을 제시한다. 이는 LLM 심사관이 놓칠 수 있는 오류를 탐지하고 검증 가능한 피드백을 제공한다.
items.why_ko: LLM 기반 자동 형식화의 신뢰성을 높이기 위한 중요한 방법론을 제시하며, 이는 수학적 추론 및 소프트웨어 검증과 같은 고정밀 AI 애플리케이션 개발에 필수적이다.

items.title: Recovering Reliable Supervision via Critique-Guided On-Policy Distillation
items.body: On-policy distillation (OPD) trains a student model on its own rollouts with token-level supervision from a teacher, assuming that the teacher can reach a correct answer from any prefix the student writes. We call this property the recoverability of the teacher and show it fails on incorrect rollouts: the teacher follows student errors, although it recognizes them. We propose CriticOPD, using error recognition to restore recoverability. The teacher critiques an incorrect rollout, allowing the student to rewrite its solution following the error. The resulting output, including the critique as privileged information, is scored by the teacher while the student uses the revision without the critique for training. On two Qwen3 students and six mathematical reasoning benchmarks, CriticOPD improves OPD, with the largest gains on competition problems.
items.title_ko: 비판 기반 온-정책 증류를 통한 신뢰할 수 있는 감독 회복
items.summary_ko: 온-정책 증류(OPD)는 학생 모델이 교사의 토큰 수준 감독을 받아 자체 롤아웃에서 훈련되지만, 학생의 잘못된 롤아웃에서 교사의 회복성(recoverability) 문제가 발생한다. CriticOPD는 오류 인식을 사용하여 회복성을 복원하는 방법을 제안한다.
items.why_ko: LLM의 온-정책 증류 학습 과정에서 발생하는 감독 신호의 신뢰성 문제를 해결하여, 모델 학습의 안정성과 효율성을 높이고 더욱 정확한 에이전트 개발을 가능하게 한다.

items.title: Manacá-1B-Instruct-2: Reproducible Safety Alignment for a Native Brazilian-Portuguese LLM. Negative DPO Results, a Controlled Composition Scan, and a Silent Failure Mode of the LLM Judge
items.body: Brazilian Portuguese remains underserved by open-source language models, and the few that are safety-aligned rarely document what did not work or validate comparisons with statistical significance. We present Manacá-1B-Instruct-2, the second-generation post-training alignment of Manacá-1B (1.72B parameters, trained from scratch for PT-BR), with an SFT corpus of 291,223 examples. We document three DPO attempts, all negative, including a case where the training reward margin reaches 1.0 while free generation does not change at all, and show that safety came from a dedicated safety-SFT (LLM-jp AnswerCarefully style), refined over three iterations until closing the safety-helpfulness frontier. A controlled scan of the fraction of general data in the safety-SFT mix (10% to 60%) reveals a non-monotonic over-refusal curve with a knee point at 40-50%. The final model is compared against four external PT-BR models on the same items, with Wilson confidence intervals and paired McNemar tests with Holm-Bonferroni correction: the lower bound of its safety interval (94.1%) lies above the upper bound of all four baselines. We also report a methodological finding for LLM-judge evaluation: on two of six safety items in MT-Bench-PT, the judge categorically refuses to assign a score regardless of the evaluated response, silently reducing the effective N of that category in every prior report of the project. We complement this with an n-gram decontamination check and a Chinchilla-anchored compute-budget table that attributes the gap in general capability to pre-training scale rather than alignment methodology. All code, raw data, logs, and scripts that produce every reported number are publicly released.
items.title_ko: Manacá-1B-Instruct-2: 브라질 포르투갈어 LLM의 재현 가능한 안전 정렬 및 DPO 실패 사례 보고
items.summary_ko: 이 연구는 브라질 포르투갈어 기반의 오픈소스 LLM인 Manacá-1B-Instruct-2의 후처리 정렬 결과를 제시한다. DPO 시도가 모두 실패했으며, LLM 심사관의 '침묵 실패 모드'를 포함하여 실패 사례를 상세히 문서화했다.
items.why_ko: 오픈소스 LLM의 안전 정렬 과정에서 발생할 수 있는 실제적인 어려움과 실패 사례를 투명하게 공개하여, 다른 개발자들이 비슷한 문제를 피하고 더 견고한 다국어 LLM을 구축하는 데 귀중한 실무 지식을 제공한다.

items.title: Scaling Discovery Requires Forgetting
items.body:
Automated research with LLM agents has shown promising results in various domains. Through iterative refinement and scored verifiers, LLM agents are capable of discovering new ideas. There are different ways to scale automated research: let one agent iterate for longer, run several agents in parallel, or further let the parallel agents communicate and build on one another's candidates. However, we find that all three strategies eventually plateau as the agents accumulate history. Each agent becomes anchored to its own past attempts, making fewer and smaller edits. Beyond this point, additional budget brings little further improvement. In this paper, we show that the key to scaling discovery further is to forget. Periodically discarding the search state, including every agent's session and the candidate history, and restarting from the best candidate found so far, unblocks the search and pushes the same budget further.
We implement forgetting in a team of agents with communication and evaluate it on four tasks spanning heuristic programming, kernel optimization and model training. The results show up to 15% improvement compared to parallel agents, and up to 39% compared to a single agent. Our results suggest that, for open-ended discovery, what an agent is allowed to remember matters as much as how much compute it is given.
items.title_ko: 규모 확장을 위한 발견에는 망각이 필요하다: LLM 에이전트의 히스토리 누적 문제 해결
items.summary_ko: LLM 에이전트를 활용한 자동화된 연구는 유망한 결과를 보이지만, 에이전트들이 히스토리를 축적하면서 결국 성능이 정체된다. 이 연구는 규모 확장을 위해 '망각'의 중요성을 강조한다.
items.why_ko: LLM 에이전트의 장기적인 자율 연구 및 문제 해결 능력 향상을 위한 근본적인 한계를 지적하고, 정보 관리 및 '망각' 메커니즘을 통해 확장성을 확보하는 중요한 통찰을 제공한다.

items.title: PhySGA: A Physics-Space Grounded Agentic Framework for Generalizable and Interactive 3D Composition
items.body: 3D object composition is pivotal to digital content creation and robot simulation, while also serving as a critical testbed for physical intelligence in foundation models. Previous methods either leverage large language models to directly predict object coordinates, or utilize generative diffusion priors to synthesize composite images for visual alignment, both of which rely on static priors in digital spaces. However, these methods consistently struggle with complex compositions such as precise hanging, gravity-driven settling and hidden containment, as these tasks require interactive construction processes involving global planning, fine-grained alignment, and physical simulation. To address these challenges, we propose PhySGA, a Physics-Space Grounded Agentic Framework for 3D composition via agent exploration and physical simulation, enabling the universal interactive assembly of rigid, articulated, and deformable objects. Directly applying vanilla LLMs or VLMs to this task proves insufficient, as current models inherently lack grounded physical understanding and interactive construction experience. To overcome this limitation, we design a collaborative feedforward-feedback architecture: an Assembly Agent focuses on geometric and kinematic reasoning for global step planning and coarse adjustment, while a Critic Agent reasons over contact dynamics for simulator state diagnosis and fine-grained closed-loop correction. Furthermore, Action Routers map semantic planning and analysis onto executable physical primitives within the simulator, while a task-specific Self-Evolving Skill Library distills historical trial-and-error feedback into reusable experiences, boosting success rates and minimizing exploration attempts. Extensive experiments within Isaac Sim demonstrate that PhySGA significantly surpasses existing methods in relation fidelity, physical plausibility, and visual quality.
items.title_ko: PhySGA: 물리 공간 기반 에이전트 프레임워크를 이용한 일반화 가능하고 상호작용적인 3D 구성
items.summary_ko: 3D 객체 구성은 디지털 콘텐츠 생성과 로봇 시뮬레이션에 중요하며, 파운데이션 모델의 물리적 지능 테스트베드 역할을 한다. 이 연구는 물리적 제약을 고려한 'PhySGA' 프레임워크를 통해 복잡한 3D 구성 문제를 해결한다.
items.why_ko: AI가 실제 물리 세계의 복잡성을 이해하고 상호작용하는 3D 환경을 구성하는 능력을 향상시켜, 로봇 공학, 시뮬레이션, 디지털 콘텐츠 제작 분야에 큰 발전을 가져올 수 있다.

items.title: PerSo: Investigating Facets of LLMs' Social Intelligence in Real-World Persuasion Scenarios
items.body: Understanding the social intelligence of large language models (LLMs) is increasingly important for applications involving human-AI interaction and multi-agent environments. Social intelligence comprises two aspects: cognitive intelligence, the ability to infer others' mental states, and behavioral intelligence, the ability to select appropriate social actions based on these inferences to achieve social goals. Persuasion provides a natural testbed in which both aspects are simultaneously at play, yet prior benchmarks typically evaluate them in isolation using synthetic scenarios. We introduce PerSo, a benchmark that evaluates both aspects on real-world persuasion dialogues from Reddit's ChangeMyView community, using an LLM-in-the-loop pipeline to construct the evaluation tasks, validated through human annotation. Our evaluation of diverse LLMs shows that performance generally scales with model size but varies across dimensions. The strongest LLM slightly surpasses the best observed human performance on the behavioral task, while the best human participant remains ahead on the cognitive task.
items.title_ko: PerSo: 실제 설득 시나리오에서 LLM의 사회 지능 연구
items.summary_ko: LLM의 사회 지능 이해는 인간-AI 상호작용 및 다중 에이전트 환경에서 중요하며, 이 연구는 실제 설득 시나리오를 통해 LLM의 인지 및 행동 지능 측면을 탐구한다.
items.why_ko: LLM이 단순히 정보를 처리하는 것을 넘어 인간과 유사한 사회적 상호작용 능력을 갖추도록 발전시키는 데 중요한 통찰을 제공하며, 이는 대화형 AI 및 에이전트 시스템의 실용성을 높일 것이다.

items.title: Detection of Potato Plant Leaf Diseases using Convolutional Neural Networks
items.body: Potato is an important food-security crop in Ethiopia, but its production is affected by foliar diseases, particularly early blight and late blight. This study develops a lightweight convolutional neural network (CNN) to classify potato leaves into three categories: healthy, early blight, and late blight. The proposed model was trained using 2,215 images from the PlantVillage dataset and evaluated on an independent field dataset containing 247 images collected from potato farms in Banja, Awi Zone, Ethiopia. On PlantVillage, the model achieved 99.04% training accuracy, 98.21% validation accuracy, and 98.66% test accuracy. On the field dataset, it achieved 90.28% accuracy. The study also compares the proposed CNN with VGG16 and MobileNetV2 in terms of classification performance and computational efficiency. The proposed model contains 446,787 trainable parameters, occupies approximately 1.70 MB, and requires an average of 5.58 seconds per training epoch in the reported experimental setup, compared with 9.96 seconds for VGG16 and 7.68 seconds for MobileNetV2. The results demonstrate the potential of a compact CNN for potato leaf disease classification and highlight the importance of independent field evaluation, where image conditions are more variable than in controlled benchmark datasets. The proposed approach may support preliminary disease identification for smallholder farmers in Ethiopia and similar agricultural settings.
items.title_ko: CNN을 이용한 감자 잎 질병 탐지 연구
items.summary_ko: 이 연구는 경량 Convolutional Neural Network(CNN) 모델을 개발하여 감자 잎을 건강한 잎, 초기 역병, 늦은 역병 세 가지 카테고리로 분류한다. PlantVillage 데이터셋으로 훈련하고 현장 데이터셋으로 평가했다.
items.why_ko: AI가 농업 분야에서 작물 질병을 조기에 효과적으로 진단하는 데 활용될 수 있음을 보여주며, 이는 식량 안보와 농업 생산성 향상에 기여할 수 있다.

items.title: PrismaCoder: Pushing the Boundaries of Open Multimodal Code Intelligence through Decomposed Rubric Synthesis
items.body: Multimodal code intelligence connects the symbolic world of programs with the visual world their execution creates. Interest in this capability is burgeoning, as models are increasingly asked to produce charts, webpages, animations, and semi-structured documents. Recently, proprietary models have pushed far ahead, producing interactive artifacts even from a text description or a screenshot alone. Yet their data and training remain closed, and open progress is held back by the quantity and quality of available data and by the pipelines and methods for producing it. Quality is the harder of the two, since a sample must be correct as a program, well built, and above all visually right once rendered. No existing signal covers all three. Execution often returns just a pass or fail, code similarity does not map to the visual output, and task-specific verifiers do not generalize. To push open progress further, we start from the data side with PrismaForge, a hierarchical data pipeline centered on a synthesized rubric that decomposes these factors into checkable criteria. The same rubric serves as both filter and reward: it curates the supervised corpus, then drives reinforcement learning on visual-coding tasks. Leveraging PrismaForge for data synthesis and filtering, we build PrismaCoder-2M, the most diverse open dataset for multimodal code intelligence and the largest to date. On the model side, we train PrismaCoder-9B and PrismaCoder-35B on this data and release both. They lead the open state of the art by a wide margin and rival leading proprietary systems. Our analyses further show that the proposed rubric-based pipeline improves multimodal coding performance across model backbones. We release our code and data at https://qiushisun.github.io/PrismaCoder-Home/.
items.title_ko: PrismaCoder: 분해된 루브릭 합성을 통한 오픈 멀티모달 코드 인텔리전스 강화
items.summary_ko: 멀티모달 코드 인텔리전스는 프로그램의 상징적 세계와 실행 결과의 시각적 세계를 연결한다. PrismaCoder는 분해된 루브릭 합성을 통해 개방형 멀티모달 코드 인텔리전스의 한계를 확장한다.
items.why_ko: 시각적 요소를 포함한 코드 이해 및 생성 능력을 향상시켜, 개발자가 더 복잡한 시각적 출력(예: 차트, 웹페이지)을 요구하는 코드를 효율적으로 다룰 수 있도록 돕는다.

items.title: Revisiting Simple Baselines for Relational Deep Learning
items.body: Relational deep learning has emerged as a powerful paradigm for learning end-to-end predictive models over relational databases by representing them as temporal heterogeneous graphs. Recent advances based on graph neural networks and Transformers have achieved strong performance across diverse domains. However, the effectiveness of simpler relational baselines remains underexplored, making it difficult to assess how much architectural complexity is needed to achieve strong predictive performance. Motivated by the observation that predictive signals arise from target attributes, relational attributes, and historical labels, we revisit how effectively these signals can be exploited using simple propagation methods. We adapt fixed low-pass feature propagation to relational entity graphs and train an MLP for prediction. The resulting predictions are further refined using Correct-and-Smooth, a graph-based label propagation algorithm that incorporates historical labels over task-specific meta-graphs connecting target entities. Across classification and regression tasks on RelBench, an MLP trained on neighborhood-filtered features outperforms one using only target-entity features on most tasks and recovers a substantial portion of the performance of heterogeneous GNNs. Correct-and-Smooth provides further gains from historical labels, although applying it requires a separately constructed meta-graph because connections among target entities are not directly specified by the relational entity graph. Together, our studies revisit the effectiveness of established propagation methods as simple RDL baselines while identifying canonical meta-graph construction as a key challenge for effective label propagation.
items.title_ko: 관계형 딥러닝을 위한 간단한 베이스라인 재검토
items.summary_ko: 관계형 딥러닝은 관계형 데이터베이스에서 종단 간 예측 모델을 학습하는 강력한 패러다임이지만, 더 간단한 베이스라인의 효과는 덜 탐구되었다. 이 연구는 모델의 복잡성이 강한 예측 성능에 얼마나 필요한지 평가하기 위해 간단한 관계형 베이스라인을 재검토한다.
items.why_ko: 복잡한 모델에 앞서 간단한 베이스라인의 성능을 이해하는 것은 연구 및 실무에서 모델 선택과 효율성 개선에 중요한 기준을 제공한다.

items.title: Generative Representation Learning for Scalable Latent Tokenization
items.body: We introduce an approach for self-supervised representation learning designed to be used as a tokenizer for generative modeling. Our objective supervises a representation loss by factorizing the pointwise mutual information of the data, which we estimate by taking information differences between conditional predictions from a learned generative model. We justify our algorithm theoretically and empirically, demonstrating that our generative approach to representation learning avoids dimensional collapse and feature suppression in cases where commonly used methods like DINO and LeJEPA fail. Moreover, we show our representation learning technique is scalable; expending more compute leads to predictably better latent tokenization. For the first time, we perform a careful analysis of the combined flop efficiency of tokenizer and generative model and demonstrate that our approach is a compute-optimal improvement over direct diffusion for pixel-space generation, obtaining an FID-50K of 2.18 with JiT-L. Applied to ImageNet and the text-to-image dataset GPIC, we show tokenizer encoder scaling laws for diffusability, where extrapolating our approach achieves representations in 7x fewer FLOPs than DINOv2 on ImageNet and 8x fewer FLOPs than WebSSL on GPIC.
items.title_ko: 생성형 표현 학습을 통한 확장 가능한 잠재 토큰화
items.summary_ko: 이 연구는 생성형 모델링을 위한 토크나이저로 사용될 수 있도록 설계된 자기 지도 표현 학습 접근 방식을 소개한다. 데이터의 점별 상호 정보량을 인수분해하여 표현 손실을 감독한다.
items.why_ko: 생성형 모델의 핵심 구성 요소인 토큰화 과정을 효율적으로 개선하여, 모델의 확장성과 성능을 높일 수 있는 새로운 방법을 제시한다.

items.title: ActiveEvidence: Decision-Focused Evidence Graphs with Verifiable Acquisition Gaps
items.body: A multimodal agent must decide whether visual evidence is worth acquiring, which candidate or resolution to query, and when further interaction can no longer change its decision. We study this problem under a strict free-metadata/paid-observation boundary, stochastic vector costs, and a frozen execution trace, and treat it as decision-certifiable active evidence acquisition. A Counterfactual Evidence Interaction Graph (CEIG) represents unary evidence value, signed second-order interaction, and directed conditional harm while maintaining explicit score enclosures for unresolved interactions; a decision-weighted enclosure objective tightens the bounds that can change action identity. Gap-directed refinement evaluates only interactions that can displace the incumbent acquisition and stops once an $ε$-decision certificate shows that unresolved terms cannot change the selected action beyond a declared tolerance. The certificate is model-relative: it verifies policy-consistent optimality under the pinned learned score, and semantic quality is measured separately through post-freeze labels. Paired continuation rollouts learn the downstream value of paid previews, an online operational cost filter is separated from independent finite-policy-family trajectory certification, and an acquisition monitor with an independently implemented verifier binds every certificate to the frozen trace. On 640 cases split into 384/128/128 training, validation, and test cases, the controller reaches task score 0.842, grounding F1 0.816, evidence recall 0.873, 1.74 accepted calls, 286.5K visual tokens, and 742ms p95 latency. Dense replay of issued certificates shows 0.992 action agreement and a 0.988 certificate rate while evaluating 19.6 instead of 191.4 expensive interaction terms per decision.
items.title_ko: ActiveEvidence: 검증 가능한 획득 격차를 가진 의사결정 중심 증거 그래프
items.summary_ko: 멀티모달 에이전트는 시각적 증거를 획득할 가치가 있는지, 어떤 후보나 해상도를 쿼리할지, 그리고 언제 추가 상호작용이 더 이상 결정을 바꿀 수 없는지 결정해야 한다. 이 연구는 이를 '의사결정 인증 가능한 능동적 증거 획득' 문제로 다룬다.
items.why_ko: 멀티모달 에이전트가 제한된 자원 내에서 가장 효율적이고 신뢰할 수 있는 정보를 획득하고 의사결정을 내리는 방법을 개선하여, 복잡한 현실 세계 문제 해결 능력을 향상시킨다.

items.title: The Physics Is the Network: Fast, Training-Free Neural Emulation
items.body: Neural emulation need not require learning a substitute for known physics. We investigate PolyNets that couple a continuous-time neural representation of polynomial dynamics with a simple recurrent network for discrete-time integration. When the governing coefficients are known, the resulting tensor graph requires no training and preserves the prescribed numerical scheme while enabling efficient hardware execution and parallel simulation. Using the one-dimensional Korteweg-de Vries equation, we compare PolyNet with CPU and GPU finite-difference Runge-Kutta solvers and three trained neural models: a state-map emulator, a physics-informed predictor, and a learned-tendency integrator. Analytical soliton solutions provide a reference for amplitude and phase errors across grid resolutions, 10^6 dispersively scaled time steps, ensembles of up to 10^4 trajectories, and varying initial amplitudes. PolyNet achieves accuracy comparable to the numerical solvers, including at amplitudes outside the learned models' training conditions. It combines this fidelity with high GPU throughput, approximately constant over the tested resolution range, and favorable ensemble scaling.
items.title_ko: 물리는 곧 네트워크: 훈련 없는 빠른 신경 에뮬레이션
items.summary_ko: 신경 에뮬레이션이 알려진 물리 현상에 대한 대체 학습을 반드시 필요로 하지 않는다는 점을 밝힌다. 이 연구는 연속 시간 다항 역학의 신경 표현과 이산 시간 통합을 위한 간단한 순환 네트워크를 결합한 PolyNets를 제안한다.
items.why_ko: 물리 기반 시스템 시뮬레이션에 AI를 적용할 때, 훈련 없이도 효율적인 하드웨어 실행과 병렬 시뮬레이션을 가능하게 하여, 과학 컴퓨팅 및 공학 설계 분야에 새로운 가능성을 제시한다.

items.title: The Wealth of Agents: Scaling Agentic AI Across Developers
items.body: Today's agentic systems are typically designed, built, and deployed by single developers with full control over all participating agents. While this simplifies development, it limits the potential scale of agentic systems. We study multi-developer agentic systems (MDAs) which enable developers to collaboratively build agentic systems to push frontier capability beyond what any individual developer could achieve alone. We construct empirical and theoretical models of developers to compare MDAs with single-developer agentic systems (SDAs). On GAIA, a general assistant benchmark, a population of specialized developers whose individual agents do not exceed 35% accuracy reaches 70% when their agents are combined in an MDA. This MDA performs 12 percentage points above the median general-purpose SDA built with several times each specialist's development budget. Our theoretical models show how MDAs can incentivize specialization and encourage more efficient use of aggregated developer resources. Put together, our results make a preliminary case for MDAs as a new scaling axis by enabling developers with diverse capabilities and resources to advance agentic AI collaboratively.
items.title_ko: 에이전트의 부: 개발자 간 에이전트 AI 확장의 연구
items.summary_ko: 현재 에이전트 시스템은 보통 단일 개발자에 의해 설계 및 배포되지만, 이는 잠재적 확장성을 제한한다. 이 연구는 여러 개발자가 협력하여 에이전트 시스템을 구축하는 다중 개발자 에이전트 시스템(MDA)을 분석한다.
items.why_ko: AI 에이전트 시스템 개발의 병목 현상을 해결하고, 여러 개발자가 협력하여 대규모 에이전트 시스템을 구축할 수 있는 모델을 제시하여, AI 개발의 확장성과 생산성을 높이는 데 기여한다.

items.title: VASPO: Self-Distillation with Privileged Value Estimation
items.body: On-policy self-distillation provides dense supervision for reasoning models via a privileged self-teacher. However, this supervision reflects local token preferences rather than the expected return of an unguided student continuation. Recent methods combine this signal with GRPO. They use GRPO for update directions and the teacher for signal scaling. However, we demonstrate a more effective integration within PPO. Specifically, we identify complementary positional dynamics: privileged information enhances a critic's value-prediction accuracy toward the response's end, whereas self-teacher guidance is strong initially, drops mid-generation, and rebounds finally. These insights motivate Value-Augmented Self-Distillation Policy Optimization (VASPO), wherein a self-teacher and critic evaluate identical privileged information at student-generated prefixes. The critic computes token-level PPO advantages from predicted continuation returns, while the self-teacher modulates selected positive advantages via bounded probability ratios. Across six mathematical reasoning benchmarks, VASPO improves mean accuracy over PPO by 2.59 and 1.81 percentage points on Qwen3-4B and OLMo3-7B variants, respectively, and achieves the highest mean accuracy among evaluated methods on Knights and Knaves. Our code is available at https://github.com/cii030/VASPO.
items.title_ko: VASPO: 특권 가치 추정치를 사용한 자기 증류(Self-Distillation) 강화 학습
items.summary_ko: 온-정책 자기 증류는 특권적인 자기 교사를 통해 추론 모델에 풍부한 감독을 제공한다. 이 연구는 PPO 내에서 더 효과적인 통합을 위해 특권 가치 추정치를 사용한 VASPO를 제안한다.
items.why_ko: 강화 학습에서 자기 증류의 효율성을 높여 모델이 더 안정적이고 빠르게 학습하도록 돕는다. 특히 토큰 수준의 보상 할당 문제를 개선하여 LLM 기반 에이전트의 성능 향상에 기여할 수 있다.

items.title: Bayesian Learning to Select Fair Classifiers
items.body: Evaluations of classifiers (AI or human or agents) often assume a batch setting in which every agent produces labels on every example in a test set, which can be expensive or impractical in many contexts. This motivates online policies that adaptively select agents to query as examples arrive and update policies as outcomes are observed. We study the problem of selecting, in an online stream, the agent that best balances (i) predictive performance and (ii) subgroup fairness of a sensitive attribute, and that allows for delayed observations of true class labels. We formulate this as a Bayesian multi-armed bandit problem using Thompson Sampling, explicitly balancing accuracy and fairness. We conduct empirical evaluations on real-world datasets spanning problems involving tabular classifiers, large language models, and human labelers, demonstrating substantial reductions in regret relative to baselines. Our theoretical contributions include guarantees on the performance of the selected agent that incorporate both the accuracy and fairness aspects of the problem.
items.title_ko: 베이지안 학습을 통한 공정한 분류기 선택
items.summary_ko: 분류기 평가는 일반적으로 모든 에이전트가 테스트 세트의 모든 예제에 레이블을 생성하는 배치 설정을 가정하지만, 이는 비현실적이다. 이 연구는 온라인 스트림에서 예측 성능과 하위 그룹 공정성을 모두 고려하여 에이전트를 적응적으로 선택하는 베이지안 학습 정책을 제안한다.
items.why_ko: 동적으로 데이터가 유입되는 환경에서 AI 모델의 공정성과 성능을 동시에 고려하여 최적의 분류기를 선택하는 방법을 제시하며, 이는 책임감 있는 AI 시스템 구축에 중요하다.

items.title: A Two-Level Clinical Novelty Prioritization Framework for Disease Trajectories Discovered from Longitudinal Electronic Health Records
items.body: Graph-based analysis of electronic health records (EHRs) yields disease-trajectory catalogs, but structural support does not establish semantic novelty. We present a two-level framework to prioritize 99,527 branching motifs previously discovered by an upstream patient-disjoint, train-only MIMIC-IV v3.1 pipeline and frozen after validation-based catalog selection. The framework separates path-level and node-to-endpoint semantic sparsity from reliability-adjusted clinical priority. Three deterministic textualizations per motif or node-target pair were embedded with BAAI/bge-small-en-v1.5 and calibrated against 166,972 pre-2023 PubMed references using mean top-20 cosine distance. Positive recombination occurred in 8.63% of motifs and had negligible effect on global ranking, whereas specificity and support/GNN reliability terms changed clinical-priority ordering. Robustness analyses across neighbor counts, templates, encoders, generic-label taxonomies, score settings, PrimeKG, and corrected density-based RND showed that broad ordering was more stable than hard top-k membership. A semantic-dose analysis did not support a monotonic relation between score and forecasting benefit after endpoint and token-count adjustment (1.96 days per SD; 95% CI, -0.75 to 4.68). In the frozen catalog-q90 high-semantic subgroup, branch-enhanced forecasting reduced conditional event-time MAE by 20.1 days (95% CI, 13.3-27.0) and sMAPE by 2.37 percentage points (95% CI, 1.81-2.93), while discrimination and endpoint-ranking differences were inconclusive. Corrected RND showed low tail agreement with the primary score (Spearman rho = 0.430; q90 Jaccard = 0.125) despite a similar aggregate timing association. These findings support representation-aware, uncertainty-aware literature-relative prioritization of discovered trajectories rather than causal discovery or clinician-adjudicated novelty.
items.title_ko: 장기 전자의무기록에서 발견된 질병 궤적을 위한 2단계 임상적 참신성 우선순위 프레임워크
items.summary_ko: 전자의무기록(EHR)의 그래프 기반 분석은 질병 궤적 카탈로그를 생성하지만, 구조적 지원만으로는 의미론적 참신성을 확립하기 어렵다. 이 연구는 99,527개의 분기 모티프를 우선순위화하기 위한 2단계 프레임워크를 제시한다.
items.why_ko: 방대한 의료 데이터를 분석하여 질병 진행 경로의 새로운 패턴을 효과적으로 발견하고 우선순위를 지정하는 방법을 제시하며, 이는 개인 맞춤형 의료 및 질병 예측에 기여할 수 있다.

items.title: VascuSR: Iterative Anatomy-Aware Diffusion for CT Super-Resolution
items.body: Generative super-resolution (SR) can recover sharp detail in computed tomography (CT) images from severely downsampled observations, but the missing high-frequency content is not uniquely determined by the low-resolution input. Consequently, visually plausible reconstructions may contain anatomically unsupported vascular detail, such as missing, spurious, or incorrectly connected vessels. To overcome this challenge, we introduce VascuSR, an iterative anatomy-aware diffusion framework that combines image reconstruction with explicit 3D vascular guidance. First, to provide richer anatomical guidance, we use an explicit 3D vascular representation that captures structural information beyond individual slices. This representation also simplifies vascular refinement by allowing a lightweight 3D generative refiner to focus on vascular structure rather than complex CT appearance. Second, to guide slice-wise SR, a lightweight anatomy controller injects the refined structure into the diffusion decoder, while iterative feedback updates this guidance from each new SR volume. On re-annotated MSD Task08 and HVM datasets, VascuSR outperforms interpolation and learning-based SR baselines in segmentation accuracy (Dice and clDice) and 3D vascular structure (connectivity and mean centerline distance), while maintaining image quality comparable to its SR backbone. Compared with learning-based baselines, VascuSR reduces class-averaged connected-component counts by over 20% on both datasets and mean centerline distance by over 10% on MSD.
items.title_ko: VascuSR: 반복적 해부학 인식 확산 모델을 이용한 CT 초해상도
items.summary_ko: 생성형 초해상도(SR)는 심하게 다운샘플링된 CT 이미지에서 선명한 디테일을 복원할 수 있지만, 해부학적으로 부적절한 혈관 디테일을 생성할 수 있다. VascuSR은 이러한 문제를 해결하기 위해 반복적인 해부학 인식 확산 프레임워크를 제안한다.
items.why_ko: 의료 영상 분야에서 AI 기반 초해상도 기술의 정확성과 신뢰성을 높여, 의료 진단 및 치료 계획 수립에 더 유용한 정보를 제공할 수 있다.

items.title: ReaDy: Recurrent States as Dynamic Context for Speculative Drafting in Hybrid Linear Attention Large Language Models
items.body: Speculative decoding accelerates autoregressive generation by drafting multiple tokens per step, yet feature-based drafters rely on target hidden features whose contextual emphasis may not align with the needs of subsequent draft positions. Hybrid linear attention (HLA) models maintain compact recurrent states that accumulate historical associations, offering an efficient source of complementary context for speculative drafting. We introduce ReaDy, the first speculative decoding method, to the best of our knowledge, to leverage HLA recurrent states for position-specific context retrieval during drafting. ReaDy equips each draft position with a learned query to retrieve supplementary context directly from the target's committed recurrent states. A lightweight state reader integrates this context into draft representations through residual updates, while low-rank state reads and fused operators keep additional computation and I/O overhead low. Building on DSpark's parallel backbone and sequential prediction head, ReaDy employs a lightweight two-stage adaptation strategy, with reader capacity, state sources, and residual placement examined through ablation studies. Across seven benchmarks spanning mathematics, code generation, and dialogue, ReaDy achieves an average $3.16\times$ decoding speedup over autoregressive decoding with Qwen3.8-27B on a single NVIDIA B200 GPU. It outperforms DSpark on every benchmark, improving throughput by 7.97% and acceptance length by 8.50% on average. Our code is available at https://github.com/StartLuxLabs/ReaDy.
items.title_ko: ReaDy: 하이브리드 선형 어텐션 LLM에서 재귀 상태를 동적 컨텍스트로 활용한 추측 초안 작성
items.summary_ko: 추측 디코딩(speculative decoding)은 단계당 여러 토큰을 초안 작성하여 자동 회귀 생성을 가속화한다. 이 연구는 하이브리드 선형 어텐션(HLA) 모델의 컴팩트한 재귀 상태를 동적 컨텍스트로 활용하는 첫 번째 추측 디코딩 방법인 ReaDy를 소개한다.
items.why_ko: LLM의 텍스트 생성 속도를 획기적으로 향상시킬 수 있는 새로운 추측 디코딩 기법을 제시하여, 실시간 대화형 AI 시스템의 사용자 경험을 개선하는 데 기여할 수 있다.

items.title: Graph-Enhanced Disease Trajectory Discovery and Temporal Endpoint Forecasting from Longitudinal Electronic Health Records
items.body: Longitudinal electronic health records (EHRs) can reveal disease-progression structure, while useful forecasting requires leakage-controlled discovery, censor-aware outcomes, and inspectable trajectory evidence. We developed a graph-enhanced framework in MIMIC-IV v3.1 that splits patients before graph construction, learns train-only consecutive-admission transitions, and freezes endpoint-specific branching-motif policies selected on validation data. The final catalog contained 99,527 motifs, and a time-aware Transformer retrieved at most 24 patient-compatible motifs per endpoint through endpoint-specific cross-attention. Across five training seeds, micro-AUPRC increased from 0.9330 to 0.9357, while event-time MAE decreased from 676.9 to 657.7 days (reduction 19.2 days; 95% paired patient-cluster bootstrap CI, 13.8-24.8). Timing effects were heterogeneous: MAE worsened for events within 730 days but improved by 58.9 days for events occurring after 730 days. In an exploratory internal temporal split, branch conditioning reduced conditional event-time MAE by 26.9 days (95% CI, 23.0-30.8) without evidence of better micro-AUPRC. Corrected survival evaluation over the supported 0-2,555-day interval did not establish macro C-index or integrated Brier score superiority over a matched history-only discrete-hazard model. A directed, degree-matched GNN repair substantially improved unseen-edge discovery, yet replacing GNN-derived scores within fixed motif identities did not improve downstream forecasting. These results position branching motifs as structured trajectory context whose main value is long-range timing support rather than uniformly stronger endpoint discrimination, survival prediction, or causal explanation.
items.title_ko: 그래프 강화 질병 궤적 발견 및 장기 전자의무기록 기반 시간적 결과 예측
items.summary_ko: 장기 전자의무기록(EHR)은 질병 진행 구조를 밝혀낼 수 있지만, 유용한 예측을 위해서는 누출 제어된 발견, 검열 인식 결과, 검사 가능한 궤적 증거가 필요하다. 이 연구는 MIMIC-IV v3.1에서 그래프 강화 프레임워크를 개발했다.
items.why_ko: 의료 데이터에서 질병 진행 패턴을 더 정확하게 식별하고 미래 결과를 예측하는 프레임워크를 제시하여, 개인 맞춤형 예방 및 치료 전략 수립에 기여할 수 있다.

items.title: Hindsight-Privileged RLVR: Single-Rollout Token Credit Without Group Sampling
items.body: Reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR) trains language models from checked task outcomes, but assigning a terminal reward to individual reasoning tokens or actions remains difficult. Group-relative methods such as Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) sample several attempts per prompt, but lose their reward-based learning signal when all attempts receive the same outcome. We propose Hindsight-Privileged RLVR (HP-RLVR), a single-rollout method that turns a completed trajectory's own future into token-level update weights. The generating policy snapshot scores each eligible token under its causal history and under a hindsight context containing the realized future and verifier feedback. A normalized Jensen--Shannon divergence between the two views weights the reward relative to a historical baseline, yielding bounded token credit for both successful and failed attempts, with no reference solution or learned critic. In paired Qwen3-8B runs over a shared $100$-step schedule, HP-RLVR trains $1.21\times$, $1.46\times$, and $2.30\times$ faster than GRPO on mathematics, code generation, and ALFWorld, using one eighth the rollouts per prompt. Accuracy is comparable overall, with HP-RLVR ahead on mathematics at all three sizes and GRPO ahead on code and ALFWorld. In ALFWorld, $43.2\%$ (4B) and $49.0\%$ (8B) of GRPO's gradient-norm records are zero, versus none for HP-RLVR.
items.title_ko: Hindsight-Privileged RLVR: 그룹 샘플링 없는 단일 롤아웃 토큰 크레딧 할당
items.summary_ko: 검증 가능한 보상 기반 강화 학습(RLVR)은 검증된 작업 결과로부터 언어 모델을 훈련하지만, 개별 추론 토큰에 보상을 할당하는 것은 어렵다. Hindsight-Privileged RLVR(HP-RLVR)은 단일 롤아웃으로 완료된 궤적을 활용하는 방법을 제안한다.
items.why_ko: LLM 강화 학습에서 토큰 수준의 보상 할당 문제를 효율적으로 해결하여, 모델의 추론 과정을 더 정교하게 지도하고 학습 효율성을 높일 수 있는 실용적인 방법론을 제시한다.

items.title: Quantifying privacy risks in foundation model representations of brain MRI
items.body: Pretrained representations are increasingly used to share and reuse information from medical images without exposing the original scans, but it is unclear how much patient-specific information these representations retain. We investigate this question for brain magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) by evaluating five frozen pretrained encoders spanning different architectures, pretraining objectives, and training domains on two longitudinal T1-weighted datasets, OASIS-2 and MIRIAD. Under an attacker model with access to released embeddings, the corresponding public encoder, and auxiliary MRI scans, we evaluate patient linkage and sensitive-attribute inference. Across the evaluated representations, we observe substantial subject-specific information: rank-1 patient linkage reaches up to 99\% on MIRIAD and exceeds 90\% on OASIS-2 for the highest-risk representation, despite the absence of an identification objective during encoder training. We further show that the released embeddings retain information about a demographic attribute, with recorded-sex prediction reaching balanced accuracy of 90.9\% on OASIS-2 and 95.5\% on MIRIAD. Overall, our results demonstrate that replacing raw brain MRI with learned embeddings does not, by itself, eliminate patient-linkage or attribute-inference risk, and is therefore insufficient on its own to establish anonymity.
items.title_ko: 뇌 MRI 파운데이션 모델 표현의 개인정보 침해 위험 정량화
items.summary_ko: 사전 훈련된 표현은 의료 영상 정보를 공유하고 재사용하는 데 점점 더 많이 사용되지만, 이러한 표현이 환자별 정보를 얼마나 유지하는지는 불분명하다. 이 연구는 뇌 MRI에 대해 이러한 질문을 조사하여 개인정보 침해 위험을 정량화한다.
items.why_ko: 의료 AI 분야에서 파운데이션 모델 활용 시 민감한 환자 정보의 프라이버시 위험을 객관적으로 평가하는 방법을 제시하며, 이는 의료 AI의 안전하고 윤리적인 개발 및 배포에 필수적이다.

items.title: Average-Reward Policy Identification from a Single Continuing Trajectory
items.body: In reinforcement learning, an agent must explore an unknown environment to learn how to make good decisions. Unlike methods that can freely sample any state--action pair, an agent learning from a single trajectory must spend additional time navigating between states. It is therefore natural to expect that learning from a single trajectory requires more experience. In this paper, we show that this additional cost is not always necessary. For average-reward reinforcement learning, we develop an algorithm that learns where to collect information while ensuring that the required samples can be obtained efficiently. We establish an upper bound on the number of interactions needed to identify a near-optimal policy. Furthermore, we prove a matching information theoretic lower bound, showing that, for a broad class of environments and at sufficiently high accuracy, learning from a single trajectory is no harder in the worst case than learning with unrestricted access to state action samples. Our results reveal that the additional complexity cost of navigation can be avoided by adapting information gathering requirements to how the environment provides information.
items.title_ko: 단일 연속 궤적에서 평균 보상 정책 식별의 비점근적 수렴
items.summary_ko: 강화 학습에서 단일 궤적으로부터 학습하는 에이전트는 상태 간 이동에 추가 시간을 소요해야 한다. 이 연구는 평균 보상 강화 학습에서 이러한 추가 비용이 항상 필요한 것은 아님을 보여주고, 단일 궤적에서 평균 보상 정책 식별을 위한 알고리즘을 개발한다.
items.why_ko: 단일 궤적 환경에서 강화 학습의 효율성을 높이는 이론적 기반을 제공하며, 이는 실제 환경에서 데이터 수집이 어렵거나 비용이 많이 드는 로봇 학습과 같은 분야에 중요한 의미를 가진다.

items.title: Decoupled Marginal Sharpening for Training-Free Inference-Time Scaling
items.body: We study how to improve LLM reasoning at inference time without updating model weights or using external reward models. Recent reward-free power-sampling methods define the sequence-level power target $π_α(y\mid x)\propto p_0(y\mid x)^α$, where $α>1$, which increases the relative probability of completions that are already likely under the base model. Existing methods use Metropolis--Hastings or Sequential Monte Carlo (SMC) to approximately sample from this target. However, two challenges arise at different levels. At the target level, full-sequence sharpening can concentrate probability on a few exact reasoning--answer trajectories, suppressing alternative paths that support the same answer. At the sampler level, finite-particle SMC can suffer from path collapse when resampling repeatedly duplicates a few high-weight prefixes. To address these challenges, we propose Decoupled Marginal Sharpening (DMS), which separately controls how strongly the model favors particular reasoning paths and how strongly it favors final answers after aggregating support across those paths. At the target level, DMS first samples from a sharpened reasoning distribution, then marginalizes the model's answer probabilities over the resulting weighted reasoning population and sharpens the induced answer marginal. Separate exponents allow mild reasoning sharpening to encourage exploration of diverse paths, followed by stronger answer-marginal sharpening to concentrate probability on answers with greater aggregate support across those paths. At the sampler level, we develop Fully Adapted Annealed SMC, which combines an annealed sequence of power targets with locally fully adapted proposals and predictive ancestor resampling. Experiments on MATH500, GPQA-Diamond, HumanEval, and AIME24/25 across three base models show that DMS achieves the highest mean pass@1 among the compared methods in all tasks.
items.title_ko: 훈련 없이 추론 시간에 스케일링을 위한 분리된 마진 샤프닝
items.summary_ko: 이 연구는 모델 가중치를 업데이트하거나 외부 보상 모델을 사용하지 않고 추론 시간에 LLM 추론을 개선하는 방법을 다룬다. 특히 $α>1$일 때 시퀀스 수준 파워 타겟 $π_α(y\mid x)\propto p_0(y\mid x)^α$를 정의하는 reward-free power-sampling 방법을 개선한다.
items.why_ko: 추론 시간에 LLM의 성능을 향상시키는 효율적인 훈련 없는 방법을 제시하여, 모델 재훈련 비용 없이 다양한 애플리케이션에서 LLM의 유용성을 높일 수 있다.

items.title: Lost in Translation: Why Lower Bias Scores Don't Mean Fairer Models
items.body: Bias audits of multilingual language models usually compare a model's average stereotype score in English with its average in another language and read the difference as a difference in fairness. We ask how much of that difference is noise. Auditing ten open models in eight languages, we measure how far scores move when English test items are merely reworded, test every language shift item by item, and check that the test catches shifts we inject on purpose. In all 70 model-language pairs the stereotype score falls below its English level, and for Hindi, Korean and Swahili the drop clearly exceeds what rewording English produces; most of it comes from StereoSet items. Judging every translation, we find that imperfect ones drop more, but faithful translations alone drop nearly as much. Still, a lower average does not show that a model is fairer. An item's English score predicts its translated score far less well than its reworded score (correlation 0.23, 0.27 on faithful translations, vs. 0.48), while scores stay as far from neutral, models agree on translated items, and within Hindi or Spanish a translated item's score correlates with its own rewording at 0.84 and 0.82.
