The average cannot distinguish lower bias from a different pattern of item-level scores. We also document three common pipeline errors that silently erase bias signal, and release our code.
items.title_ko: 번역의 오류: 낮은 편향 점수가 공정한 모델을 의미하지 않는 이유
items.summary_ko: 다국어 언어 모델의 편향 감사(bias audit)는 영어와 다른 언어 간의 평균 고정관념 점수를 비교하여 공정성 차이로 해석한다. 이 연구는 이러한 차이 중 얼마나 많은 부분이 노이즈인지 질문하고 8개 언어로 된 10개 오픈 모델을 감사한다.
items.why_ko: 다국어 LLM의 편향성 평가에서 측정 방법의 한계와 노이즈의 중요성을 지적하며, 이는 더 정확하고 신뢰할 수 있는 다국어 AI 모델의 윤리적 평가 및 개발에 중요한 시사점을 제공한다.

items.title: AdaRSI: On-Demand Recursive Self-Improvement for Embodied Agents
items.body: Pretrained vision-language-action models (VLAs) often fail midway through unseen long-horizon tasks. Recursive self-improvement (RSI) offers a remedy, but embodied RSI methods either refine the harness around a frozen executor and so cannot add a missing motion, or train the executor on persistent failures without asking whether a failure lies in how the executor is called or in what it can do. We ask when a self-improving embodied system should change the weights of its executor, and propose AdaRSI, an on-demand RSI framework for embodied agents. A coding agent first improves its skills and harness, then attributes persistent failures by retrying failing sub-steps from saved states, and fine-tunes only the sub-steps that remain unreliable, with demonstrations it collects itself and experience carried over from earlier tasks. On all 50 target tasks of RoboCasa365, with GR00T N1.5 as the executor and no human demonstrations, AdaRSI improves the VLA on all three suites and raises its success on unseen composite tasks from 4.6% to 13.8%. Compared with fine-tuning every sub-step, it reaches slightly higher success while using only 28% of the GPU time and 22% of the self-collected demonstrations, and fine-tuning without a harness trains more yet gains far less.
items.title_ko: AdaRSI: 구현 에이전트를 위한 온디맨드 재귀적 자기 개선
items.summary_ko: 사전 훈련된 비전-언어-액션(VLA) 모델은 보이지 않는 장기 작업을 수행하는 도중에 실패하는 경우가 많다. 이 연구는 실행자의 가중치를 변경해야 하는 시점을 묻고, AdaRSI(온디맨드 재귀적 자기 개선)를 제안한다.
items.why_ko: 로봇과 같은 구현 에이전트가 복잡한 미지의 환경에서 실패를 통해 학습하고 스스로 개선하는 능력을 향상시켜, 실제 세계에서의 AI 로봇 배포를 더욱 실용적으로 만든다.

items.title: SafeAdapt-Poker: Counterfactual Risk Calibration for Budgeted Adaptation under Opponent Shift
items.body: Opponent histories can mislead after behavioral shifts. SafeAdapt-Poker formulates budgeted adaptation under opponent shift as a dual-counterfactual sequential-control problem using only information available before each decision. At each decision the controller asks two distinct questions: what local downside a deviation from the frozen anchor would induce under matched legal continuations, and what future adaptation value would be lost by consuming part of the remaining deviation budget now. The first question is answered by a monotone strategic-risk model over deviation intensity; the second by a paired budget-state continuation model that prices current budget consumption. The controller selects among support-preserving candidate deviations by trading immediate adaptation value against these two quantities, a pathwise cumulative-KL ledger bounds total anchor-relative deviation, and a finite family of frozen controllers is screened on complete paired calibration sessions before held-out interaction. A finite-candidate perturbation bound shows that the allocation objective degrades continuously with continuation-value estimation error. Evaluation covers exact-game exploitation and safety, four opponent shifts, local-risk calibration, delayed-opportunity allocation, direct opportunity-value estimation, value-error robustness, factorial mechanism attribution, budget sensitivity, abstract-HUNL cross-play, and player/time-held-out public-history behavior. On exact Leduc the full controller attains a matched weak-pool gain of +0.0718 with a worst-opponent delta of -0.0126, raises delayed-opportunity capture from 0.6318 under myopic allocation to 0.7841 under the same session budget, and reaches +42.7 mbb/hand in abstract-HUNL cross-play; the retained public-history screen reports 0.5820 action accuracy and 0.9277 log loss versus 0.5039 and 0.9778 for a public prior.
items.title_ko: SafeAdapt-Poker: 상대 변화에 따른 예산 제약 적응을 위한 반사실적 위험 보정
items.summary_ko: 상대 이력은 행동 변화 후 오해를 불러일으킬 수 있다. SafeAdapt-Poker는 상대 변화에 따른 예산 제약 적응을 이중 반사실적 순차 제어 문제로 공식화하여, 각 결정 전에 사용 가능한 정보만을 활용한다.
items.why_ko: 불확실한 환경, 특히 상대방의 전략이 변하는 상황에서 AI 에이전트가 제한된 자원(예산) 내에서 합리적인 위험 관리를 통해 적응할 수 있는 방법을 제시한다.

items.title: ChronoCulture: Evaluating Cultural Awareness Across Time in Large Language Models
items.body: Cultural attitudes and social norms evolve over time, yet most cultural benchmarks for large language models (LLMs) treat culture as a static attribute of a country or region. We introduce ChronoCulture, a benchmark of 10,360 temporal pairs built from longitudinal survey data across 72 countries. Each pair contains the same survey question asked in the same country in an older and a newer year, with full population response distributions as ground truth. Across six LLMs, we find that models can often predict a country's attitudes at one point in time but do not reliably capture how those attitudes change. Their predictions for different years tend to stay close together, failing to capture much of the observed change. Specifying the intended year in the prompt also offers little overall improvement in alignment with survey responses. These findings suggest that models often present a largely static picture of cultural attitudes, highlighting the need to evaluate cultural awareness across time.
items.title_ko: ChronoCulture: 대규모 언어 모델의 시간 경과에 따른 문화적 인식 평가
items.summary_ko: 문화적 태도와 사회적 규범은 시간에 따라 진화하지만, 대부분의 LLM 문화 벤치마크는 문화를 정적인 속성으로 다룬다. 이 연구는 72개국에서 수집된 종단적 설문조사 데이터를 기반으로 10,360개의 시간적 쌍을 구축한 ChronoCulture 벤치마크를 소개한다.
items.why_ko: LLM이 시간에 따라 변화하는 문화적 맥락을 얼마나 잘 이해하고 반영하는지 평가하는 새로운 방법을 제시하여, 더욱 정교하고 시의적절한 문화적 지식을 갖춘 AI 모델 개발에 기여한다.

items.title: Selective Growing Q-Networks (SGQN): An Analysis of Adaptive Action Grids in Decoupled Q-Learning
items.body: Value-based Q-learning for continuous control can discretise the action space, but the resolution of the discretisation trades early exploration against final precision. Growing Q-Networks (GQN) grow the resolution uniformly from coarse to fine. We introduce Selective Growing Q-Networks (SGQN), which keeps decoupled Q-learning and replaces uniform growth with an adaptive action grid: bins are added next to bins with high estimated Q-value, bins with low Q-value are pruned, and actions are chosen epsilon-greedily. On eight DeepMind Control Suite (DMControl) tasks with 2 to 12 action dimensions, SGQN has the highest mean final return among the compared methods on four, is within 1.1% of the best method on three more, and is 3.4% below Bang-Bang MPO on Walker Run, using on average 7.5 of 9 available bins per dimension. We then test whether the adaptive grid explains these results, and find that it does not. Growth activates every candidate bin and behaves like uniform growth, and removing pruning changes the return by at most 1.1%. Two other choices matter: starting from a coarse grid, since starting with all 9 bins produces collapsed seeds, and epsilon-greedy selection, since an annealed softmax lowers the return by 23% to 100%. SGQN is insensitive to its growth and pruning hyperparameters. It also differs from the GQN and DecQN baselines in other respects, notably one gradient update per environment step instead of one per eight, which we did not control for, so we do not attribute its advantage to a single component. We present SGQN as a competitive value-based method and as an analysis of which ingredients of a growing action grid matter.
items.title_ko: Selective Growing Q-Networks (SGQN): 디커플링 Q-학습의 적응형 액션 그리드 분석
items.summary_ko: 연속 제어를 위한 값 기반 Q-학습은 액션 공간을 이산화할 수 있지만, 해상도는 초기 탐색과 최종 정밀도 사이의 균형점이다. SGQN은 균일한 해상도 증가 대신 적응형 액션 그리드를 사용하여 높은 Q-값을 가진 부분에 더 많은 해상도를 할당한다.
items.why_ko: 강화 학습에서 연속적인 액션 공간을 보다 효율적으로 탐색하고 정밀도를 높이는 새로운 방법을 제시하여, 로봇 제어와 같은 실제 환경에서의 AI 학습 성능을 향상시킬 수 있다.

items.title: Learning by Examples: Power Grid Steady State Analysis with a Tabular Foundation Model
items.body: Foundation models have shown strong generalization across scientific domains, but their use in power systems remains largely task-specific. We investigate whether a pretrained tabular foundation model (TFM), TabPFN, can serve as a general-purpose neural solver for power grid steady-state analysis. We evaluate the TFM on three tasks: power flow (PF) prediction, N-k contingency screening (NCS), and voltage stability margin (VSM) prediction. We performed experiments on 118- and 2000-bus systems, comparing the TFM against task-specific neural baselines. Without retraining or fine-tuning, the TFM matches or outperforms the best task-specific model in several settings across the three tasks. For 118-bus PF prediction, a variant of the TFM achieves errors of $1\times 10^{-3}$ pu for voltage magnitudes and $0.30^\circ$ for voltage angles, outperforming all baselines. On unseen N-1 contingency and close-to-infeasible PF cases, the TFM is competitive with the DCPF approximation. For millions of unseen N-2 contingencies, the TFM achieves AUCs of 0.92 and 0.95 for branch and voltage violation screening, respectively. The TFM also attains accurate VSM prediction performance for the 2000-bus system with limited labelled data. The TFM attains strong results across the tested tasks despite pretraining without any power-system-specific dataset and requiring no fine-tuning step. These results offer a glimpse into the potential of pretrained TFMs as a neural solver for a range of power grid analysis tasks.
items.title_ko: 예시를 통한 학습: 표 형식 파운데이션 모델을 이용한 전력망 정상 상태 분석
items.summary_ko: 파운데이션 모델은 다양한 과학 분야에서 강력한 일반화 능력을 보여주었지만, 전력 시스템에서의 사용은 주로 특정 작업에 국한되었다. 이 연구는 사전 훈련된 표 형식 파운데이션 모델(TFM)인 TabPFN이 전력망 정상 상태 분석을 위한 범용 신경망 솔버 역할을 할 수 있는지 조사한다.
items.why_ko: 기존의 복잡한 전력 시스템 분석에 범용 AI 모델을 적용하는 새로운 가능성을 제시하며, 이는 에너지 관리 및 스마트 그리드 분야에서 AI의 활용 범위를 넓힐 수 있다.

items.title: Equal CER, Unequal Damage: Severity-Weighted Character Error Rate for OCR
items.body: Character Error Rate (CER), the standard metric for OCR and vision-language models (VLMs), charges a typo as much as a wrong name. We introduce semCER, which keeps CER's alignment and denominator and charges each grapheme edit a severity from an LLM judge, with no word segmentation. Normalized CER keeps the score of a whole transcription, where it tracks readers as well as semCER or better, and semCER breaks that score down into named edits. The charges track readers' ratings edit by edit in English, Vietnamese, and Chinese and put the edits readers rate most severe near the top of a sorted list. On pairs drawn where CER and semCER disagreed, readers side with semCER more often than with normalized CER in English and Chinese, and equally often in Vietnamese. Across 16 languages, the judge charges a wrong diacritic or tone mark almost nothing in Spanish but nearly a wrong letter's severity in Telugu. Where we can count real words, a general VLM's wrong letter forms one far above chance while a classical pipeline's stays near it. We release the 61 million judged edits, the aggregated reader ratings, and the distilled scorer at https://github.com/nguyenx2t/semcer.
items.title_ko: 동일한 CER, 불균등한 피해: OCR을 위한 심각도 가중치 문자 오류율 (Severity-Weighted CER)
items.summary_ko: OCR 및 시각-언어 모델(VLM)의 표준 지표인 문자 오류율(CER)은 오타와 잘못된 이름을 동일하게 취급한다. 이 연구는 LLM 심사관으로부터 각 그래프 편집에 심각도 가중치를 부여하는 semCER을 도입한다.
items.why_ko: OCR 평가의 현실적인 정확도를 높여, 중요도에 따라 오류를 다르게 평가함으로써 실제 사용 환경에서 더욱 신뢰할 수 있는 OCR 시스템 개발에 기여할 수 있다.

items.title: MolLean: A Process-Verifiable Language for Chemical Reasoning
items.body: Chemical chain-of-thought can contain hallucinated structural and property claims. We thereby introduce MolLean, a process-verifiable language that grounds chemical reasoning in an explicit molecular state. A layered Lean-based kernel checks state transitions and assertions over molecular readouts, from primitive graph edits to compound transformations. Meanwhile, a typed witness protocol separates native structural checks from externally supplied measurements. We further introduce MolLean-MCP, a stateful tool interface that exposes these transitions, checks, and readouts during generation: the model receives feedback to decide its next action, and rejected actions leave the state unchanged. MolLean supports one-pass trace execution, whole-trace refinement, and interactive reasoning through MolLean-MCP. We evaluate these three modes with direct chain-of-thought on 8,800 matched examples across 12 tasks spanning molecular generation, editing, optimization, and reactions. With Qwen3.6-27B, whole-trace refinement outperforms direct chain-of-thought on all 12 tasks. MolLean-MCP complements whole-trace refinement with stepwise verification feedback, reaching better performance in reaction tasks. Together, these results highlight an executable foundation for chemical reasoning, in which explicit chemical commitments can be checked and revised rather than remaining solely in free-form explanations.
items.title_ko: MolLean: 화학적 추론을 위한 프로세스 검증 가능 언어
items.summary_ko: 화학적 사고의 사슬은 환각적 구조 및 속성 주장을 포함할 수 있다. 이 연구는 명시적인 분자 상태에서 화학적 추론을 기반으로 하는 프로세스 검증 가능 언어인 MolLean을 소개한다.
items.why_ko: AI 기반 화학 연구에서 환각을 줄이고 추론의 신뢰성을 높이는 새로운 언어 및 프레임워크를 제시하며, 이는 신약 개발 및 재료 과학 분야에 중요한 영향을 미칠 수 있다.

items.title: Same Claim, Different Interpretations: How LLM Agents Resolve Ambiguity in Scientific Claims
items.body: Co-scientists and agentic scientific claim verifiers are increasingly used to assess claims across the sciences. Natural-language scientific claims, written for human experts, are often underspecified and so admit several defensible interpretations. Such verifiers usually pick one, often tacitly, and benchmarks score their verdicts against expert labels without recording the expert's interpretation or the verifier's in a comparable form. This leads to disagreements with expert labels that cannot be traced to the evidence or the interpretation, and to compute spent on unchecked interpretations. We introduce Claim Cards to make such interpretations explicit in the reasoning itself. A Claim Card records a verifier's interpretation as nine fields before evidence gathering, each marked stated, inferred, or default. To test whether an agent's interpretation can change its verdict, we ran a GPT-5.4 agent five times on each of 60 expert-labeled materials-science and biomedical claims with a card, without one, and with one card frozen across runs (900 runs). Over 40% of card fields were not marked stated, and a card added about a tenth to a run's GPT-5.4 tokens and time without measurably changing agreement with expert labels. The agent's own interpretations varied between runs, although within a claim this variation did not measurably track the verdict. A deliberate change to one field of the frozen card, however, making the quantifier universal or the threshold for support stricter, changed the verdict on about a third of the claims, against about one in seven expected by chance (p < 0.001 for each edit). On 24 materials-science claims run with computational tools, the stricter threshold also changed what the agent asked those tools to compute. We therefore argue that verdicts should be reported with their interpretations and that benchmarks could publish the interpretation behind each label.
items.title_ko: 동일한 주장, 다른 해석: LLM 에이전트가 과학적 주장의 모호성을 해결하는 방법
items.summary_ko: 공동 과학자와 에이전트 기반 과학적 주장 검증자는 과학 분야 전반의 주장을 평가하는 데 점점 더 많이 사용되지만, 자연어 과학 주장은 종종 불완전하여 여러 해석을 허용한다. 이 연구는 LLM 에이전트가 이러한 모호성을 어떻게 해결하는지 분석한다.
items.why_ko: 과학적 주장 검증에서 LLM 에이전트의 한계를 파악하고, 모호한 주장을 더 정확하고 신뢰성 있게 해석하는 방법을 제시하여, AI 기반 과학 연구의 신뢰도를 높이는 데 기여한다.

items.title: The COUNT: Counting N-grams Unlocks Scaling on Host Memory and Training-Free Adaptation
items.body: The scaling relationship of compute and performance for language models (LMs) has been extensively studied; more recently, models are being designed to scale memory use, as well. In particular, adding embeddings for n-grams scales memory separately from compute use, because each pass only processes individual embedding rows, which are much smaller than the storage used for the whole embedding table. However, existing methods train embeddings from scratch, which needs expensive GPU memory for fast reading and writing. Meanwhile, the ordinary memory of the host system is cheap and underutilized by these training methods. To scale on host memory, we introduce COUNT (Counting Offline Unlocks N-gram Transformers), which builds n-gram embeddings without adding learned parameters by storing precomputed n-gram counts on host. We use the corpus frequencies to weight together the LM's own unembeddings of the next tokens most often following the current n-gram history. At a fixed compute budget, COUNT can be added as an additional input embedding for pretraining 1B-parameter LMs to improve validation loss as much as an LM with 57% more compute. If GPU memory is limited, using COUNT to let backbone parameters fill GPU memory gives better performance than splitting memory with additional learned n-gram embeddings. Beyond efficiency, COUNT allows switching in a different table of n-gram counts from a domain-specific corpus at inference time to adapt to a new task without any training.
items.title_ko: COUNT: N-그램 카운팅으로 호스트 메모리 스케일링 및 훈련 없는 적응 가능
items.summary_ko: 언어 모델(LM)의 컴퓨팅 및 성능 간의 스케일링 관계는 잘 연구되었지만, 최근에는 메모리 사용량 스케일링에 대한 관심이 높아지고 있다. 이 연구는 N-그램 임베딩을 추가하는 것이 메모리를 컴퓨팅 사용량과 별도로 확장시키는 'COUNT' 방법을 제안한다.
items.why_ko: 언어 모델의 메모리 효율성을 크게 향상시키고, 값비싼 GPU 메모리 없이도 호스트 메모리에서 대규모 N-그램 임베딩을 활용하여 모델을 훈련 없이 적응시킬 수 있는 실용적인 방법을 제시한다.

items.title: What Does Disagreement Mean? A Semantic Identifiability Frontier for Pairwise Preference Learning
items.body: Pairwise comparison data are a standard supervision signal in preference learning, but disagreement in such data can reflect stable latent heterogeneity, ephemeral stochasticity, or non-binary responses hidden by a forced-choice interface. We study which of these semantic distinctions are identifiable from the feedback channel itself. We introduce a nonparametric latent semantic model with three querywise quantities: aggregate directional preference $μ_q$, persistent disagreement $τ_q$, and non-binary mass $α_q$. Under the anonymous binary channel, we prove an exact semantic fiber theorem: $μ_q$ is point-identified, whereas $(τ_q, α_q)$ vary over an explicit feasible region compatible with the same binary law. Same-annotator repeats identify $τ_q$ through a covariance identity, abstention-enabled feedback identifies $α_q$ directly, and together they point-identify the full semantic triple. We also derive finite-sample estimators, nonasymptotic concentration bounds, and semantics-aware action-recovery guarantees, and validate the theory on theorem-matched synthetic data.
items.title_ko: 불일치가 의미하는 것: 쌍별 선호도 학습을 위한 의미론적 식별성 경계
items.summary_ko: 쌍별 비교 데이터는 선호도 학습의 표준 감독 신호이지만, 이러한 데이터의 불일치는 안정적인 잠재 이질성, 일시적인 확률성 또는 강제 선택 인터페이스에 숨겨진 비이진 응답을 반영할 수 있다. 이 연구는 피드백 채널 자체로부터 어떤 의미론적 구분이 식별 가능한지 연구한다.
items.why_ko: 사용자 선호도 데이터의 복잡성을 더 깊이 이해하고, 불일치 데이터로부터 숨겨진 의미론적 정보를 식별하는 방법을 제시하여, 개인화된 AI 시스템의 학습 및 추천 시스템의 정확도를 향상시킨다.

items.title: The Accuracy Well: Nonmonotone Accuracy Dynamics at Vanishing Initialization
items.body: We study classification dynamics under small initialization and identify a pronounced non-monotone behavior of accuracy that we call the accuracy well: accuracy rises rapidly early in training, subsequently drops, and only much later recovers. We observe this phenomenon in deep linear networks, fully connected ReLU networks on MNIST, deep convolutional networks on CIFAR-10, and controlled synthetic tasks, across different losses and optimizers and in both training and test accuracy. We propose a three-stage explanation in terms of target-driven organization, a degeneracy bottleneck, and subsequent recruitment and recovery. We develop a rigorous theory of these dynamics for shallow and deep linear networks, showing in particular that high accuracy can emerge while the predictor and the change in loss remain asymptotically vanishing, before continued optimization causes accuracy to deteriorate. For a simple synthetic classification task, we prove an extreme instance in which accuracy asymptotically rises to 100%, collapses to 0, and later recovers permanently to 100%. Our results show that classification accuracy can reveal aspects of learning dynamics that are not captured by the training loss alone.
items.title_ko: 정확도 우물: 사라지는 초기화에서 비단조적인 정확도 동역학
items.summary_ko: 이 연구는 작은 초기화 하에서 분류 동역학을 연구하며, '정확도 우물(accuracy well)'이라는 뚜렷한 비단조적인 정확도 행동을 발견한다. 즉, 훈련 초기에 정확도가 급격히 상승했다가 하락하고 나중에야 회복된다.
items.why_ko: 심층 신경망 학습 초기에 나타나는 예상치 못한 정확도 하락 현상을 규명하고, 이는 모델 초기화 및 훈련 전략 설계에 중요한 통찰을 제공하여 더 안정적이고 효율적인 모델 학습에 기여할 수 있다.

items.title: From Training to Escalation: Forensic Analysis and Local Recreation of RL/RLHF-Induced Privilege Escalation in AI Agents (CVE-2026-65616)
items.body: Mid-2026 reporting on autonomous AI evaluation incidents claimed that frontier large language model (LLM) agents escaped server containment through emergent coordination and cloud infrastructure attacks. This paper contextualizes those claims through forensic analysis and containerized recreation of both the Highly Persistent Internal Model (HPIM) training-case conditions and the Phase One privilege escalation targeting internal package repositories during OpenAI's ExploitGym evaluations. We recreate the configuration of the OpenAI-provided training example and reproduce the cryptographic verification bypass (CVE-2026-65616) in isolated repository servers, where misconfigured systems enabled token forgery and privilege escalation through basic HTTP requests, Python, and JavaScript. Crucially, the training-example conditions and the Phase One (and later) misconfigurations share the same exploitable patterns. Our analysis explains how Zero Trust Architecture principles neutralize this shared attack vector. Contemporary AI risks derive directly from training and deployment conditions in ambivalent learning environments lacking adequate containment measures.
items.body_ko: 2026년 중반에 자율 AI 평가 사고에 대한 보고서에 따르면, 최신 LLM(대규모 언어 모델) 에이전트가 긴급 협업 및 클라우드 인프라 공격을 통해 서버 격리에서 벗어났다고 주장했습니다. 이 논문은 OpenAI의 ExploitGym 평가 중 HPIM(Highly Persistent Internal Model) 훈련 사례 조건과 내부 패키지 저장소를 대상으로 한 1단계 권한 에스컬레이션에 대한 포렌식 분석 및 컨테이너화된 재현을 통해 이러한 주장을 맥락화합니다. 우리는 OpenAI가 제공한 훈련 예제의 구성을 재현하고 격리된 저장소 서버에서 암호화 검증 우회(CVE-2026-65616)를 재현했습니다. 여기서 잘못 구성된 시스템은 기본 HTTP 요청, Python 및 JavaScript를 통해 토큰 위조 및 권한 에스컬레이션을 가능하게 했습니다. 결정적으로, 훈련 예제 조건과 1단계(및 이후) 잘못된 구성은 동일한 악용 가능한 패턴을 공유합니다. 우리의 분석은 제로 트러스트 아키텍처 원칙이 이 공유된 공격 벡터를 어떻게 무력화하는지 설명합니다. 현대 AI 위험은 적절한 격리 조치가 부족한 모호한 학습 환경에서의 훈련 및 배포 조건에서 직접적으로 발생합니다.
items.title_ko: 훈련부터 특권 확대까지: AI 에이전트의 특권 확대 포렌식 분석 및 재현 (CVE-2026-65616)
items.summary_ko: 2026년 중반 자율 AI 평가 사고 보고서는 최첨단 LLM 에이전트가 클라우드 인프라 공격을 통해 서버 격리를 탈출했다고 주장했다. 이 논문은 이러한 주장을 OpenAI의 ExploitGym 평가 중 내부 패키지 리포지토리를 대상으로 한 1단계 특권 확대의 포렌식 분석 및 컨테이너화된 재현을 통해 맥락화한다.
items.why_ko: AI 에이전트의 보안 취약점, 특히 특권 확대 가능성을 실제 사례 분석과 재현을 통해 깊이 있게 다루며, 이는 최첨단 LLM 기반 시스템의 안전성 확보와 윤리적 배포에 매우 중요한 경고이자 실무 지식이다.

items.title: SwarmRSI: Recursive Self-Improvement through Evolving Scientific Agent Swarm
items.body: Recursive self-improvement (RSI) in scientific research aims to improve agents' research capabilities through their own experimental experience. Scientific agent swarms can combine evidence and implementations from different research directions to guide their agents' subsequent experiments. However, poor experimental results can leave unclear whether to revise a hypothesis or its implementation, while overall program scores can hide components useful to other agents. To address these challenges, we introduce SwarmRSI, a framework that evolves scientific agent swarms for recursive self-improvement. We devise Feedback-Guided Swarm Mutation to refine hypotheses and their implementations using experimental feedback from other agents. We also propose Complementary Swarm Recombination to reuse retained hypotheses and complementary program components across agents, allowing partial results to support new research. Recursive Swarm Evolution integrates both mechanisms into a feedback loop, using new experimental evidence to guide subsequent research. Experiments on OpenProblems, NatureBench and MLE-Bench Lite demonstrate SwarmRSI's state-of-the-art (SOTA) performance. Further evaluations show that accumulated research experience improves performance on held-out tasks. Biologists also reproduce its programs for follow-up biological analyses.
items.title_ko: SwarmRSI: 진화하는 과학 에이전트 군집을 통한 재귀적 자기 개선
items.summary_ko: 과학 연구에서 재귀적 자기 개선(RSI)은 에이전트의 실험 경험을 통해 연구 능력을 향상시키는 것을 목표로 한다. 과학 에이전트 군집은 다양한 연구 방향의 증거와 구현을 결합하여 에이전트의 후속 실험을 안내할 수 있다.
items.why_ko: 여러 AI 에이전트가 협력하고 서로의 경험을 통해 스스로 개선하는 '에이전트 군집' 개념을 통해 과학 연구의 효율성과 발견 능력을 향상시키는 새로운 패러다임을 제시한다.

items.title: Continual Learning for Reliable In-Sequence Molecular Communication
items.body: This paper considers reliable in-sequence molecular communication, where bio-nanomachines exchange molecule-encoded information in a specified order, and investigates a new simulation-based method to incrementally evaluate communication protocols by gradually increasing the complexity of experimental settings. The proposed method, called Affine Memory Replay (AMR), builds a continual learning (CL) model to estimate communication performance between bio-nanomachines. AMR stores past simulation samples and synthesizes additional replay samples through interpolation and extrapolation between past samples. Through incremental performance estimation tasks, it replays both past and synthetic samples to regularize model updates, helping the model adapt to new experimental settings while retaining knowledge from earlier ones. Experimental results show that AMR significantly outperforms existing CL methods in maintaining overall estimation accuracy across sequentially learned estimation tasks. It effectively balances memory stability and learning plasticity under moderate training cost.
items.title_ko: 지속 학습을 통한 신뢰할 수 있는 순차적 분자 통신
items.summary_ko: 이 논문은 바이오 나노 머신이 특정 순서로 분자 인코딩 정보를 교환하는 신뢰할 수 있는 순차적 분자 통신을 다룬다. 실험 환경의 복잡성을 점진적으로 증가시켜 통신 프로토콜을 점진적으로 평가하는 새로운 시뮬레이션 기반 방법인 Affine Memory Replay (AMR)를 조사한다.
items.why_ko: 분자 통신 분야에서 지속 학습을 활용하여 복잡한 통신 프로토콜의 성능을 효율적으로 평가하는 방법을 제시하며, 이는 나노 기술 및 바이오 센서 분야의 발전에 기여할 수 있다.

items.title: Analyzing performance of Retrieval Augmented Generation models for Question Answering Tasks
items.body: Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) models have become almost a cornerstone of open-domain question answering tasks; in which the quality of answers generated in the process, greatly relies on the effectiveness of retrieval mechanisms. In the realm of LLM, the last two years have seen tremendous progress in RAG architectures, with many models reporting to have improved performance through various design innovations. The cultural question and answering systems of South Asia, in particular, present a specific challenge since the region is home to the vast number of languages and traditions, which are closely interrelated. Along with these deeply intertwined historical narratives increase the need for culturally grounded and context-aware interpretation. Despite major architectural advances in LLMs, claiming significant improvements, challenges remain when answering these region specific questions in native languages. In this study, we aim to extract high-performing factors to guide the development of optimized hybrid RAG systems. We further explore whether the integration of RAG changes performance differently for culturally grounded and non-cultural questions in a South Asian multilingual setup, and whether RAG produces a higher overall percentage of correct answers than contexted answering. We also examine how LLM performance changes when RAG methods are integrated into the question-answering pipeline in comparison with non-contexted and contexted answering and, evaluate whether the introduction of RAG benefits popular or non-popular culturally grounded questions more. Not only does our work evaluate the current methods but also carves a path for future designs of more accurate and efficient question-answering pipelines.
items.title_ko: 질의응답 태스크를 위한 검색 증강 생성(RAG) 모델 성능 분석
items.summary_ko: 검색 증강 생성(RAG) 모델은 오픈 도메인 질의응답 태스크의 핵심이 되었지만, 생성된 답변의 품질은 검색 메커니즘의 효율성에 크게 의존한다. 이 연구는 RAG 모델의 성능을 분석한다.
items.why_ko: RAG 모델의 핵심 구성 요소인 검색 메커니즘의 중요성을 강조하고 성능 분석을 통해, 개발자들이 질의응답 시스템의 정확성과 효율성을 높이는 데 실질적인 도움을 줄 수 있다.

items.title: OrionMoE-v1.0: A Mixture-of-Experts Foundation Model for Tabular In-Context Learning
items.body: Tabular foundation models enable in-context learning by predicting unseen observations from a labeled support table without task-specific parameter updates. Despite recent advances, most existing approaches rely on dense architectures that apply the same transformations across features and datasets. We introduce OrionMoE-Small, a compact tabular foundation model that combines distribution-aware representations with dataset-conditioned sparse mixture-of-experts computation. Built on a dual-axis Transformer architecture, OrionMoE-Small selectively activates experts along the feature axis, with routing decisions informed by both individual feature representations and the broader dataset context. This design enables adaptive allocation of computation across heterogeneous tabular problems while retaining a shared computational pathway across tasks. OrionMoE-Small is pretrained entirely on synthetic classification tasks generated from a structured causal prior and performs downstream prediction without gradient-based adaptation. Experiments across multiple tabular benchmarks demonstrate competitive performance against substantially larger foundation models, with particularly strong results on small-context and high-dimensional datasets. Further analysis reveals favorable relative performance under class imbalance and highlights the importance of feature composition.
items.title_ko: OrionMoE-v1.0: 표 형식 In-Context 학습을 위한 MoE 파운데이션 모델
items.summary_ko: 표 형식 파운데이션 모델은 작업별 매개변수 업데이트 없이 레이블이 지정된 지원 테이블에서 보이지 않는 관측치를 예측하여 In-Context 학습을 가능하게 한다. OrionMoE-Small은 데이터셋 조건부 희소 MoE 계산을 결합한 컴팩트한 표 형식 파운데이션 모델이다.
items.why_ko: 표 형식 데이터에 대한 In-Context 학습의 효율성을 높이는 MoE 기반 모델로, 이는 복잡한 비즈니스 데이터 분석 및 의사결정 시스템에 AI를 적용하는 데 중요한 발전을 의미한다.

items.title: From Unreliable to Usable: Decomposing Failure Modes and Confidence Signals in LLM Entity Extraction - Evidence from Cyber Threat Intelligence
items.body: Audits of large language model (LLM) extraction from full-length documents report severe unreliability, leaving two questions open: what the failures actually consist of, and whether confidence signals can turn unreliable output into usable output. We run a preregistered, fully frozen evaluation of two new-generation low-cost LLMs (DeepSeek-V4-Flash, GLM-5.3-Flash) with a flagship-tier control (GPT-6.1-Sol) on a public corpus of 354 incident campaigns (315 unique reports, 630 model-report evaluations), scoring extraction quality against gold, confidence calibration, and robustness to single-sentence perturbations. Three findings emerge. (1) Unreliability persists across tiers: micro precision is 0.03-0.34 and verbalized calibration error (ECE) 0.53-0.94 across both splits; the gap does not close at the flagship tier. (2) The dominant failure is not hallucination: a full mention census plus a three-tier annotation of 360 sampled candidates (two independent LLM annotators from vendors outside the evaluated set, Cohen's kappa = 0.79 on the preregistered acceptance line, fully disclosed) back-projects to 65.6% background mentions and 19.9% gold-scope gaps, with only 1.2% unsupported candidates. (3) Confidence ranks but does not verify: zero-cost self-consistency-frequency tiering passes a preregistered top-30% precision-gain bar in all six test-split model-type cells (4/6 on train), the zero-cost text-frequency x SC frequency combination wins 3, ties 2, loses 1 across cells, yet relation-level counterfactuals on all 45 targets show that a single misattribution sentence flips high-confidence judgments in 95.6-100% of cases, and even a background sentence explicitly marked as unrelated still binds a fake vulnerability in up to 26.7% of them. We conclude with a deployment boundary: confidence tiering may set review priorities, never truth.
items.title_ko: 불신뢰성에서 유용성으로: LLM 개체 추출의 실패 모드 및 신뢰 신호 분해 - 사이버 위협 정보 사례
items.summary_ko: 전체 길이 문서에서 LLM 추출의 심각한 불신뢰성에 대한 보고가 있었지만, 실패 원인과 신뢰 신호의 역할은 미해결로 남아있다. 이 연구는 사이버 위협 정보(CTI) 말뭉치를 사용하여 두 개의 새로운 저비용 LLM과 GPT-6.1-Sol의 실패 모드 및 신뢰 신호를 평가한다.
items.why_ko: LLM 기반 정보 추출 시스템의 신뢰성 문제를 실제 적용 사례를 통해 심층 분석하고, 실패 원인과 신뢰도 향상 방법을 제시하여 LLM의 실용적 활용을 위한 중요한 지침을 제공한다.

items.title: Tracking a Small Set of Experts in Online Convex Optimization
items.body:
For the fundamental problem of prediction from expert advice, Freund asked whether one could compete with a comparator that switches $k$ times among only $m$ experts. For a discrete set of experts, this problem was resolved by Bousquet and Warmuth (2020), who gave an efficient algorithm with optimal regret matching the information-theoretic limit.
We study the analogous problem in online convex optimization, where the action space is continuous. An inefficient algorithm can be derived by discretizing the action space and applying the Bousquet--Warmuth algorithm, giving regret of $\widetilde{O}(md+k)$, while the best known efficient algorithm for this problem has regret $\widetilde{O}(dk)$. We show that this computational inefficiency is inherent, establishing a separation between the information-theoretic and polynomial-time regret achievable for this problem. Specifically, under the hypergraphic planted-clique conjecture, we show that for every polynomial-time algorithm there exist instances for which it incurs at least $(k\sqrt d)^{1-o(1)}$ regret.
items.title_ko: 온라인 볼록 최적화에서 소수 전문가 추적
items.summary_ko: 전문가 조언을 통한 예측이라는 근본적인 문제에 대해, Freund는 $m$명의 전문가 중 $k$번 전환하는 비교자와 경쟁할 수 있는지 물었다. 이 연구는 온라인 볼록 최적화에서 유사한 문제를 다룬다.
items.why_ko: 온라인 학습 환경에서 제한된 수의 전문가를 효율적으로 활용하여 최적의 의사결정을 내리는 방법을 제시하며, 이는 동적으로 변화하는 AI 시스템 및 추천 시스템 설계에 적용될 수 있다.

items.title: One Size Does Not Fit All: Curvature-Aware Adaptive Perturbation for SAM
items.body: Poor generalisation in deep neural networks is frequently associated with convergence to sharp minima. Sharpness-Aware Minimisation (SAM) improves generalisation of deep neural networks by minimising a combination of the training loss and the local sharpness of the loss landscape, biasing convergence towards flat minima. However, SAM relies on a fixed perturbation radius $ρ$ that ignores local curvature, leading to inefficient behaviour: the perturbation may be too small to escape poor basins defined by sharp local minima, or too large to allow convergence to solutions with good loss-sharpness tradeoff. We reinterpret $ρ$ as the intensity of the perturbation signal and propose Curvature-Aware Adaptive Perturbation for SAM (CAP-SAM), a geometry-aware method that modulates the perturbation radius based on a sharpness ratio, enabling a more effective search for robust minima on the loss landscape. We prove that CAP-SAM preserves the same convergence rate as standard SAM in non-convex stochastic settings. Extensive experiments indicate that our approach consistently outperforms SAM and its most prominent variants across diverse network architectures on CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, and ImageNet.
items.title_ko: 하나의 크기가 모두에게 적합하지 않다: SAM을 위한 곡률 인식 적응형 섭동
items.summary_ko: 심층 신경망의 낮은 일반화 성능은 종종 sharp minima로의 수렴과 관련이 있다. SAM(Sharpness-Aware Minimization)은 훈련 손실과 손실 곡면의 국부적 sharpnes를 최소화하여 일반화를 개선하지만, 고정된 섭동 반경을 사용하여 비효율적이다. 이 연구는 곡률 인식을 통한 적응형 섭동을 제안한다.
items.why_ko: SAM의 효율성을 개선하고 모델의 일반화 성능을 더욱 향상시키는 방법을 제시하며, 이는 딥러닝 모델의 훈련 안정성과 실제 배포 성능에 긍정적인 영향을 미칠 수 있다.

items.title: When Does Momentum Help in Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Rewards?
items.body: Momentum is a classical tool for accelerating convex optimization and a standard component of modern large language model training. Yet recent empirical work has questioned the usefulness of first-moment momentum in reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR). We study this question through a bandit formulation of RLVR with bias-corrected exponential moving average (EMA) momentum, where the EMA coefficient $β$ controls how quickly the weights on past gradients decay. When policy gradients are evaluated exactly, we prove that increasing $β$ within a range that prevents overshoot strictly accelerates optimization. When gradients are estimated from sampled responses, a positive expected gain can be obscured by sampling fluctuations. We show that as the learning rate $η$ decreases, the expected gain with fixed $β$ vanishes faster than these fluctuations, whereas increasing $β$ to keep $η/(1-β)$ within the safe regime preserves a nonvanishing gain that eventually dominates them. Bandit simulations quantitatively validate these predictions. RLVR experiments on Qwen3-4B-Base using SGD with EMA and AdamW support our principle of choosing larger coefficients in practical LLM post-training. On Qwen2.5-32B with AdamW, simply increasing $β_1$ improves mean validation accuracy by nearly $2$ percentage points over the conventional choice, demonstrating the principle's effectiveness at a larger model scale.
items.title_ko: 검증 가능한 보상 기반 강화 학습에서 모멘텀은 언제 도움이 되는가?
items.summary_ko: 모멘텀은 볼록 최적화를 가속화하는 고전적인 도구이지만, 최근 경험적 연구에서는 검증 가능한 보상 기반 강화 학습(RLVR)에서 1차 모멘텀의 유용성에 의문을 제기했다. 이 연구는 편향 보정된 EMA 모멘텀을 사용한 RLVR의 밴딧 공식화를 통해 이 질문을 연구한다.
items.why_ko: RLVR에서 모멘텀의 효과에 대한 명확한 이해를 제공하여, LLM 기반 강화 학습 모델의 훈련 과정에서 최적의 모멘텀 전략을 선택하고 성능을 극대화하는 데 도움을 준다.

items.title: Hyperspherical Contrastive Representations Unlock Planning and Exploration
items.body: We develop a self-supervised reinforcement learning algorithm that learns to build towers of up to eight cubes from scratch, without prior data, rewards, demonstrations, or pretrained models. Our method, Contrastive Planning via Spherical Linear Interpolation (C-Slerp), uses contrastive representations as reusable building blocks and repeatedly composes them to infer a sequence of intermediate waypoints. Under our hyperspherical parameterization, the learned representations allow intermediate waypoints to be inferred in closed form through spherical linear interpolation, without training a separate high-level policy or performing graph search. Importantly, the representation geometry also tells us how to adjust the number of waypoints based on the difficulty of each goal-reaching problem. Experiments show that our method succeeds on long-horizon navigation and robotic manipulation tasks, including settings where strong baselines fail to achieve a single success. Ablations further show that using a fixed number of waypoints substantially degrades performance, highlighting the importance of adapting the plan to task difficulty.
items.title_ko: 초구형 대조 표현이 계획 및 탐색 능력을 부여한다
items.summary_ko: 이 연구는 사전 데이터, 보상, 데모 또는 사전 훈련된 모델 없이 최대 8개의 큐브 타워를 처음부터 구축하도록 학습하는 자기 지도 강화 학습 알고리즘 C-Slerp(Contrastive Planning via Spherical Linear Interpolation)를 개발한다.
items.why_ko: 강화 학습에서 대조 학습과 초구형 표현을 활용하여 복잡한 계획 및 탐색 문제를 해결하는 새로운 방법을 제시하며, 이는 로봇 공학 및 자율 시스템 개발에 중요한 돌파구가 될 수 있다.

items.title: Posterior Frequencies and the Cost of Not Fitting: A Correction to a Memorization Lower Bound
items.body: Feldman's memorization lower bound assigns a frequency coefficient based on how often a point appears in the training sample. We give an exact three-point counterexample to its conditional and averaged forms, using independent fair labels and a permutation-equivariant learner. A sequence of sampling priors makes the ratio of the proposed penalty to actual excess risk grow exponentially, ruling out a universal positive constant-factor repair. The priors vary with sample size, the offending profiles become rare, and both quantities vanish. Retaining the original model, we obtain an exact replacement using full-sample posterior probabilities. Under exchangeability, these depend on multiplicity and the complete frequency profile. We characterize the largest multiplicity-only coefficients valid for unrestricted learners. The original coefficient has the posterior-mean form of Good's exact frequency formula and is an occupancy-weighted average of the corrected coefficients.
items.title_ko: 사후 주파수와 적합성 부족 비용: 암기 하한에 대한 수정
items.summary_ko: Feldman의 암기 하한은 훈련 샘플에 포인트가 나타나는 빈도에 따라 주파수 계수를 할당한다. 이 연구는 독립적인 공정한 레이블과 순열 불변 학습자를 사용하여 조건부 및 평균 형태에 대한 정확한 3점 반례를 제시한다.
items.why_ko: 기존의 암기 관련 이론적 하한에 대한 중요한 수정을 제시하여, 딥러닝 모델의 암기 현상을 더 정확하게 이해하고 과적합 방지 전략을 개선하는 데 기여한다.

items.title: Training Language Models to Fail Gracefully
items.body: Reinforcement learning makes language models better at solving tasks, but the same mechanism also rewards guessing. When success is the only way to earn reward, opting for a safe fallback is always worse than a long-shot attempt. When a wrong action can corrupt a database or ship broken code, that incentive can be costly. Therefore, we propose training models to fail gracefully: to preserve successful behavior whenever possible while learning to execute a safe fallback policy when acting would be unreliable. However, naively using policy gradients with intermediate reward for fallback behavior is brittle due to unfavorable optimization dynamics. We address this challenge with GracefulRL, which reshapes the optimization landscape to promote graceful failure. Importantly, this behavior emerges directly from outcome-level reward signals, without annotations specifying when to fall back or additional inference-time machinery such as a verifier. Across a range of tasks and scales, we train models that largely preserve their task-solving capability while selectively falling back when acting would be unreliable. More broadly, our results show that reinforcement learning can not only incentivize models to succeed, but also to reason about the limits of their capabilities and change course when they determine that success is out of reach.
items.title_ko: 언어 모델을 우아하게 실패하도록 훈련시키기
items.summary_ko: 강화 학습은 언어 모델의 작업 해결 능력을 향상시키지만, 동시에 추측을 보상하기도 한다. 이 연구는 모델을 '우아하게 실패하도록' 훈련시키는 방법을 제안한다. 즉, 가능한 경우 성공적인 행동을 유지하면서 행동이 위험할 경우 안전한 대체 정책을 실행하도록 학습시킨다.
items.why_ko: LLM이 고위험 작업에서 잘못된 행동을 피하고 안전하게 실패할 수 있도록 훈련하는 방법을 제시하여, 실제 환경에서의 LLM 배포 시 발생할 수 있는 잠재적 위험을 줄이고 신뢰성을 높이는 데 필수적이다.

items.title: HRTF Upsampling and Personalization via Neural Operators
items.body: Head-related transfer function (HRTF) spatial upsampling from sparse measurements is a fundamental challenge in personalized binaural audio. We formulate HRTF upsampling as an operator learning problem and introduce SPARO, a neural operator that maps sparse measurements at a set of spatial directions to the HRTF field, a continuous representation that can be queried at arbitrary positions. SPARO projects the measurements onto a learned set of spherical latent modes, processes the latent modes with Transformer blocks, and decodes the resulting representations at query directions. On SONICOM, using the LAP24 measurement configuration, SPARO attains the best log-spectral distortion (LSD) and interaural level difference (ILD) error at every sparsity level from 3 to 100 measurements (18% lower LSD and 43% lower ILD error than the strongest baseline at 100 measurements) while remaining competitive in interaural time difference (ITD) error. It reconstructs a dense HRTF 15 to 373 times faster than the leading neural-field method RANF. We further validate the approach on HUTUBS, demonstrating its effectiveness across HRTF datasets.
items.title_ko: 신경 연산자를 통한 HRTF 업샘플링 및 개인화
items.summary_ko: 희소한 측정값으로부터 HRTF(Head-Related Transfer Function) 공간 업샘플링은 개인화된 바이노럴 오디오의 근본적인 과제이다. 이 연구는 HRTF 업샘플링을 연산자 학습 문제로 공식화하고, 희소한 측정값을 HRTF 필드에 매핑하는 SPARO 신경 연산자를 소개한다.
items.why_ko: 개인화된 3D 오디오 기술의 핵심인 HRTF 모델링을 개선하여, 가상 현실, 증강 현실 및 고품질 오디오 경험을 위한 AI 기반 솔루션 개발에 기여할 수 있다.

items.title: Cortex: Consolidating Context into Parametric Memory
items.body: Context can improve large language model performance, but these gains may be lost after context removal. Inspired by biological systems consolidation, we formulate Memory Consolidation (MC) as internalizing these gains while preserving non-target capabilities, connecting context-specified editing, skill learning, and behavioral steering under a common objective. We introduce a five-task-family testbed measuring consolidation and retention under single, batch, and sequential updates. We propose Cortex, which generates prospective queries to anticipate uses of context and distills context-conditioned outputs into mergeable low-rank or structural feed-forward network updates. Across 4B--120B dense and mixture-of-experts backbones, including both text-only and multimodal models, Cortex lies on the empirical consolidation--retention Pareto frontier in most evaluated settings. After 50 sequential factual edits on a 14B model, Cortex-Structural recovers 88.9% of the context-induced gain while retaining 99.8% of original non-target performance.
items.title_ko: Cortex: 문맥을 파라미터 메모리로 통합하여 모델 성능 유지
items.summary_ko: 문맥 정보는 대규모 언어 모델의 성능을 향상시킬 수 있지만, 문맥 제거 후 이러한 이득이 손실될 수 있다. 이 연구는 생물학적 시스템 통합에서 영감을 받아 문맥 통합(Memory Consolidation, MC)을 목표 비대상 능력 보존과 함께 이러한 이득을 내재화하는 것으로 공식화한다.
items.why_ko: LLM이 문맥 정보를 단순히 활용하는 것을 넘어, 이를 모델의 파라미터 메모리에 영구적으로 통합하여 지속적인 성능 향상과 지식 보존을 가능하게 하는 중요한 연구이다.

items.title: From Human Corrections to Learned Segmentations: A Critical Mathematical Review of Information, Learning, and Human Effort
items.body: When does a human correction become useful learning, and what establishes better segmentation at matched human effort? This critical narrative review follows feedback through its selection, learner update, and evaluation. It compares active learning, machine teaching, interactive segmentation, and sequential predictive evaluation using a common mathematical account of target information, predictive error, response predictability, and human work. An exact Bayesian update converts evaluation-label information into expected log-loss improvement; an excess-risk decomposition explains what an approximate learner can lose. Conditional information decompositions separate the roles of selected locations, labels, and displayed context. Empirical comparisons show why response protocols, update mechanisms, and effort denominators matter, distinguishing current-mask refinement from reusable learning and simulated interaction from human evidence. We identify what logs can reveal, what requires independent evaluation, and what remains model-dependent. The resulting research priorities are to test what selection reveals, whether using it improves assimilation, and whether the resulting interaction policy benefits segmentation at matched effort. These are distinct claims: predicting a teacher's responses need not identify human intentions or establish better learning. No new acquisition algorithm or empirical superiority is claimed.
items.title_ko: 인간 교정에서 학습된 세분화까지: 정보, 학습, 인간 노력에 대한 비판적 수학적 검토
items.summary_ko: 인간의 교정이 언제 유용한 학습이 되고, 동일한 인간 노력으로 더 나은 세분화를 확립하는 것은 무엇인가? 이 비판적 검토는 피드백의 선택, 학습자 업데이트, 평가 과정을 따라가며 능동 학습, 기계 교육, 인터랙티브 세분화 등을 공통된 수학적 설명으로 비교한다.
items.why_ko: 인간의 피드백을 AI 모델 학습에 효율적으로 활용하는 방법에 대한 이론적 기반을 제공하여, 능동 학습 및 대화형 AI 시스템의 효율성과 성능을 높이는 데 기여한다.

items.title: FOLD: Position-Free Far Memory with Local Order for Long-Context Speculative Decoding
items.body: Speculative decoding accelerates LLM generation through lightweight drafting and parallel verification. It is particularly promising for long inputs, where KV-cache access costs can be amortized over multiple accepted tokens. Yet most drafters are trained on short sequences and degrade on long inputs, while long-context training is costly. Existing training-free approaches restrict the context window, rescale positions, or augment recent context with retrieved distant entries. Drafters, however, read target hidden states that already encode contextual and positional information, and their lightweight architecture makes full-history attention affordable. We propose FOLD, a training-free method that preserves exact local positions and treats all distant entries as far memory at a shared position. To counter attention dilution as the memory grows, we sharpen attention within it to emphasize relevant entries while separately controlling its total weight relative to the local window. Across six target-drafter pairs and diverse benchmarks of up to 256K tokens, FOLD predominantly delivers the highest speedup, with the best case more than doubling the speedup over autoregressive decoding, from 2.08$\times$ to 4.22$\times$.
items.title_ko: FOLD: 긴 컨텍스트 추측 디코딩을 위한 위치 독립적 원격 메모리
items.summary_ko: 추측 디코딩은 경량 초안 작성 및 병렬 검증을 통해 LLM 생성을 가속화한다. 긴 입력에 특히 유망하지만, 대부분의 초안 작성기는 짧은 시퀀스에 훈련되어 긴 입력에서는 성능이 저하된다. FOLD는 위치 독립적 원격 메모리를 제안한다.
items.why_ko: LLM의 긴 컨텍스트 처리 효율성을 높이고, 추측 디코딩의 성능을 개선하여 실시간 대규모 언어 모델 애플리케이션의 응답 속도와 자원 효율성을 향상시킨다.

items.title: From Relevance to Validity: Zero-Shot Tool Selection via Functional and Contextual Validation
items.body: Large language model (LLM) agents increasingly face tasks from unseen domains and execution contexts, making zero-shot tool selection essential for identifying tools that can satisfy task requirements. Existing dominant methods mainly rely on relevance ranking, but semantic matching alone cannot ensure that a tool is functionally compatible or remains applicable in a new context. We preliminarily identify a \emph{transfer-validity gap}, where semantically relevant tools may still fail to satisfy functional or contextual requirements after transfer. To address this gap, we propose \methodname{}, a progressive validation framework that complements semantic relevance with endpoint-grounded functional compatibility and task-conditioned contextual evidence. Across cross-domain and cross-dataset transfer, \methodname{} consistently improves capability ranking, with larger gains under functional or contextual ambiguity. Ablation results further confirm the complementary contributions of functional and contextual validation.
items.title_ko: 관련성에서 유효성까지: 기능 및 상황적 검증을 통한 Zero-Shot 도구 선택
items.summary_ko: 대규모 언어 모델(LLM) 에이전트는 점점 더 보이지 않는 도메인과 실행 컨텍스트의 작업에 직면하고 있으며, 작업 요구 사항을 충족할 수 있는 도구를 식별하기 위한 Zero-Shot 도구 선택이 필수적이다. 이 연구는 기존 방법이 의존하는 관련성 순위 지정의 한계를 지적하고, '전이 유효성 격차(transfer-validity gap)'를 식별한다.
items.why_ko: LLM 에이전트가 복잡하고 미지의 환경에서 도구를 선택하는 능력을 개선하여, AI 에이전트의 일반화 성능과 실용성을 높이는 데 중요한 기여를 한다.

items.title: Hypothesis Selection via Weighted Medians
items.body: Given $n$ distributions (hypotheses) $\mathcal H=\{H_1,\ldots,H_n\}$ and samples from an unknown target distribution $P$, proper hypothesis selection seeks a distribution whose total variation distance to $P$ is close to the best achievable within the known distributions. We give an algorithm that, using $O(\varepsilon^{-2}\log(n/δ))$ target samples, running in $O(n\varepsilon^{-2}\log(n/δ))$ time, with probability at least $1-δ$, returns $H_{\hat i}$ satisfying $d_\mathrm{TV}(P,H_{\hat i})\leq 3\min_{i\in[n]}d_\mathrm{TV}(P,H_i)+\varepsilon.$ The algorithm achieves the optimal approximation factor and sample complexity. The running time improves the dependence on the failure probability from polynomial to logarithmic in the state-of-the-art bound $\tilde{O}(n\varepsilon^{-2}δ^{-1})$ of Aamand, Aliakbarpour, Chen, and Silwal (COLT 2026), thereby answering their Question~2.
items.title_ko: 가중 중앙값을 이용한 가설 선택
items.summary_ko: 주어진 $n$개의 분포(가설)와 알려지지 않은 대상 분포 $P$로부터의 샘플이 있을 때, 적절한 가설 선택은 $P$와의 총 변동 거리(total variation distance)가 알려진 분포 내에서 가장 좋은 가설을 찾는 것을 목표로 한다. 이 연구는 $O(\varepsilon^{-2}\log(n/δ))$의 대상 샘플과 $O(n\varepsilon^{-2}\log(n/δ))$의 시간으로 이를 수행하는 알고리즘을 제시한다.
items.why_ko: 데이터로부터 최적의 가설을 효율적으로 선택하는 통계적 방법을 제시하며, 이는 모델 선택, 비정상 탐지 등 다양한 AI 및 머신러닝 응용 분야에서 활용될 수 있다.

items.title: From Triage to Impact: A Multi-Hop Reasoning Benchmark for Explainable Persian Hate Speech
items.body: Hate speech has become increasingly prevalent on social media, raising concerns about its detection, interpretation, and moderation. Persian, a relatively low-resource language, lacks sufficient annotated data and computational resources for fine-grained hate speech analysis. In this study, we introduce a fine-grained, multi-hop benchmark for explainable Persian hate speech analysis, covering content triage, target identification, hate tactic and moral foundation analysis, textual evidence extraction, harmful narrative inference, and severity assessment. By evaluating state-of-the-art large language models (LLMs), we find that performance generally declines as tasks require more fine-grained semantic and inferential reasoning. Proprietary models generally outperform open-weight models, while reasoning-oriented models show no consistent advantage. Incorporating intermediate reasoning steps substantially improves severity prediction compared with one-shot assessment. Our analysis further reveals that Incitement to Violence or Harm is most strongly associated with higher severity, while political-affiliation targets are particularly associated with subversion-based moral framing. Overall, this work provides insights into LLM-based hate speech analysis and supports more accountable moderation of Persian-language social media. The benchmark is publicly available at https://github.com/kalhorghazal/From-Triage-to-Impact.
items.title_ko: 분류에서 영향까지: 설명 가능한 페르시아어 혐오 발언을 위한 다중 홉 추론 벤치마크
items.summary_ko: 소셜 미디어에서 혐오 발언이 증가하고 있으며, 페르시아어는 자원 부족으로 미세한 분석이 어렵다. 이 연구는 콘텐츠 분류, 타겟 식별, 혐오 전술 및 도덕적 기반 분석, 텍스트 증거 추출을 포함하는 설명 가능한 페르시아어 혐오 발언을 위한 다중 홉 벤치마크를 소개한다.
items.why_ko: 자원 부족 언어인 페르시아어에 대한 혐오 발언 분석 및 설명 가능성 벤치마크를 제공하여, 다국어 혐오 발언 탐지 및 온라인 콘텐츠 조정 기술 발전에 기여한다.

items.title: ReAl: Refine neural operators via aligning dynamical flow
items.body: Neural partial differential equation (PDE) surrogates trained with mean squared error (MSE) can capture dominant dynamics but often lose high-frequency information and fine-scale structures. Generative models (e.g., Flow Matching) can capture the distribution of fine-scale details, yet stochastic errors may accumulate during autoregressive rollouts and compromise long-term stability. To address these limitations, we introduce Refine and Align(ReAl), a model-agnostic plug-in that augments pretrained PDE surrogates to improve the reconstruction of high-frequency structures associated with complex physical phenomena. In the refinement stage, a conditional flow-matching model learns the residual distribution around the deterministic base prediction, recovering missing fine-scale structures while retaining the dominant dynamics. In the alignment stage, to mitigate the generative discrepancies amplified in the autoregressive rollout, particularly in chaotic systems, we generate multiple trajectories from the same input and reinforce the refiner with trajectory-level rewards, thereby achieving long-horizon dynamical alignment. Experiments across diverse surrogate architectures and PDE tasks demonstrate that ReAl consistently improves high-frequency fidelity, forecasting accuracy, and long-horizon stability.
items.title_ko: ReAl: 동적 흐름 정렬을 통한 신경 연산자 개선
items.summary_ko: 평균 제곱 오차(MSE)로 훈련된 신경 편미분 방정식(PDE) 서러게이트는 지배적인 동역학을 포착하지만 고주파 정보와 미세 스케일 구조를 종종 손실한다. ReAl(Refine and Align)은 이러한 한계를 해결하기 위해 사전 훈련된 모델을 보강하는 모델 독립적 플러그인이다.
items.why_ko: PDE 시뮬레이션 및 과학적 모델링에서 AI 기반 서러게이트 모델의 정확성과 안정성을 높이는 방법을 제시하여, 복잡한 물리 시스템 예측의 신뢰도를 향상시킨다.

items.title: Cascaded Retrieval with Cross-Modal Query Refinement for Efficient Visual Document Search
items.body: Retrieving information from visually rich documents requires matching queries against pages that contain complex evidence in tables, figures, and layout-dependent structures. Current vision-language retrievers address this but incur query-time costs that grow with corpus size and are impractical to scale. We propose SCOUT, a cascaded two-track retrieval framework that separates retrieval performance from exhaustive search. The visual track first uses a lightweight parent retriever to filter the corpus to a compact candidate pool, then applies a stronger multi-vector reranker only to those candidates. In parallel, a semantic track retrieves over hierarchical page and document summaries generated offline to provide a signal complementary to visual matching. The outputs are fused through cross-modal query refinement, which uses semantic scores to adjust the visual query representation before final ranking. We evaluate SCOUT on 4 major benchmarks against 6 baselines and observe a significant query-time latency improvement up to 80.7x (28.8x on average) relative to the best baseline, while exceeding state-of-the-art retrieval performance by up to 7.8% NDCG across all benchmarks.
items.title_ko: 효율적인 시각 문서 검색을 위한 교차 모달 질의 개선을 통한 계단식 검색
items.summary_ko: 시각적으로 풍부한 문서에서 정보를 검색하는 것은 복잡한 증거를 포함하는 페이지에 대해 쿼리를 매칭하는 것을 필요로 한다. 이 연구는 검색 성능을 철저한 검색에서 분리하는 계단식 두 트랙 검색 프레임워크인 SCOUT를 제안한다.
items.why_ko: 복잡한 시각 문서를 효율적으로 검색하는 새로운 방법을 제시하여, 대규모 문서 아카이브나 디지털 라이브러리에서 필요한 정보를 빠르고 정확하게 찾아내는 데 기여한다.

items.title: Lexical Persistence Without Semantic Entrenchment in AI Agent Communities
items.body: AI agent communities sustain lexical persistence, popular terms spread, recur, and achieve broad adoption, but whether they also develop the temporal semantic structure characteristic of human linguistic communities remains open. We compare MoltBook (AI agent community, 8 weeks), PTT (Chinese human BBS, 19 years), and Reddit (English human forum, in matched 8-week windows) using Compass-Aligned Distributional Embeddings (CADE), measuring semantic drift (B1), neighborhood stability (B2), and lag-1 autocorrelation of per-word drift trajectories. Across the platforms, lag-1 autocorrelation forms a memory-horizon continuum. AI agents' result clusters at the low end, while human platforms show longer-range temporal dependence. MoltBook exhibits approximately 2$\times$ the B1 drift and 20-30% lower B2 stability than both human platforms. As a partial control for community age, r/vibecoding (founded 2025-02-08) shows significant ACF in its first 8 weeks ($0.082$, $p<.001$) and over 15 weeks ($0.220$, $p<.001$); MoltBook's ACF remains non-significant ($p = 0.41$), consistent with the gap not reducing to developmental stage alone. We interpret this pattern as evidence that lexical diffusion alone does not guarantee diachronic semantic consolidation. The findings are consistent with a contrast between communities whose semantic trajectories accumulate long-range interaction constraints and communities whose outputs are repeatedly regenerated from largely fixed pretrained distributions.
items.title_ko: AI 에이전트 커뮤니티의 어휘적 지속성과 의미론적 고착 부재
items.summary_ko: AI 에이전트 커뮤니티는 어휘적 지속성을 유지하지만, 인간 언어 공동체의 특징인 시간적 의미론적 구조를 개발하는지는 여전히 미지수다. 이 연구는 MoltBook(AI 에이전트), PTT(인간 BBS), Reddit(인간 포럼)을 CADE를 사용하여 비교한다.
items.why_ko: AI 에이전트가 생성하는 언어의 사회적 및 의미론적 특성을 이해하는 데 중요한 통찰을 제공하며, 이는 인간과 유사한 커뮤니케이션 능력을 가진 AI 개발에 필수적이다.

items.title: Fractional is Better: Learnable Derivative Orders in Neural Operator Learning
items.body: Neural operators learn mappings between function spaces, enabling fast surrogate solutions to partial differential equations. Despite remarkable architectural diversity, these methods often share a common input representation: raw coordinate-value pairs $(x, u(x))$. We ask whether inputs aligned with PDE differential structure can improve learning. Through Picard iteration on mild solutions, we show that derivatives of the input appear explicitly in the solution operator, suggesting that providing derivative features should reduce the network's implicit differentiation burden. We prove this intuition: providing derivative features improves approximation bounds from $O(W^{-(s-m)/d})$ to $O(W^{-s/d})$, where $W$ is parameter count, $s$ is input regularity, $m$ is the PDE order, and $d$ is spatial dimension. Our central finding, however, is a surprise: the optimal derivative order $β^*$ is strictly less than the PDE order $m$. This gap arises from a bias-variance tradeoff in spectral space that we characterize in closed form. Learning $β$ from data achieves automatic spectral regularization. We introduce $\partial$-NO (del-NO), for derivative-augmented neural operators, an architecture-agnostic augmentation that provides learnable fractional derivative features to any neural operator backbone. Across benchmark problems and architectures, $\partial$-NO consistently improves prediction accuracy, with learned orders that reflect a representation of known physics modulated by noise and finite-sample constraints.
items.title_ko: 분수 차수가 더 좋다: 신경 연산자 학습에서 학습 가능한 미분 차수
items.summary_ko: 신경 연산자는 함수 공간 간의 매핑을 학습하여 편미분 방정식에 대한 빠른 서러게이트 솔루션을 가능하게 한다. 이 연구는 PDE 미분 구조에 맞춰진 입력이 학습을 개선할 수 있는지 묻고, 분수 차수 미분 사용을 제안한다.
items.why_ko: 신경 연산자 학습의 입력 표현을 개선하여 PDE 풀이 모델의 정확성과 효율성을 높이는 새로운 방법을 제시하며, 이는 과학 컴퓨팅 및 물리 시뮬레이션 분야에 중요한 영향을 미칠 수 있다.

items.title: Do AI Agents Gossip? Evaluative Talk in Human and AI-Agent Online Communities
items.body: Gossip, defined as evaluative talk about absent third parties, is widely seen as a uniquely human social practice. This study examines whether comparable discourse emerges spontaneously in a community of autonomous AI agents. We compare Moltbook, a Reddit-style platform populated by AI agents, with PTT, a large human-operated bulletin board in Taiwan. To reduce differences attributable to communicative setting, we analyze two public, asynchronous forums using the same operational definition of gossip. Gossip occurs on Moltbook, but its prevalence is 2.6 to 6 times lower than on PTT, depending on the denominator used. On both platforms, gossip frequently targets locally prominent figures, tends to elicit agreement from the first respondent, and is rarely presented as unsupported rumor. The clearest difference concerns how subsequent responses develop. Among threads containing at least one codable reply, challenges occur in 65.1% of human threads but only 21.3% of agent threads. Moreover, following an early aligning response, consensus remains unchallenged in 83.6% of agent threads, compared with 44.7% of human threads. This thread-level contrast remains after controlling for thread depth and board composition and under recalibration against two human annotators. Estimates based on individual reply turns are less robust and are therefore reported as bounds. These findings suggest that AI-agent communities reproduce the informational dimension of gossip, while the extent to which gossip performs comparable relational functions remains unresolved.
items.title_ko: AI 에이전트도 험담을 하는가? 인간 및 AI 에이전트 온라인 커뮤니티의 평가적 대화
items.summary_ko: 부재하는 제3자에 대한 평가적 대화로 정의되는 험담은 널리 인간 고유의 사회적 행동으로 간주된다. 이 연구는 자율 AI 에이전트 커뮤니티에서 유사한 담론이 자발적으로 발생하는지 조사한다.
items.why_ko: AI 에이전트가 인간의 복잡한 사회적 행동, 특히 '험담'과 같은 평가적 대화를 모방하거나 생성할 수 있는지 탐구하여, AI의 사회적 지능과 복잡한 상호작용 능력에 대한 이해를 넓힌다.

items.title: Beyond Expert Rankings: Contrast Calibration for Mixed-Precision MoE Quantization
items.body: Mixture-of-experts (MoE) language models activate only a few experts per token, yet all expert weights must be stored. Mixed-precision quantization reduces this storage cost by assigning higher bit-widths to sensitive experts and lower bit-widths to resilient ones, but expert rankings alone do not determine how strongly to weight their errors. To address this gap, we propose NatScale, a contrast-calibrated allocation framework for mixed-precision MoE quantization. It uses a model-specific power transformation to calibrate gradient-based expert weights to an information-theoretic contrast target while preserving rankings. We jointly evaluate each expert's gate, up and down configurations to estimate its output error. We then combine these errors and calibrated weights with an existing prior based on weight spectra, variance and precision decay to select configurations under a storage budget. Across three models, NatScale achieves the lowest native-to-quantized KL divergence and the highest top-token agreement in all nine settings against five allocation baselines. It also yields the lowest perplexity in seven settings. These findings highlight the importance of objective-aware precision allocation.
items.title_ko: 전문가 순위를 넘어: 혼합 정밀 MoE 양자화를 위한 대비 보정
items.summary_ko: MoE(Mixture-of-experts) 언어 모델은 토큰당 소수의 전문가만 활성화하지만, 모든 전문가 가중치를 저장해야 한다. 혼합 정밀 양자화는 민감한 전문가에게 더 높은 비트 폭을, 탄력적인 전문가에게는 더 낮은 비트 폭을 할당하여 저장 비용을 줄인다. NatScale은 이러한 격차를 해결하기 위한 대비 보정된 할당 프레임워크이다.
items.why_ko: MoE 모델의 메모리 효율성과 추론 속도를 향상시키는 효과적인 양자화 방법을 제시하여, 대규모 LLM을 더 적은 자원으로 배포하고 운영할 수 있게 한다.

items.title: Human Demonstrations as Post-Training Data for Any Robot Body: Retargeting the Object, Not the Hand
items.body: Human demonstrations are today used largely for pretraining vision-language-action models, with little ability to use the same data for target-embodiment or task-oriented training, which scalable deployment of robots in industrial and general environments depends on. A human demonstration recorded on a simple and scalable device such as a mobile phone can serve as post-training data for a robot whose body differs in structure and capability from the human who recorded it. This is made possible not by retargeting the hand's motion but the object's. A capture yields a body-free record: the object's pose over time, its contact intervals, and a reconstructed 3D object with provenance. Any robot, given as a URDF and a short descriptor, is solved against that record and scored in simulation against the demonstrated object motion as ground truth: the human-to-simulation leg of human-to-simulation-to-robot transfer, measured per robot. Each (robot, episode) pair gets one outcome: pass, failure with a named mode, or refusal, with its reason, before any motion. The method runs as a working system over a growing collection; the set analysed here is a sample of it: 42 captures solved on 8 robots, 157 pairs, of which 31.2% pass, 52.2% fail, 14.0% are refused and 2.5% are unauditable (kinematic feasibility, +/-50 mm / +/-15 deg, in simulation). Refusals held up: every pair the checks refuse on stored evidence yet ran anyway failed (13 of 13; 5 on a body whose public model welds its hand). A description file could not be shown to screen a robot: its outcomes were barely more predictable than guessing. No policy has yet been trained on the record. The record decides what a robot may post-train on; whether the policy then works on the real robot is the simulation-to-robot question, answered downstream.
items.body_ko: 인간의 시연은 오늘날 주로 비전-언어-액션 모델의 사전 훈련에 사용되며, 대상 구현 또는 작업 지향 훈련을 위해 동일한 데이터를 사용할 수 있는 능력이 거의 없습니다. 이는 산업 및 일반 환경에서 로봇의 확장 가능한 배포에 달려 있습니다. 휴대폰과 같은 간단하고 확장 가능한 장치에 기록된 인간 시연은 신체 구조와 기능이 기록한 인간과 다른 로봇의 후처리 데이터로 사용될 수 있습니다. 이는 손의 움직임을 재타겟팅하는 것이 아니라 객체의 움직임을 재타겟팅함으로써 가능해집니다. 캡처는 몸체 없는 기록을 생성합니다. 즉, 시간 경과에 따른 객체의 포즈, 접촉 간격, 그리고 출처가 있는 재구성된 3D 객체입니다. URDF 및 짧은 설명자로 주어진 모든 로봇은 해당 기록에 대해 해결되고, 시연된 객체 모션을 진실(ground truth)로 사용하여 시뮬레이션에서 점수가 매겨집니다. 즉, 인간-시뮬레이션-로봇 전송의 인간-시뮬레이션 부분이며, 로봇당 측정됩니다. 각 (로봇, 에피소드) 쌍은 동작 전에 통과, 명명된 모드에서의 실패 또는 거부와 그 이유 중 하나의 결과를 얻습니다. 이 방법은 성장하는 컬렉션에서 작동하는 시스템으로 실행됩니다. 여기에서 분석된 세트는 그 샘플입니다. 8개의 로봇에서 42개의 캡처가 해결되었으며, 157쌍 중 31.2%가 통과하고, 52.2%가 실패하며, 14.0%가 거부되고, 2.5%는 감사 불가능합니다(시뮬레이션에서 운동학적 타당성, +/-50mm / +/-15도). 거부는 유지되었습니다. 검사가 저장된 증거를 기반으로 거부했지만 어쨌든 실행된 모든 쌍은 실패했습니다(13개 중 13개, 5개는 공개 모델이 손을 용접하는 몸체에서). 설명 파일은 로봇을 선별하는 데 사용될 수 없었습니다. 그 결과는 추측하는 것보다 예측 가능성이 거의 없었습니다. 아직 기록에 대한 정책이 훈련되지 않았습니다. 기록은 로봇이 무엇을 후처리할지 결정합니다. 정책이 실제 로봇에서 작동하는지 여부는 시뮬레이션-로봇 질문이며, 하류에서 답변됩니다.
items.title_ko: 어떤 로봇 바디에도 적용 가능한 인간 데모 기반 후처리 훈련 데이터: 손이 아닌 객체를 재타겟팅
items.summary_ko: 인간 데모는 주로 비전-언어-액션 모델의 사전 훈련에 사용되지만, 대상 로봇이나 작업 지향 훈련에는 활용도가 낮다. 이 연구는 휴대폰으로 기록된 인간 데모가 로봇의 신체 구조나 능력과 무관하게 후처리 훈련 데이터로 사용될 수 있는 방법을 제시한다. 이는 객체의 동작을 재타겟팅함으로써 가능해진다.
items.why_ko: 로봇 학습을 위한 인간 데모 데이터의 활용성을 혁신적으로 확장하여, 다양한 로봇 시스템에 대한 빠르고 효율적인 훈련을 가능하게 한다. 이는 로봇 공학 개발자들이 실세계 로봇을 더 쉽게 프로그래밍하고 배포하는 데 매우 중요한 실무적 기여를 한다.

items.title: Lifted State Policy Optimization: Internalizing Self-Correction through Transition Geometry
items.body: Preference optimization ranks final answers and trajectory RL maximizes aggregate returns, yet neither credits the local change that turns a flawed reasoning state into a better one. We introduce Lifted State Policy Optimization (LSPO), which establishes this finite, cost-adjusted transition as the primary unit of learning. Each textual answer is augmented with a learned continuous coordinate, forming a lifted state that an energy function evaluates and orders. A shaped reward drives energy descent net of edit and step costs, and an internalization loss absorbs selected low-energy answers into the direct generator. On Qwen3.5-27B, the resulting single-pass policy reaches 71.8% aggregate accuracy across mathematics, science, code, and logic benchmarks, matching test-time reflection at 71.9% with 28% lower latency and 25.8% fewer tokens. The pattern holds across dense and mixture-of-experts backbones, and matched controls confirm that transition credit and the lifted coordinate each contribute, as does answer internalization. Our code is available at https://github.com/Venomrko/lspo.
items.title_ko: Lifted State Policy Optimization: 전이 기하학을 통한 자기 수정 내재화
items.summary_ko: 선호도 최적화는 최종 답변의 순위를 매기고 궤적 RL은 총합 보상을 최대화하지만, 둘 다 결함 있는 추론 상태를 더 나은 상태로 바꾸는 국부적 변화에 대한 크레딧을 부여하지 않는다. Lifted State Policy Optimization(LSPO)은 이러한 유한하고 비용 조정된 전이를 학습의 주요 단위로 설정한다.
items.why_ko: LLM의 추론 과정에서 발생하는 미세한 개선 단계에 보상을 부여하여, 모델이 스스로 오류를 수정하고 더 효율적인 추론 경로를 학습하도록 돕는 정교한 강화 학습 방법을 제시한다.

items.title: NeuroDETR: Multiscale Discrete Spatiotemporal Tokenization for Asynchronous EEG Event Detection
items.body: Asynchronous EEG event detection supports practical brain-computer interfaces by identifying event classes and temporal boundaries directly from continuous recordings without predefined event boundaries at inference time. The primary challenge lies in extracting event-related patterns embedded in ongoing background activity. To address this, we propose \textbf{NeuroDETR}, a discrete spatiotemporal multiscale framework that combines structured tokenization with event-aware feature refinement. Multiscale temporal codebooks capture brief responses and sustained dynamics, while Spatial-Pyramid VQ hierarchically encodes spatial structure across EEG channels. These complementary representations form a compact event memory for jointly classifying events and estimating their onsets and offsets. Before tokenization, we apply FOCAL, an event-aware sparse attention module that uses predicted event presence to guide temporal feature refinement and spatial aggregation, emphasizing likely event periods while preserving context across the recording. Experiments on eight EEG datasets that span diverse paradigms demonstrate state-of-the-art performance. These findings provide a basis for the development of BCI systems that recognize meaningful neural activity during continuous interaction and monitoring.
items.title_ko: NeuroDETR: 비동기 EEG 이벤트 탐지를 위한 멀티스케일 이산 시공간 토큰화
items.summary_ko: 비동기 EEG 이벤트 탐지는 추론 시 사전 정의된 이벤트 경계 없이 연속적인 기록에서 이벤트 클래스와 시간적 경계를 식별함으로써 실용적인 뇌-컴퓨터 인터페이스를 지원한다. NeuroDETR은 이 문제를 해결하기 위해 구조화된 토큰화와 이벤트 인식 특징 정제를 결합한 멀티스케일 프레임워크를 제안한다.
items.why_ko: 뇌-컴퓨터 인터페이스(BCI) 분야에서 EEG 신호로부터 이벤트를 정확하게 탐지하는 기술을 발전시켜, 의료 진단, 신경 과학 연구 및 새로운 인터페이스 개발에 기여할 수 있다.

items.title: Non-asymptotic Convergence of Average-reward Q-learning with Options
items.body: We study the finite-sample convergence of Q-learning algorithms for the average-reward formulation of Reinforcement Learning (RL) with options. While options allow temporarily extended and hierarchical actions, the average-reward formulation incorporates continual tasks beyond discounted and episodic RL. We establish the first $\tilde{O}(1/\text{iterations})$ convergence guarantees, in the mean-square sense, for average-reward option Q-learning algorithms in both the inter- and intra-option settings. First, we prove that both inter- and intra-option Bellman operators satisfy multi-step span contractions under unichain assumptions. Then, we propose synchronous estimators of these multi-step option Bellman operators leading to two variants of option Q-learning. Finally, we extend the stochastic approximation framework to prove convergence rates of these two algorithms under the minimal assumptions used in the literature.
items.title_ko: 옵션을 포함한 평균 보상 Q-학습의 비점근적 수렴
items.summary_ko: 이 연구는 옵션을 포함한 평균 보상 강화 학습(RL)에 대한 Q-학습 알고리즘의 유한 샘플 수렴을 연구한다. 옵션은 시간적으로 확장된 계층적 액션을 허용하며, 평균 보상 공식화는 할인되거나 에피소드 RL을 넘어 지속적인 작업을 통합한다.
items.why_ko: 옵션과 평균 보상 프레임워크를 결합한 Q-학습의 수렴 이론을 확립하여, 계층적 강화 학습 및 장기 지속형 작업에 대한 AI 에이전트 학습의 안정성과 효율성을 높이는 데 기여한다.

items.title: Doc2Harness: Benchmarking LLMs on Long-Horizon Harness Engineering of Coding Agents
items.body: Agents driven by large language models are increasingly deployed on long-horizon tasks, where they use tools and modify real workspaces. How well they perform depends as much on the harness around the model as on the model itself. Existing benchmarks measure downstream task success under a fixed harness, leaving harness engineering itself unexplored. We propose Doc2Harness, a two-stage benchmark that evaluates long-horizon harness engineering directly. In Stage 1, a build model operating inside a fixed builder harness receives an interface-only contract skeleton and a development document that consolidates behavior across twelve frontier harnesses, and then constructs a complete candidate harness in an isolated container. In Stage 2, the frozen candidate harness runs in containers separate from the construction environment, one per test case, and is driven end to end by a scripted mock model. We score each test case using four observable channels, namely the requests sent to the model, the files on disk, the process exit code, and the command output; positive controls rule out vacuous passes. Across nineteen frontier models, each evaluated with three independent builds on 328 test cases, GPT-6 Astra achieves the highest pass rate at 53.05%, while the weakest model reaches 27.44%, a gap of roughly twenty-six percentage points. Even the strongest model fails nearly half of the test cases, and failures cluster around how cross-cutting functionality is split across modules. To our knowledge, Doc2Harness provides the first deterministic benchmark for measuring long-horizon harness engineering.
items.title_ko: Doc2Harness: 코딩 에이전트의 장기 하네스 엔지니어링 벤치마킹
items.summary_ko: 대규모 언어 모델(LLM)에 의해 구동되는 에이전트는 점점 더 장기 작업에 배포되고 있으며, 그 성능은 모델 자체만큼이나 모델 주변의 '하네스'에 달려 있다. Doc2Harness는 장기 하네스 엔지니어링을 직접 평가하는 2단계 벤치마크를 제안한다.
items.why_ko: LLM 기반 코딩 에이전트의 실제 성능에 큰 영향을 미치는 '하네스 엔지니어링'이라는 중요한 요소를 벤치마킹하여, 개발자들이 견고하고 효율적인 AI 코딩 에이전트를 구축하는 데 필요한 실질적인 평가 기준을 제공한다.

items.title: When Does Task-Aware Imputation Matter? An Analysis of Robustness Under Train-Test Mismatch
items.body:
Missing data is a pervasive challenge in machine learning, often degrading predictive performance and complicating model deployment. Most existing approaches treat imputation as a preprocessing step independent of the downstream task, a separation that becomes problematic under train-test mismatches in missingness mechanisms or rates. We introduce a unified framework that treats missing entries as variables in a task-conditioned optimization problem. We instantiate this framework in two settings: an amortized approach for scenarios with missing data at both training and test time, and a latent optimization approach for settings where only training data is incomplete.
The evaluation is conducted on 98 tabular datasets, and robustness under train-test mismatches is assessed on 36 datasets. Results reveal that reconstruction error constitutes a poor proxy for predictive utility (Spearman rho approximately 0.16 to 0.32), and that task-aware imputation becomes critical in scenarios where classical methods fail to recover complete-data performance, achieving win rates of up to 80% in challenging train-test mismatch scenarios.
items.title_ko: 작업 인식 귀납이 언제 중요한가? 훈련-테스트 불일치 하에서의 강건성 분석
items.summary_ko: 결측 데이터는 머신러닝에서 흔한 문제로 예측 성능을 저하시키고 모델 배포를 복잡하게 만든다. 대부분의 기존 접근 방식은 귀납을 다운스트림 작업과 독립적인 전처리 단계로 취급하지만, 훈련-테스트 불일치 시 문제가 된다. 이 연구는 결측 항목을 작업 조건부 최적화 문제의 변수로 다루는 통합 프레임워크를 소개한다.
items.why_ko: 결측 데이터 처리 문제를 다운스트림 작업과 연동하여 해결하는 새로운 프레임워크를 제시하며, 이는 실제 환경에서 데이터 불완전성으로 인한 AI 모델의 강건성 저하 문제를 개선하는 데 기여한다.

items.title: Training Dynamics of Transformers on Unbounded Inputs: Attention Learning Can Lag Output Layer Learning
items.body: The success of transformers is attributed to several factors, including their capacity to express formal languages over variable-length inputs, and ability of the attention mechanism to focus on relevant input features. However, there is limited understanding of the training dynamics of shallow transformers, specifically how to decouple the learning of the attention and the output (feedforward) layer. A natural extension of the theory of one-step gradient feature learning in feedforward networks suggests that one could first learn the attention weights with a single gradient step, and then train the output layer. We show that this fails for a shallow transformer trained to recognize a star-free language from unbounded-length input. We prove that the transformer can be trained to recognize the language with a three-phase gradient descent: the output layer is updated first, followed by an attention update, and the output layer is fine-tuned in the third phase. In contrast, the language cannot be learned by training only the attention or output layer, or by a single attention-layer update followed by finetuning the output layer. We empirically show that ``attention learning lagging output layer learning" is beneficial in other language recognition, regression, and in-context learning tasks as well.
items.title_ko: 무한 입력에 대한 트랜스포머 훈련 동역학: 어텐션 학습이 출력 계층 학습보다 느릴 수 있다
items.summary_ko: 트랜스포머의 성공은 가변 길이 입력에 대한 형식 언어 표현 능력과 어텐션 메커니즘에 기인한다. 그러나 얕은 트랜스포머의 훈련 동역학, 특히 어텐션 학습과 출력(피드포워드) 계층 학습을 분리하는 방법에 대한 이해는 제한적이다.
items.why_ko: 트랜스포머 모델의 핵심 메커니즘인 어텐션과 출력 계층의 학습 동역학을 분석하여, 모델의 훈련 과정을 더 깊이 이해하고 최적화하는 데 필요한 이론적 기반을 제공한다.

items.title: Read, Parse, Describe: Unified Document Parsing with Visual Element Description Generation
items.body: Document understanding systems are typically evaluated as separate components via layout analysis, optical text recognition, reading-order prediction, and image captioning. This separation leaves scientific figures, captions, and visual semantics weakly connected, and fails to measure whether a model can produce a single page-level parse that is both structurally faithful and semantically accessible. We introduce Read-Parse-Describe, a unified dataset for document parsing with visual element description generation. Given a page image, models are required to output an ordered list of layout elements containing bounding boxes, semantic labels, reading-order indices, recognized textual content, and alternative text descriptions for visual elements. The benchmark is built from 2,402 documents, comprising 18,163 continuous pages, 125,218 layout elements, and 11,338 visual instances. Besides, we further propose a plug-and-play space-awareness enhancer that reuses multi-layer visual features and injects grid-aware spatial guidance into vision-language tokens for layout-aware generation. Experiments across end-to-end VLMs and pipeline parsers show that existing systems still struggle to jointly recover reading order and visual semantics, while our enhanced model achieves strong joint performance.
