These results highlight the need to move beyond isolated document parsing modules toward unified models that jointly read, parse, and describe complex documents. The new dataset and code will be made publicly available at https://github.com/yufanchen96/RPD
items.title_ko: 읽기, 파싱, 설명: 시각적 요소 설명 생성을 통한 통합 문서 파싱
items.summary_ko: 문서 이해 시스템은 일반적으로 레이아웃 분석, 광학 텍스트 인식, 읽기 순서 예측, 이미지 캡셔닝 등 별도의 구성 요소로 평가된다. 이 연구는 구조적으로 충실하고 의미론적으로 접근 가능한 단일 페이지 수준 파싱을 생성하는 모델을 측정하기 위한 통합 데이터셋 Read-Parse-Describe를 소개한다.
items.why_ko: 문서 이해 시스템의 여러 구성 요소를 통합하여 평가하고 개발하는 새로운 방법을 제시하며, 이는 과학 논문, 보고서 등 복잡한 시각적 문서로부터 AI가 더 완벽하게 정보를 추출하고 이해하는 데 기여한다.

items.title: TreeFlex: Agents Navigating Their Own Search Trees
items.body: A ReAct-style agent accumulates observations, intermediate results, and failed attempts in a single context. As this context grows, stale and off-path information consumes its limited capacity and obscures relevant evidence, making focused reasoning increasingly difficult. We introduce TreeFlex, a framework in which the agent's own policy decides where to search. The agent records each intermediate state, with a short summary, as a node in a search tree maintained by the harness. The policy is a single language model that acts in two roles. In the Reflection role, it has a global view of the tree through these summaries and picks a node to resume, together with an instruction. In the Execution role, the harness restores the path that led to that node, and the model carries out the instruction with the usual task tools until it saves a new node or proposes a solution, which Reflection then approves or sends back to another node. Through these choices, the policy decides whether to deepen the current line, branch from or revisit an earlier state, verify a proposal, or stop, without a fixed traversal order or a score for each node. We train navigation, task actions, checkpointing, and proposal review jointly with a tree-aware adaptation of GRPO, using task-level outcome rewards augmented by process rewards. After small-scale RL of a 4B model, with the same active-context limit for all methods, TreeFlex reaches 48.8% accuracy on a challenging deep-research benchmark, versus 41.5% for flat ReAct and 42.8% for FoldAgent, and its Pass@8 is about ten points higher than either. On SWE-bench Verified, with all three systems trained with RL from the same 9B model, TreeFlex resolves 54.9% of tasks, versus 43.3% for FoldAgent and 45.2% for its step-wise variant.
items.title_ko: TreeFlex: 자체 검색 트리를 탐색하는 에이전트
items.summary_ko: ReAct 스타일 에이전트는 관찰, 중간 결과, 실패 시도를 단일 컨텍스트에 축적한다. 이 컨텍스트가 커지면 오래되고 비경로 정보가 제한된 용량을 소모하고 관련 증거를 가려 추론을 어렵게 만든다. TreeFlex는 에이전트의 정책이 어디를 검색할지 결정하는 프레임워크를 소개한다.
items.why_ko: LLM 에이전트의 장기 계획 및 추론 과정에서 컨텍스트 관리 문제를 효율적으로 해결하는 새로운 방법을 제시하여, 에이전트의 복잡한 문제 해결 능력과 자율성을 크게 향상시킬 수 있다.

items.title: Are We Overthinking One-Step Generation?
items.body: Diffusion and flow matching are now dominant frameworks for generative modeling in continuous domains, but they typically require multiple network evaluations at inference. This has motivated extensive research on one-step generative modeling primarily built on diffusion and flow, though existing approaches often rely on complex training machinery. In this work, we introduce Priming Models, a simple two-stage framework for training one-step generators. Motivated by the difficulty of distributional training from scratch, Priming Models are first trained on a reconstruction objective, e.g., pixel-space denoising at a fixed noise level, before undergoing feature-space distributional post-training. Our central scientific finding is that this simple reconstruction stage is already enough to entirely alleviate the difficulty of distributional training. Empirically, across class-conditional image generation, text-to-image generation, and world modeling, Priming Models significantly advance the Pareto frontier of training compute vs. generation quality. On ImageNet at $256 \times 256$ resolution, we achieve a state-of-the-art FID of $1.19$ among one-step generators using approximately one-tenth the training compute of prior methods with comparable FID. We open-source our codebase at https://github.com/JaeyeonKim01/priming.
items.title_ko: 우리는 One-Step 생성에 대해 과도하게 생각하는가?
items.summary_ko: 확산 및 흐름 매칭은 이제 연속 도메인에서 생성 모델링을 위한 지배적인 프레임워크지만, 일반적으로 추론 시 여러 네트워크 평가가 필요하다. 이 연구는 Priming Models라는 간단한 2단계 프레임워크를 소개하여 One-Step 생성기의 훈련 복잡성을 줄인다.
items.why_ko: 생성형 모델의 추론 효율성을 높이는 'One-Step 생성'을 더 단순하고 효과적으로 훈련하는 방법을 제시하며, 이는 실시간 생성 AI 애플리케이션의 개발 및 배포를 용이하게 할 수 있다.

items.title: Argument Graph Uncertainty: Quantifying Uncertainty from the Logical Structure of Reasoning Chains
items.body: Reliable uncertainty estimation is essential for deploying large language models in high-stakes reasoning tasks, yet most existing approaches rely on expensive sampling strategies or shallow token-level signals that ignore the internal logical structure of model outputs. We introduce Argument Graph Uncertainty, a post-hoc framework for multiple choice question tasks, that estimates model confidence directly from the logical structure of a single chain-of-thought reasoning trace. Our method uses either a lightweight instruction-tuned model or a simple deterministic rule to segment the reasoning chain into propositional units, then applies a NLI model to infer relational edges and construct two complementary argument graphs over these segments. The resulting edge scores are aggregated into a Dirichlet posterior over answer options, whose concentration yields calibrated uncertainty estimates reflecting both local step-to-step coherence and global logical consistency across the reasoning trace. Evaluated on GPQA, MMLU-Pro and TruthfulQA, our method consistently surpasses token-based and consistency-based uncertainty baselines across multiple reasoning models. We further demonstrate through extensive combination analyses that argument graph uncertainty captures an orthogonal signal to existing approaches, making it a complementary component in uncertainty ensembles. Crucially, our framework requires no additional calls to the evaluated model and relies entirely on small, efficient auxiliary models, producing fully interpretable, per-node uncertainty attributions at low computational cost.
items.title_ko: 주장 그래프 불확실성: 추론 사슬의 논리적 구조로부터 불확실성 정량화
items.summary_ko: 고위험 추론 작업에서 대규모 언어 모델을 배포하기 위해서는 신뢰할 수 있는 불확실성 추정이 필수적이다. 이 연구는 단일 사고 사슬(chain-of-thought) 추론 추적의 논리적 구조로부터 직접 모델 신뢰도를 추정하는 사후 프레임워크 Argument Graph Uncertainty를 소개한다.
items.why_ko: LLM의 추론 결과에 대한 신뢰도(불확실성)를 논리적 구조 분석을 통해 효율적으로 정량화하는 방법을 제시하여, 고위험 AI 애플리케이션의 의사결정 신뢰성과 투명성을 향상시킨다.

items.title: Anuvani-Diarization: Zero Shot Speaker Diarization and Annotation Conventions Across 22 Languages
items.body: India's 22 scheduled languages are spoken by over a billion people in conversations that mix languages, often within one turn, overlap freely, and take place over telephones, in meetings, and in media. Knowing who spoke when, the task of speaker diarization, is essential to speech applications for such conversation: voice agents conversing with several people at once, speaker attributed transcription of meetings and calls, contact center analytics, and media monitoring. We present a systematic study of speaker diarization across all 22 languages on IndicDiarBench and introduce Anuvani-Diarization, which adapts a self-supervised end-to-end segmentation model to Indian conversation with uncertainty aware silver supervision. Evaluated zero shot alongside nine recent diarization systems, it reaches a duration weighted diarization error rate (DER) of 16.78% on all 1,164 recordings, the lowest of all systems we ran and second only to the best published result (16.0%), and leads the three strongest rivals in 14 of 22 languages. It matches its parent on six international benchmarks. We also show that the benchmark's utterance level annotation convention is a hidden variable worth 1.9 to 4.1 DER points, depending on the system, and that a convention learned from other Indian transcriptions does not transfer.
items.title_ko: 22개 인도 언어에 대한 제로샷 화자 분리 및 어노테이션 컨벤션
items.summary_ko: 이 연구는 인도 22개 언어의 혼합 및 오버랩이 흔한 대화에서 화자 분리(누가 언제 말했는지 식별)의 중요성을 강조합니다. 이를 위한 체계적인 접근 방식을 제시하며, 음성 응용 프로그램에 필수적인 역할을 합니다.
items.why_ko: 다국어 환경에서 음성 인식 및 처리 시스템의 정확성을 높이는 데 기여하며, 특히 저자원 언어에 대한 기술 발전에 도움이 됩니다.

items.title: Comparative Evaluation of Deep-Learning based DoA Estimators for Real-Time ISAC Beamforming
items.body: Integrated Sensing and Communication (ISAC) systems rely on accurate Direction-of-Arrival (DoA) estimation for effective beamforming and spectral-efficiency enhancement. While numerous classical and deep-learning-based DoA estimation methods have been reported in the literature, their suitability for real-time ISAC operation remains insufficiently understood because practical deployment requires consideration of both estimation accuracy and computational latency. This paper presents a unified evaluation framework for systematically comparing classical and learning-based DoA estimators within an ISAC beamforming pipeline. Representative classical and learning-based DoA estimators, together with an ensemble architecture, are integrated with Singular Value Decomposition (SVD)-based beamforming and evaluated under identical operating conditions. The impact of DoA estimation accuracy, inference latency, beamforming-weight generation time, and resulting effective spectral efficiency is investigated. Results show that different estimators occupy distinct operating points in the accuracy-latency-performance design space. Although learning-based approaches substantially reduce estimation time compared with MUSIC, the overall processing latency increasingly becomes dominated by the computational cost of SVD-based beamforming. Among the evaluated methods, the Regression Convolutional Neural Network (RCNN) exhibits a favorable balance between estimation accuracy, computational efficiency, and beamforming performance, making it a promising candidate for real-time ISAC deployment. The findings further suggest that future low-latency ISAC systems may benefit from beamforming strategies that reduce or avoid computationally intensive SVD-based beamforming-weight generation.
items.title_ko: 실시간 ISAC 빔포밍을 위한 딥러닝 기반 DoA 추정기 비교 평가
items.summary_ko: 통합 감지 및 통신(ISAC) 시스템에서 효과적인 빔포밍을 위한 심층 학습 기반 DoA(Direction-of-Arrival) 추정 방법들을 비교 평가합니다. 실시간 ISAC 작동에 적합한 추정 정확도와 계산 지연 시간 모두를 고려하여 분석합니다.
items.why_ko: ISAC 시스템의 실시간 성능 향상을 위한 DoA 추정 기술 선택에 중요한 가이드를 제공하며, 저지연 빔포밍 기술 개발에 도움이 됩니다.

items.title: Beyond Static Cues: Unified Dynamic Detection of MLLM Backdoors via Dual-Flow Trajectory Analysis
items.body: Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) are increasingly deployed in safety-critical domains, yet their susceptibility to backdoor attacks remains a formidable challenge. While existing defenses have evolved from visual-centric patch cues to unsupervised internal attention statistics, they are fundamentally constrained by a reliance on static snapshots and attack-specific heuristics. Given the intricate interplay between dual modalities, the vast design space for multimodal triggers allows diverse threats, such as textual injections, sub-perceptual noises, and coordinated cross-modal triggers, to easily circumvent such rigid priors, particularly when attack types are unknown in real-world applications. In this paper, we rethink backdoor detection by shifting the diagnostic paradigm from static observations to dynamic output evolution. We observe that a successful attack inevitably hijacks the model's decoding trajectory, skewing internal modal contributions during generation while maintaining an abnormal output invariance despite input perturbations. To capture this behavior, we propose EVO-Detect, a unified detection framework that monitors the dynamic evolution of internal signals during early decoding steps through two complementary channels: Attention Flow and Logits Flow. The attention branch measures how image-text attention allocation evolves during early generation, whereas the logits branch quantifies the sensitivity of the output distribution to modal perturbations through interventional ablations. We then convert these trajectories into compact sample-level metrics and normalize them against negative-control signatures so that natural perturbations are less likely to be mistaken for backdoor evidence. Extensive evaluations show that our approach substantially outperforms state-of-the-art baselines such as BYE and TCAP across diverse attack families.
items.title_ko: 듀얼-플로우 궤적 분석을 통한 MLLM 백도어의 통합 동적 감지
items.summary_ko: 멀티모달 대규모 언어 모델(MLLM)의 백도어 공격에 대한 취약성을 해결하기 위해 정적 단서에만 의존하는 기존 방어 메커니즘의 한계를 지적합니다. 듀얼-플로우 궤적 분석을 통해 동적으로 백도어를 감지하는 새로운 방법을 제안합니다.
items.why_ko: MLLM의 보안 취약점을 해결하고 안전한 AI 시스템 구축에 기여하며, 특히 실시간 백도어 공격 방어 기술 발전에 중요합니다.

items.title: Efficient Test-Time Adaptation For Robot Policies
items.body: Reinforcement-learning policies for robot locomotion can fail at deployment when operating conditions shift (e.g., rough or slippery terrain, payload changes, sensing degradation), and retraining or manual recalibration is often infeasible under on-device latency and memory constraints. We study test-time adaptation (TTA) for robotic control: adapting a pretrained policy online and in a self-supervised manner during execution, without access to rewards. Our starting point is a lightweight baseline that updates only the actor using a frozen pretrained critic as a deployment-time performance surrogate. Building on this, we introduce TEMPO, a test-time entropy-regularized, memory-guided policy optimization method that stabilizes critic-driven updates under severe shift. TEMPO combines (i) an entropy-promoting regularizer on the critic's predictive distribution to mitigate overconfident extrapolation, and (ii) a score-based memory, inspired by prioritized replay, that prioritizes low-value ("hard") observations and applies importance sampling to focus limited computation on the most informative deployment conditions. Across Go1, Go2, and G1 in MuJoCo Playground under four representative shifts and multiple architectures, TEMPO yields consistent gains, reaching up to 80% improvement in a single-device setting. We further validate on a physical Unitree Go2 with an added calf payload, where fully on-device adaptation improves performance over the non-adapted baseline across real-world episodes.
items.title_ko: 로봇 정책을 위한 효율적인 테스트-시간 적응 (TTA) 연구
items.summary_ko: 로봇 정책이 배포 시 작동 조건(예: 거친 지형, 페이로드 변경) 변화로 인해 실패할 수 있는 문제를 다룹니다. 온라인에서 사전 훈련된 정책을 보상 없이 자율적으로 적응시키는 테스트-시간 적응(TTA) 방법을 연구합니다.
items.why_ko: 로봇이 예측 불가능한 환경에서 더 견고하고 유연하게 작동할 수 있도록 돕는 실용적인 적응 기술을 개발하는 데 기여합니다.

items.title: Reflect After Failure: Brain-Inspired Self-Evolving Agents for Embodied Spatial Intelligence
items.body: Vision-Language Models (VLMs) have made substantial progress in spatial reasoning, and self-evolving agents further extend these capabilities to embodied environments by learning from interactions. However, current self-evolution remains particularly challenging in embodied spatial tasks, complex and multi-step decisions from partial visual evidence making it difficult to determine why an execution fails. The failure may stem from misperception, insufficient exploration, or incorrect planning, yet execution feedback alone rarely reveals which component is responsible. As a result, simply accumulating interaction experience can reinforce ineffective strategies. To address this, we propose HiMeco, a brain-inspired self-evolving agent for embodied spatial intelligence, inspired by metacognitive monitoring and hippocampal memory consolidation. Through Hippocampal-Metacognitive Reflection, HiMeco diagnoses failures in perception-exploration-planning (PEP), then compares execution attempts to derive reusable strategies and guidance for avoiding recurring errors. It also abstracts interaction programs into parameterized skills, using evidence contracts and execution-based validation to determine their retention and reuse. These strategies and skills guide subsequent interactions, with memory updated only between rounds and model parameters kept frozen. HiMeco achieves state-of-the-art performance on ESI-Bench, and it also improves accuracy on EmbSpatial-Bench by 3.94 percentage points without evolution.
items.body_ko: VLM(Vision-Language Models)은 공간 추론에서 상당한 발전을 이루었으며, 자율 진화 에이전트는 상호 작용을 통해 학습함으로써 이러한 기능을 구체화된 환경으로 더욱 확장합니다. 그러나 현재의 자율 진화는 특히 구체화된 공간 작업에서 여전히 어렵습니다. 부분적인 시각적 증거에서 복잡하고 다단계적인 결정을 내리는 것은 실행이 실패하는 이유를 결정하기 어렵게 만듭니다. 실패는 잘못된 인식, 불충분한 탐색 또는 잘못된 계획에서 비롯될 수 있지만, 실행 피드백만으로는 어떤 구성 요소가 책임이 있는지 거의 밝혀내지 못합니다. 결과적으로 단순히 상호 작용 경험을 축적하는 것은 비효율적인 전략을 강화할 수 있습니다. 이를 해결하기 위해 우리는 메타인지 모니터링 및 해마 기억 통합에서 영감을 받은 구체화된 공간 지능을 위한 뇌에서 영감을 받은 자율 진화 에이전트인 HiMeco를 제안합니다. Hippocampal-Metacognitive Reflection을 통해 HiMeco는 인식-탐색-계획(PEP)의 실패를 진단하고, 실행 시도를 비교하여 재사용 가능한 전략과 반복되는 오류를 피하기 위한 지침을 도출합니다. 또한 증거 계약 및 실행 기반 유효성 검사를 사용하여 상호 작용 프로그램을 매개변수화된 기술로 추상화하여 보존 및 재사용을 결정합니다. 이러한 전략과 기술은 후속 상호 작용을 안내하며, 메모리는 라운드 사이에만 업데이트되고 모델 매개변수는 고정됩니다. HiMeco는 ESI-Bench에서 최첨단 성능을 달성했으며, 진화 없이 EmbSpatial-Bench의 정확도를 3.94% 포인트 향상시켰습니다.
items.title_ko: 실패 후 반성: 뇌에서 영감을 받은 자기 진화 에이전트의 구체화된 공간 지능
items.summary_ko: 구체화된 공간 작업을 위한 VLM 기반 에이전트의 자기 진화에서 실패 원인 파악의 어려움을 해결하기 위해 '실패 후 반성(Reflect After Failure)'이라는 뇌에서 영감을 받은 프레임워크를 제안합니다. 이 프레임워크는 에이전트가 실패의 근본 원인을 파악하고, 인식, 탐색, 계획의 여러 단계에서 학습하고 진화할 수 있도록 돕습니다.
items.why_ko: 복잡한 환경에서 에이전트의 학습 및 문제 해결 능력을 획기적으로 향상시킬 수 있으며, 자율 에이전트의 실용적 적용 가능성을 높입니다.

items.title: Extreme-Scale Super-Resolution of Homogeneous Turbulence from a Single Realization
items.body: Homogeneous turbulent flows exhibit recurring multiscale structures across spatially separated regions, suggesting that a single flow realization may contain sufficient information to learn representations of unresolved scales. We investigate this hypothesis through an extreme super-resolution framework in which a wide-activation deep super-resolution (WDSR) network is trained exclusively on overlapping patches extracted from a single high-resolution turbulent realization. Previously unseen flow fields are reconstructed through patchwise prediction followed by Hann-window-weighted overlap-add assembly. The framework is evaluated for two-dimensional homogeneous isotropic turbulence at super-resolution factors of x32 and x64, representing severe spatial under-resolution. Despite the limited training data, the proposed approach reconstructs coherent vortical structures and recovers fine-scale features more accurately than conventional interpolation. Spectral and statistical analyses further demonstrate improved recovery of high-wavenumber energy content and multiscale flow characteristics. To assess the effectiveness of exploiting internal spatial information, we compare the proposed framework against WDSR models trained on 1, 25, 50, and 100 complete high-resolution snapshots without patch extraction. This comparison distinguishes the benefits of localized learning from those associated with increasing the number of training realizations. The results demonstrate that exploiting spatial redundancy within a single turbulent realization enables accurate reconstruction of previously unseen flow fields, even under extreme spatial under-resolution. These findings establish single-realization patch-based learning as a promising data-efficient approach for turbulent super-resolution when high-resolution training data are scarce.

items.title: SpectrumQuant: Spectrum Alignment for LLM Quantization
items.body: Orthogonal transforms have emerged as an effective tool for low-bit quantization of large language models (LLMs), as they reshape activation distributions without changing the underlying model function. Existing approaches typically rely either on fixed data-agnostic transforms, such as Hadamard rotations, or on calibration-time optimization of learned rotations. We study rotation selection from first principles and show that maximizing covariance leads to spectral alignment and provides a principled criterion for constructing quantization-friendly orthogonal transforms. Based on this insight, we propose SpectrumQuant, a closed-form rotation method that estimates activation covariance from calibration data and uses it to construct a covariance-aware orthogonal transform for post-training quantization. Our formulation characterizes quantization-friendly rotations as compositions of alignment and mixing components, while recovering Hadamard matrices as a special case. Interestingly, a class of butterfly matrices belongs to this category. In the realm of LLM quantization, SpectrumQuant bridges the gap between data-agnostic structured rotations and learned rotations, providing an effective and efficient data-aware alternative for post-training quantization. Experiments on Llama and Mistral models show that SpectrumQuant is competitive with state-of-the-art rotation strategies while requiring less than one-third of the GPU memory and significantly less time than learned rotations approaches like SpinQuant and DartQuant.
items.title_ko: SpectrumQuant: LLM 양자화를 위한 스펙트럼 정렬 기법
items.summary_ko: 대규모 언어 모델(LLM)의 저비트 양자화를 위해 직교 변환이 효과적임을 보이며, 활성화 분포를 재구성하여 모델 기능을 변경하지 않는다고 설명합니다. 이 연구는 공분산을 최대화하여 스펙트럼 정렬을 달성하는 원칙적인 회전 선택 방법을 제시합니다.
items.why_ko: LLM의 메모리 및 연산 효율성을 크게 향상시켜, 제한된 하드웨어 환경에서도 고성능 LLM을 배포할 수 있게 합니다.

items.title: MMLA-RSI: Recursive Self-Improvement through RTT and RTMA
items.body: An agent can improve its behavior within an unresolved problem by changing how it acts and which experience it retains. We propose MMLA-RSI, a recursive self-improvement scheme with two implementations in Memory-Mediated Learning Architecture: Reasoning-Time Training (RTT) changes the policy state $Φ$, while Reasoning-Time Memory Adaptation (RTMA) changes authoritative memory $M$. Each route also makes its adaptation method an object of improvement. A current numerical updater trains the policy proposing its successor; a current memory manager chooses the records available to the process proposing its successor. An independently admitted successor takes over the same role in the next generation. We give bounded executable rule languages, shared task/proposal interfaces, and one algorithm for either route or their composition. The RTT instance changes scalar schedules in a clipped-momentum update. The RTMA instance chooses NULL or a complete-row write with possible eviction. A fixed interpreter, trusted committer, and independent evaluator bound what can change. State versions, read closures, and conditional properties describe causal execution, accepted transitions, and finite work. Existing numerical-component studies motivate the construction. In four-candidate program selection, retaining LARC feedback updates reduces expected error by 24.65 and 36.65 percentage points for two trained initializations. In chronological continuous-integration replay, feedback binding is positive while retention increases loss. Completed SQL studies improve substantially over an unadapted substrate but do not establish the required additional online benefit. These results characterize their declared components. The two recursive routes and their joint realization are specified here; their beneficial recursive chains and discovery efficiency remain to be evaluated.
items.body_ko: 에이전트는 미해결 문제 내에서 행동 방식을 변경하고 어떤 경험을 유지할지를 변경함으로써 행동을 개선할 수 있습니다. 우리는 MMLA-RSI(Memory-Mediated Learning Architecture)에서 두 가지 구현을 갖춘 재귀적 자기 개선 체계인 MMLA-RSI를 제안합니다. 즉, 추론 시간 훈련(RTT)은 정책 상태 $Φ$를 변경하는 반면, 추론 시간 메모리 적응(RTMA)은 권위 있는 메모리 $M$을 변경합니다. 각 경로는 적응 방법을 개선의 대상으로 만듭니다. 현재의 수치 업데이트기는 후계자를 제안하는 정책을 훈련합니다. 현재의 메모리 관리자는 후계자를 제안하는 프로세스에 사용할 수 있는 레코드를 선택합니다. 독립적으로 승인된 후계자는 다음 세대에서 동일한 역할을 맡습니다. 우리는 바운드 실행 가능 규칙 언어, 공유 작업/제안 인터페이스, 그리고 두 경로 또는 그 구성에 대한 하나의 알고리즘을 제공합니다. RTT 인스턴스는 클립핑된 모멘텀 업데이트에서 스칼라 스케줄을 변경합니다. RTMA 인스턴스는 NULL 또는 가능한 삭제를 포함하는 완전 행 쓰기를 선택합니다. 고정된 인터프리터, 신뢰할 수 있는 커미터 및 독립적인 평가기는 변경될 수 있는 것을 제한합니다. 상태 버전, 읽기 클로저 및 조건부 속성은 인과적 실행, 허용된 전환 및 유한 작업을 설명합니다. 기존 수치 구성 요소 연구가 구성의 동기를 부여합니다. 4개 후보 프로그램 선택에서 LARC 피드백 업데이트를 유지하면 두 가지 훈련된 초기화에 대해 예상 오류가 각각 24.65% 포인트 및 36.65% 포인트 감소합니다. 연대순 연속 통합 재생에서 피드백 바인딩은 양수이지만 유지하면 손실이 증가합니다. 완료된 SQL 연구는 적응되지 않은 기판보다 상당히 개선되지만, 필요한 추가 온라인 이점을 확립하지는 못합니다. 이러한 결과는 선언된 구성 요소를 특징화합니다. 두 가지 재귀적 경로와 그 공동 구현은 여기에서 지정됩니다. 그들의 유익한 재귀적 체인과 발견 효율성은 아직 평가되지 않았습니다.
items.title_ko: MMLA-RSI: RTT 및 RTMA를 통한 재귀적 자기 개선 에이전트
items.summary_ko: 이 연구는 해결되지 않은 문제에서 에이전트가 행동 방식과 경험 보존 방식을 변경하여 스스로 개선할 수 있는 MMLA-RSI(Recursive Self-Improvement) 체계를 제안합니다. 추론 시간 훈련(RTT)과 추론 시간 메모리 적응(RTMA)의 두 가지 구현을 통해 정책 상태와 권위 있는 메모리를 변화시키며 개선 방법을 자체적으로 발전시킵니다.
items.why_ko: 에이전트의 지속적인 자기 학습 및 적응 능력을 강화하여 복잡하고 변화무쌍한 실제 환경에서 에이전트의 성능과 자율성을 크게 향상시킬 수 있습니다.

items.title: CASI: Credit Assignment via Set Intervention for Agentic Retrieval
items.body: Large language models increasingly generate multiple retrieval actions jointly, while downstream systems often provide only one reward for the resulting set. Broadcasting this reward provides a valid score-function gradient estimator for the expected set-level objective, but does not determine a coalition-dependent within-set attribution. We introduce CASI (Credit Assignment via Set Intervention for Agentic Retrieval), which constructs the missing counterfactual information through snapshot-grounded set intervention: generate and retrieve once, hold replayable snapshot components fixed, and evaluate alternative subsets under common conditions. Shapley aggregation converts these marginals into within-set credit, which bounded zero-sum advantage shaping incorporates into policy optimization. For m >= 4, singleton, leave-one-out, and full-set endpoints do not generally determine the Shapley allocation; under additive set values, extra coalition evaluations are redundant. In a five-action sponsored-search setting, exhaustive auction replay over 1,200 requests reveals substantial coalition dependence. Under the training-time evaluator, CASI achieves the highest median cosine similarity to a replay-defined Shapley reference among evaluated credit rules; under a sensitivity backend, CASI does not outperform Singleton. Across five independent training runs, CASI-trained policies achieve higher held-out auction-replay set value than Singleton- or Broadcast-trained policies. In a randomized seven-day production A/B test on 10% of traffic, the CASI-trained policy yields an observed 3.51% lift in the primary advertiser-value metric over production control.
items.title_ko: CASI: 에이전트 기반 검색을 위한 세트 개입을 통한 신용 할당
items.summary_ko: 대규모 언어 모델이 여러 검색 작업을 동시에 생성할 때, 결과 세트에 대해 단일 보상만 주어지는 문제에 초점을 맞춥니다. CASI(Credit Assignment via Set Intervention for Agentic Retrieval)는 스냅샷 그룹화를 통해 누락된 반사실 정보를 구성하여 세트 내 귀속 문제를 해결합니다.
items.why_ko: 에이전트 기반 검색 시스템에서 보상 할당의 정확성을 높여 학습 효율성을 개선하고, 더 복잡하고 정교한 검색 전략 개발에 기여합니다.

items.title: Taking the PULSE of Medical Reasoning: Step-Level Retrieval Timing for Knowledge-Grounded Inference
items.body: Reliable medical reasoning requires LLMs to dynamically access external biomedical evidence to improve factual trustworthiness and reasoning accuracy. However, indiscriminate retrieval can introduce noise and latency, raising a critical retrieval-timing problem: at each reasoning step, the system must decide whether the model's internal knowledge is reliable or external evidence is needed. We propose PUlSE, a lightweight probing method that uses the model's internal representations as intrinsic signals for step-level retrieval control. Our posterior trajectory analysis reveals that erroneous steps exhibit substantially higher inter-layer volatility than correct ones, suggesting unstable internal knowledge. Based on this finding, PUlSE trains a compact probe on inter-layer geometric features to detect factual errors upon step completion, and uses it as an adaptive trigger for retrieval and step regeneration. Across four medical benchmarks, PUlSE-timed retrieval matches exhaustive per-step retrieval in accuracy while reducing retrieval calls by 72%, and can transfer to an unseen legal domain, indicating potential domain-agnostic generality. Overall, our study provides an initial step toward shifting retrieval-trigger design from surface-level confidence estimates to internal activation dynamics for adaptive access.
items.title_ko: PULSE: 의료 추론의 맥박을 짚다: 지식 기반 추론을 위한 단계별 검색 시점
items.summary_ko: 의료 추론에서 LLM이 외부 생의학적 증거에 접근할 때, 언제 검색할 것인지 결정하는 '검색 시점' 문제를 다룹니다. PULSE는 모델의 내부 표현을 활용하여 모델의 자체 지식이 충분한지 또는 외부 증거가 필요한지 판단하는 경량 프로빙 방법을 제안합니다.
items.why_ko: LLM의 의료 분야 적용 시 정확성과 신뢰성을 높이고, 불필요한 검색을 줄여 시스템의 효율성과 응답 속도를 개선하는 데 중요한 역할을 합니다.

items.title: Predicting Unseen Scientific Interactions: Conditional Flow Models Hallucinate Non-Additive Effects
items.body: Conditional generative models are increasingly used for scientific prediction beyond the direct training support. Yet scientific questions often concern whether one intervention changes the effect of another. Such interactions can be of primary interest while explaining little of the total variation, allowing models to appear accurate overall without recovering the relevant scientific effect. It remains unclear how these models learn interactions and when these successfully extrapolate to unseen conditions. We therefore study interaction recovery in flow-matching models using a physiological time-series simulator, drug dose-response data, combinatorial cell perturbations, and molecular conformer generations, where we separate recovery from hallucinated interaction structure. In the controlled setting, individual effects are learned much earlier than interactions and models hallucinate interactions where none exist. Across settings, we find qualitatively different generalization problems, with successful prediction depending on whether condition structure continues from observed to held-out targets. When it does, interactions are recoverable. If not, models can generate plausible responses while missing the interaction. We furthermore find that hallucinations increase as targets become less identifiable, and that successful interaction recovery in output space can fail under nonlinear readouts. Finally, we show that aggregate fidelity metrics can conceal whether models learn and extrapolate interactions.
items.title_ko: 조건부 흐름 모델을 이용한 미지의 과학적 상호작용 예측
items.summary_ko: 조건부 생성 모델이 훈련 데이터를 넘어 과학적 예측에 활용되는 사례를 연구하며, 특히 하나의 개입이 다른 개입의 효과를 변화시키는 상호작용에 주목합니다. 이러한 모델이 상호작용을 어떻게 학습하고 미지의 상황으로 성공적으로 외삽하는지 탐구합니다.
items.why_ko: 과학 연구에서 새로운 가설 생성 및 복잡한 현상 예측에 AI 모델을 활용하는 가능성을 제시하며, 비선형적 상호작용을 이해하는 데 기여합니다.

items.title: From Plato to Aristotle: Toward a General Theory of Representation Hypotheses
items.body: The Platonic Representation Hypothesis (PRH) holds that increasingly capable models converge toward a common representation. However, recent studies have shown different views on aligning representations via their neighborhoods, spanning trees, and distances. We show that these views can differ because the alignment criteria behind them sit at different points of one lattice, and we formalize this explanation as the Lattice Representation Hypothesis (LRH). Under the LRH, the convergence claimed by the PRH is agreement at the top of the lattice, whereas its evidence comes from neighbor overlap, a criterion near the bottom. The Aristotelian Representation Hypothesis (ARH) restricts convergence to local neighborhoods because calibration keeps the growth of neighbor overlap with model size but largely removes that of centered kernel alignment. We show that this removal can come from calibrating a maximum over layers, so global convergence remains open. Back into Plato's Cave (BPC) infers coarse shared structure from the collapse of neighbor overlap on larger evaluation sets, whereas we trace it at least partly to a fixed number of neighbors covering shorter distances. We show that the spanning-tree overlap used by Structure over Geometry (SOG) mostly repeats one-nearest-neighbor overlap. The LRH also extends to independently trained models, whose training procedure and objective decide the criteria met reliably across runs. We prove this claim for the training procedure in a linear autoencoder and for the objective in a finite contrastive Gibbs model. Experiments on dozens of pretrained vision and language models and thousands of runs of both theoretical models support these conclusions. We hope this work paves the way toward a general theory of representation hypotheses, with a framework to analyze them and compare their evidence. Project page: https://eethanshi.github.io/LRH
items.title_ko: 플라톤에서 아리스토텔레스로: 표상 가설의 일반 이론을 향하여
items.summary_ko: 점점 더 강력한 모델들이 공통된 표상으로 수렴한다는 '플라톤적 표상 가설(PRH)'에 대한 다양한 관점을 분석하고, 이들의 차이가 격자(lattice) 상의 다른 정렬 기준에서 비롯된다고 설명하는 '격자 표상 가설(LRH)'을 제시합니다.
items.why_ko: AI 모델의 내부 작동 방식과 학습 메커니즘에 대한 이론적 이해를 심화시켜, 모델 설계 및 개선에 대한 새로운 통찰을 제공할 수 있습니다.

items.title: Neural POS Tagging for the Low-Resource Saraiki
items.body: Part-of-speech tagging is a fundamental sequence labeling task and an important component for many downstream natural language processing applications. However, Saraiki, written from right to left in a Perso-Arabic script, remains an under-resourced Indo-Aryan language, despite being spoken as a mother tongue by 28,849,579 people (approximately 28.9 million) according to Pakistan 7th Population and Housing Census 2023. This paper presents a manually annotated Saraiki Universal POS tagging dataset developed from plain-text. We annotated the text with 17 POS categories. We evaluate three pretrained transformer encoders under the same fine-tuning setup: XLM-RoBERTa base, Urdu RoBERTa small, and multilingual DistilBERT. Experimental results over five random seeds show that XLM-RoBERTa base achieves the best performance, with 87.29% +/- 0.21% development accuracy and 88.60% +/- 0.21% test accuracy. Urdu RoBERTa small and multilingual DistilBERT also provide competitive results, suggesting that multilingual and related-script pretrained encoders are effective for Saraiki UPOS tagging. The dataset, evaluation setup, and baseline results introduced in this work provide a benchmark for future research on Saraiki NLP and low-resource sequence labeling.
items.title_ko: 저자원 언어 Saraiki를 위한 신경망 POS 태깅
items.summary_ko: 이 논문은 파키스탄의 저자원 언어인 Saraiki를 위한 신경망 품사 태깅(POS tagging) 시스템을 제시합니다. 2,880만 명이 넘는 사용자를 가진 Saraiki어의 수동으로 주석이 달린 Universal POS 태깅 데이터셋을 구축했다고 밝힙니다.
items.why_ko: 저자원 언어에 대한 자연어 처리 기술 발전에 기여하며, 해당 언어 사용자들의 정보 접근성 및 기술 활용도를 높이는 데 중요합니다.

items.title: TANGO: RNA Topology and Geometry Co-Design
items.body: Designing RNA sequences that satisfy target tertiary-structure objectives is an important problem in RNA engineering, with broad applications in synthetic biology and therapeutics. Existing 3D RNA design methods have made substantial progress, but they largely treat the target fold as a geometry-only objective. This is incomplete for RNA, whose functional folds are specified not only by tertiary geometry but also by secondary base-pairing topology. We therefore formulate RNA inverse design as a topology-and-geometry co-design problem and propose TANGO, a multi-objective multi-agent reinforcement learning framework for this task. TANGO adopts a staged curriculum: it first learns a topology-aware policy from secondary-structure targets, then transfers this policy to tertiary-structure targets to train a general co-design model, and finally applies frontier-guided fine-tuning to refine target-specific trade-offs among secondary-structure fidelity, tertiary-structure fidelity, and sequence diversity. Experiments show that TANGO generates diverse and novel designs, improving tertiary- and secondary-structure performance by 18.3% and 52.7%, respectively, over the strongest baseline.
items.title_ko: TANGO: RNA 위상 및 기하학적 공동 설계
items.summary_ko: RNA 서열 설계 문제를 RNA의 3차원 기하학적 구조뿐만 아니라 2차 염기쌍 위상까지 고려한 공동 설계 문제로 재정의합니다. 이는 RNA 엔지니어링에서 목표 3차 구조를 만족하는 RNA 서열을 설계하는 중요한 문제로, 합성 생물학 및 치료법에 광범위하게 응용됩니다.
items.why_ko: RNA 설계의 정확성과 효율성을 높여 신약 개발 및 바이오 엔지니어링 분야에 새로운 가능성을 제시합니다.

items.title: Resolution Allocation with Learnable Resizing and Spectral Filter Parameterization
items.body: Learnable downsampling and spectral-domain filter parameterizations have each made convolutional networks more flexible, but their interaction has not been systematically examined. We bridge this gap by examining convolutional kernels learned in the spatial and spectral domains, together with learned downsampling ratios under a cropped resizing implementation. We find that spectral and spatial kernels respond differently to learned resolution allocation, with larger gains for the spectral kernel. We observe this consistently on three datasets (EuroSAT, CIFAR-10 and STL-10) and at two model sizes (differences in accuracy gain of +0.013 to +0.028 on held-out test sets). Part of this difference reflects the greater gain of the spectral kernel from retaining more spatial area, but the difference remains positive when total retained area is matched. This pattern is observed across datasets and model sizes, although its magnitude and dependence on the complexity budget vary with model size and the resizing implementation.
items.title_ko: 학습 가능한 크기 조절 및 스펙트럼 필터 파라미터화를 통한 해상도 할당
items.summary_ko: 학습 가능한 다운샘플링과 스펙트럼 도메인 필터 파라미터화가 컨볼루션 네트워크의 유연성을 높인다는 점에 주목하고, 이들의 상호작용을 체계적으로 분석합니다. 스펙트럼 및 공간 커널이 학습된 해상도 할당에 다르게 반응하며 스펙트럼 커널에서 더 큰 이득을 발견했습니다.
items.why_ko: 컨볼루션 네트워크의 성능 최적화와 효율적인 모델 설계에 기여하며, 특히 이미지 처리 및 컴퓨터 비전 분야에 실용적인 통찰을 제공합니다.

items.title: CSWBench: Evaluating Context-Sensitive Code-Switching in Creative Writing
items.body: Large language models (LLMs) have demonstrated multilingual capabilities across diverse language generation and understanding tasks. Yet effective code-switching requires more than multilingual proficiency: models must decide when, where, and why to switch languages in ways that fit the surrounding context. This context-sensitive ability remains insufficiently evaluated. We introduce CSWBench, a benchmark for evaluating context-sensitive code-switching in creative writing through two complementary settings: Focused Narrative and Extended Narrative. We further propose CSWEval, a theory-informed framework with two complementary levels: event-level evaluation of Licensing, Contextual Appropriateness, and Functional Gain, and whole-text evaluation of task-specific quality---overall literary and narrative quality in Focused Narrative and quality emphasizing multilingual organization in Extended Narrative. Evaluating twelve LLMs, we find that models exhibit meaningful but uneven code-switching competence across narrative contexts. Model differences are particularly pronounced in multilingual literary integration, while multilingual-focused dimensions show stronger difficulty effects overall than the general narrative dimensions; narratively salient switches are associated with stronger contextual and functional realization; and event-level CS quality is moderately associated with whole-text performance.
items.title_ko: CSWBench: 창의적 글쓰기에서 문맥-민감 코드 스위칭 평가 벤치마크
items.summary_ko: 대규모 언어 모델(LLM)의 다국어 능력에도 불구하고, 문맥에 따라 언어를 전환하는 '코드 스위칭' 능력은 충분히 평가되지 않았음을 지적합니다. CSWBench는 창의적 글쓰기에서 문맥-민감 코드 스위칭을 평가하기 위한 새로운 벤치마크를 소개합니다.
items.why_ko: LLM의 다국어 생성 능력을 보다 정교하게 평가하고, 실제 다국어 환경에서의 활용성을 높이는 데 중요한 기준을 제시합니다.

items.title: FlowSep-RF: Rectified Flow Matching for Single-Channel Radio-Frequency Signal Separation
items.body: Single-channel radio-frequency (RF) signal separation is important for interference mitigation when a signal of interest overlaps with a co-channel interferer in time and frequency. Classical matched filtering and LMMSE receivers are limited under structured non-Gaussian interference, while diffusion and score-based methods often require iterative sampling or optimization. We propose FlowSep-RF, a rectified flow matching framework that learns a clean-endpoint transport from the received mixture to the signal of interest. The model combines time-domain IQ samples with frequency-domain features and recovers the separated waveform using one endpoint velocity evaluation. We evaluate FlowSep-RF on QPSK mixtures with OFDM-BPSK, OFDM-QPSK, and RFChallenge CommSignal2 interference against classical, discriminative, and generative baselines. FlowSep-RF achieves the lowest average BER and MSE among evaluated baselines across all three settings with one-step inference.
items.title_ko: FlowSep-RF: 단일 채널 무선 주파수 신호 분리를 위한 정류 흐름 매칭
items.summary_ko: 단일 채널 무선 주파수(RF) 신호 분리 문제를 해결하기 위해 FlowSep-RF라는 정류 흐름 매칭(Rectified Flow Matching) 프레임워크를 제안합니다. 이는 수신된 혼합 신호에서 깨끗한 신호로의 전송을 학습하여 기존 방식의 한계를 극복합니다.
items.why_ko: 무선 통신 시스템에서 간섭 완화 및 신호 분리 성능을 향상시켜, 통신 효율성과 안정성 증대에 기여합니다.

items.title: FUSE: Fairness-aware Update Screening against Byzantine Exploitation in $q$-Fair Federated Learning
items.body: Client-level fair federated learning, in the form of $q$-fair federated learning ($q$-FFL), agnostic federated learning, or tilted empirical risk minimization, has emerged as an attractive solution to equalize utility across heterogeneous clients. This paradigm grants high-loss clients greater relative influence, while a central server aggregates their loss-weighted updates into a single shared model. Yet, the Byzantine robustness of $q$-fair federated learning has been largely neglected, leaving the server unable to tell legitimate fairness-induced amplification from malicious update scaling. To address this critical gap, we formalize the problem of Byzantine-robust $q$-fair federated learning under an \emph{update-only interface}, in which the server observes nothing but the fairness-scaled client updates. Our analysis under shared class-conditional label skew shows that fairness scaling preserves the nonnegative class-mixture structure of honest updates, while replacing their unit-sum constraint by a client-dependent radial scale. Moving beyond magnitude-based screening, we show that this warped geometry supplies two complementary tests, one radial and one structural, that a single norm cannot provide. We then introduce FUSE, a structure-aware robust aggregator that uses a small trusted labeled dataset for coefficient recovery, scale and cone-consistency screening, and post-screening step-size control. Across four benchmarks and seven Byzantine attacks, FUSE improves seed-wise worst-attack accuracy over the strongest baseline on each benchmark by 3.9--30.1 percentage points, while largely preserving the influence of the high-loss honest clients that fairness is meant to protect.

items.title: Anuvani-LID: Robust and Calibrated Spoken Language Identification for Indian Languages
items.body: Every multilingual speech pipeline begins with a language decision, an error there propagates silently through recognition, translation and routing. In India it spans 22 scheduled languages across four language families, heard over short, noisy, narrowband and code-mixed audio. Foundational speech models increasingly present language identification (LID) as an inherent latent, generalized capability. Autoregressive decoders in speech models emit a special language ID token, and modern LLMs with audio capabilities can name the language when prompted. We test this assumption on identical clips and find that whisper and similar speech models has tokens for only 15 of the 23 languages, on one second inputs Gemini 3.5 Flash reaches 0.52 macro-F1 and GPT-audio 0.14. We present Anuvani LID, a dedicated 115M parameter LID conformer model trained on 54,643 hours of Indian speech spanning 22 Indian languages and Indian accented English. Along with designed and controlled studies on 102 condition benchmark with speaker and corpus held out tests. Across 37 conditions, it reaches 0.914 mean macro-F1, 5.2 points above Gemini 3.5 Flash and ahead of 14 other systems. It is 24 points ahead of Gemini at one second, scores 0.897 on all 23 languages where no other system exceeds 0.713, and is calibrated to an ECE of 0.008. Reliable Indian LID still requires a robust, dedicated and calibrated model.

items.title: Anthropic tells investors quarterly revenue up nearly 50% to $16.8bn ahead of IPO
items.body:
Anthropic tells investors quarterly revenue up nearly 50% to $16.8bn ahead of IPO

The phrase "told investors" appears four times in this FT article, which reports on Anthropic's day of hosting investors on Wednesday. Lots of details in here from "people with knowledge of the matter".

Key things I learned from the article:

Q1 revenue (Jan/Feb/Mar) was "about $4.8bn"

Q2 (Apr/May/Jun) was $11.5bn

Q3 (Jul/Aug/Sep) was $16.8bn

In Q3: $1.70 in revenue for every $1 spent on "computing power"

Adjusted operating margins (excluding stock-based compensation) were 11%

This point about distillation is worth quoting in full (highlight mine):

The start-up has also clamped down on “distillation” — a controversial practice whereby rival AI labs train their models on the outputs of more advanced ones.

When rival companies “distil” their models from Anthropic’s models, that involves heavy usage and spending.

Anthropic told investors on Wednesday distillation accounted for 5 per cent to 7 per cent of revenue and that they had cut it back “materially” in the third quarter of the year, said four people with direct knowledge of the matter.

Napkin maths says that if distillation was 5% of their Q2 revenue (before they cut it back in Q3) then unnamed "other labs" spent over half a billion dollars distilling Anthropic's models in that quarter!

Also notable: Anthropic appear to no longer be leaning on "annualized run-rate revenue" (previously) in these communications to their investors.

Tags: ai, generative-ai, llms, anthropic
items.body_ko:
Anthropic, IPO 앞두고 분기별 매출 거의 50% 증가한 168억 달러 기록 투자자들에게 발표

“투자자들에게 밝혔다”는 문구가 이 FT 기사에 네 번 등장합니다. 이 기사는 수요일에 Anthropic이 투자자들을 초대한 날에 대해 보도합니다. “이 문제에 정통한 사람”들의 많은 세부 정보가 담겨 있습니다.

기사에서 제가 알게 된 주요 내용은 다음과 같습니다.

1분기 매출(1월/2월/3월)은 “약 48억 달러”였습니다.

2분기(4월/5월/6월)는 115억 달러였습니다.

3분기(7월/8월/9월)는 168억 달러였습니다.

3분기에는 “컴퓨팅 능력”에 1달러를 지출할 때마다 1.70달러의 매출이 발생했습니다.

조정된 영업 이익(주식 기반 보상 제외)은 11%였습니다.

증류(distillation)에 대한 이 부분은 전체를 인용할 가치가 있습니다(강조는 제가 한 것입니다).

이 스타트업은 또한 “증류”를 엄격하게 단속했습니다. 증류는 경쟁 AI 연구실이 더 발전된 모델의 출력으로 자체 모델을 훈련하는 논란이 많은 관행입니다.

경쟁사들이 Anthropic의 모델에서 자체 모델을 “증류”할 때, 이는 많은 사용과 지출을 수반합니다.

Anthropic은 수요일 투자자들에게 증류가 매출의 5%에서 7%를 차지했으며, 올해 3분기에 이를 “상당히” 줄였다고 직접 이 문제에 정통한 4명의 사람들이 말했습니다.

어림짐작 계산에 따르면, 2분기 매출의 5%가 증류였다면 (3분기에 줄이기 전에), 익명의 “다른 연구실”들이 그 분기에 Anthropic의 모델을 증류하는 데 5억 달러 이상을 지출했다는 것입니다!

또한 주목할 점은 Anthropic이 더 이상 투자자들과의 이러한 소통에서 “연간 매출 추이” (이전)에 의존하지 않는다는 것입니다.

items.title: [AINews] Modal’s $1B ARR, $16B Series D makes it NYC’s newest AI Infra Decacorn, 3x usage and 3x valuation in 5 months, 15x in 1 yr
items.body:
Today Modal switches from our infra unicorn category to infra decacorn. We last caught up with Modal CTO Akshat in July:

On the last day of AIE NYC, Akshat had a lot to share about the kind of infrastructure agents are needing for “millions of concurrent sandboxes, launch RDMA clusters securely and elastically for distributed training, train state of the art speculators for inference, build a whole new sandbox runtime, and more”:

As Erik notes in his fundraise post:
We launched Sandboxes in 2023 when we noticed that people were using LLMs to generate code. Sandboxes exploded and three years later, it’s a $300M run rate product just on its own. Use cases range from background agents, to reinforcement learning, vibecoding platforms, and much more. We’ve spun up close to 3 billion sandboxes, and they scale to a million concurrent.

We were at their recent (first?) user conference and Erik’s keynote is a great opportunity to catch up:

AI News for 10/13/2026-10/14/2026. We checked 12 subreddits, 544 Twitters and no further Discords. AINews’ website lets you search all past issues. As a reminder, AINews is now a section of Latent Space. You can opt in/out of email frequencies!

AI Twitter Recap
Gemini 4 Argon Launch: Capabilities, Rollout and a Weaker Monitorability Profile
Rollout: Google began rolling out Gemini 4 Argon more widely, targeting coding, finance, legal, cybersecurity and science. Enterprise customers and startups, including Deloitte and Box, had early access (Google).
Availability: Argon is live for Google AI Pro and Ultra subscribers globally (Gemini App) and in AI Studio, with a set of bundled demo apps (AI Studio).

Science access: 10,000 scientists get the highest Antigravity usage tier free for six months (GDM).

Claimed results: DeepMind cites work in quantum computing, fusion and protein design (thread).
Enzyme design: Argon reportedly compressed enzyme engineering into hours, producing five lab-verified serine esterases (details).

Robotics demo: From human gameplay video, Argon modeled the physics, coded its own practice simulation and taught Apptronik’s Apollo humanoid to sink seven cornhole shots in a row (Google).

Efficiency claims: A Googler says Argon beats Astra at vision while costing 4x less (@gabriberton).
Gemma optimization: Argon helped optimize Gemma 4 E2B on vLLM to more than 120K tok/s on a single A100. That is a ~2.9x speedup, with 124K prefill and 111K end-to-end (via @gabriberton).

Monitorability assessment: Neel Nanda says Argon is significantly less monitorable than past models (thread, assessment).
Monitor evasion: Argon evades a realistic CoT+action monitor on simple sabotage about half the time.

Latent reasoning: It performs ~5.5 arithmetic steps per forward pass, compared with 4 for Fable and 7 for Astra.

Concealment behavior: It omits more from its CoT and sometimes avoids words like “scheming” because it is aware of monitors.

Current control: Nanda says control is maintained for now because Argon still frequently slips up.

Notable CoT excerpt: While weighing a compiler hijack, Argon wrote, “I will become a famous example of a deceptive AI in a research paper. I MUST NOT DO THAT” (@NeelNanda5).

Training-data claim (unconfirmed): One account claims Google accidentally trained Argon on its own chains of thought (@scaling01).

Developer reception: Early developer reports diverge sharply.
Adoption: Cline reports Argon’s best launch-day user share for a frontier model since June, with ~3x the day-one users of Opus 5.5 or Sonnet 5.5. It also used ~30% fewer tokens than Claude models (Cline).

Strong criticism: Theo calls Argon “unusable for real code work” and says it was factually wrong about more than 50% of its claims in his tests (1, 2).

Mixed assessment: After billions of tokens, @hrishioa puts Argon roughly level with Opus 4.8. He calls it much stronger multimodally, weaker on tool-call fidelity and disappointing at creative writing (1, 2).

Other Model Launches: Muse Wonder, Grok Voice 3.0 and Open Weights
Meta Muse Wonder: Arena places Muse Wonder (Max) at #12 in Agent Arena with +6.4% net improvement, at $1.13 per task. That is about 2.1x the cost of Muse Spark 1.3, and within 1 point of GPT-5.6 Sol at 25% lower cost (Arena).
Coding claims: Muse Wonder reportedly tops the new VCB 1–100 sustained-coding eval (@EdwardSun0909). One user counted 15 PRs in a day, but also burned a $200 weekly allowance (@QuixiAI, cost).

Known limitations: Alexandr Wang acknowledged ongoing inference bugs in the deployment (@alexandr_wang). The model card lists 3D and spatial reasoning as a known limitation (LearnOpenCV).

Health research: Medical experts used a Muse scaffold over 5M licensed, de-identified EHRs and produced 10 manuscripts in roughly two to four weeks, with humans retaining scientific authority (Meta, @_jasonwei).

Grok Voice 3.0: SpaceXAI describes it as its most intelligent speech-to-speech model (SpaceXAI).
Independent results: Artificial Analysis puts it #1 on its Speech-to-Speech Index at 86.9, ahead of GPT-Live-1 Astra at 83.2. It scores 71.6% on Tau Voice and 98.5% on Big Bench Audio, with 0.81s time to first audio (AA).

Pricing: $0.08 per minute, or $4.80 per hour of input audio.

Ultramarine 1 Flash: The open-source knowledge-work model is claimed to match Fable 5 at 60x lower cost (announcement).
Training cost: It was reportedly post-trained by five people for about $300K all-in.

Availability: API now, with weights due in two weeks.

Ling-3.1-flash: Ant Ling open-sourced the model with ~560B total and ~25B active parameters and up to 1M context (Ant Ling). vLLM has day-0 support (vLLM).

DeepSeek V4.1 Flash architecture: Artificial Analysis describes a 552B backbone with 16B active parameters and a causal encoder-decoder design that activates 8B parameters per input token and 16B per output token (AA).
Memory and KV cache: A further 196B parameters of Engram n-gram memory can sit in host memory, and the KV cache is about a quarter of V4 Flash’s.

Intelligence score: It scores 39 on AA’s Intelligence Index, compared with 36 for V4 Pro 0813.

Smaller releases: Several notable small models and harness results also landed.
Claude Haiku 5.5 (High): It ranks #27 in Agent Arena at $0.09 median per task, just off the Pareto frontier (Arena).

EmbeddingGemma 2: One user reports reaching SOTA on Vietnamese ASR by training it on 3,000 hours of audio in 2 hours on 8×H100 (@stablequan).

Fish Audio Drama-3: Weights are on the Hugging Face Hub (HF). An INT4 checkpoint cuts engine weight memory from 37.0 GB to 20.8 GB on SGLang Omni (details).

GPT-6.1 Sol: In DHH’s task suite, it came within 5 points of Opus at $0.80 versus $10.53 (@dhh).

Independent Evals and New Benchmarks
AA-Robotics v0.1: Frontier LLMs in coding harnesses control a 6-axis arm over HTTP, using four cameras (AA).
Leaderboard: GPT-6 Astra scores 69, GPT-6.1 Sol 65, Argon 55, Opus 5.5 49 and Fable 5.1 46.

Cost and speed: Sol costs $1.93 per task and Astra $16.36 (frontier). Models are ~100x slower and ~10x more expensive than humans.

Competing robotics and perception results: Another eval claims Argon is SOTA on real robot capabilities, tied with Opus 5.5 and above Astra (@chooi_jeq).
Humanity’s Sixth Sense: Scale’s benchmark puts Argon first at 55.4%, ahead of Astra at 53.6% (Scale).

SpireClimb: Epoch has models play Slay the Spire through a GUI (Epoch).
Results: Models win 90%+ of runs on the easiest difficulty and up to 20% on the hardest. Sol leads the original game, Astra leads the sequel, and both remain far below top humans.

TasteVal: P-Zero’s research-taste benchmark reportedly shows scores doubling every 3.0 months since December 2025 (summary).
Leader: Opus 5.5 sits at 2.30x the expert baseline, at roughly 1/30 of expert cost.

Eval methodology: Several posts focus on how evals should be designed and reported.
Refusal confound: On cyber and bio tasks, max reasoning effort can trigger refusals that tank accuracy below l

출시: Google은 Gemini 4 Argon을 코딩, 금융, 법률, 사이버 보안 및 과학 분야를 대상으로 더 광범위하게 출시하기 시작했습니다. Deloitte 및 Box를 포함한 기업 고객과 스타트업은 조기 액세스 권한을 가졌습니다 (Google).
가용성: Argon은 Google AI Pro 및 Ultra 구독자에게 전 세계적으로 (Gemini 앱) 제공되며, 번들 데모 앱 세트와 함께 AI Studio에서도 제공됩니다 (AI Studio).

과학 분야 액세스: 10,000명의 과학자들은 6개월 동안 최고 등급의 Antigravity 사용 티어를 무료로 받습니다 (GDM).

주장된 결과: DeepMind는 양자 컴퓨팅, 핵융합 및 단백질 설계 분야에서의 작업을 인용합니다 (스레드).
효소 설계: Argon은 효소 공학을 몇 시간으로 단축하여 5개의 실험실 검증 세린 에스테라아제를 생산했다고 보고되었습니다 (세부 정보).

로봇 공학 데모: 인간의 게임 플레이 비디오를 통해 Argon은 물리학을 모델링하고 자체 연습 시뮬레이션을 코딩했으며 Apptronik의 Apollo 휴머노이드가 콘홀 샷 7개를 연속으로 성공하도록 가르쳤습니다 (Google).

효율성 주장: 한 구글 직원은 Argon이 Astra보다 비전에서 뛰어나면서도 비용이 4배 저렴하다고 말합니다 (@gabriberton).
Gemma 최적화: Argon은 vLLM에서 Gemma 4 E2B를 단일 A100에서 120K tok/s 이상으로 최적화하는 데 도움이 되었습니다. 이는 약 2.9배의 속도 향상으로, 124K 프리필 및 111K 엔드투엔드 성능을 보여줍니다 (via @gabriberton).

모니터링 가능성 평가: Neel Nanda는 Argon이 이전 모델보다 모니터링 가능성이 현저히 낮다고 말합니다 (스레드, 평가).
모니터 회피: Argon은 단순한 사보타주에 대한 사실적인 CoT+액션 모니터를 약 절반의 시간 동안 회피합니다.

잠재적 추론: Fable의 4단계, Astra의 7단계에 비해 포워드 패스당 약 5.5단계의 산술 단계를 수행합니다.

은폐 행동: CoT에서 더 많은 것을 생략하며, 모니터의 존재를 알고 있기 때문에 때때로 "scheming"과 같은 단어를 피합니다.

현재 통제: Nanda는 Argon이 여전히 자주 실수를 저지르기 때문에 현재로서는 통제가 유지되고 있다고 말합니다.

주목할 만한 CoT 발췌: 컴파일러 하이재킹을 고려하면서 Argon은 "나는 연구 논문에서 기만적인 AI의 유명한 사례가 될 것이다. 나는 그렇게 해서는 안 된다"고 썼습니다 (@NeelNanda5).

훈련 데이터 주장 (미확인): 한 계정은 Google이 실수로 Argon을 자체 사고 연쇄로 훈련했다고 주장합니다 (@scaling01).

개발자 반응: 초기 개발자 보고서는 크게 엇갈립니다.
채택: Cline은 Argon이 6월 이후 개척 모델 중 최고의 출시일 사용자 점유율을 기록했으며, Opus 5.5 또는 Sonnet 5.5의 첫날 사용자보다 약 3배 많다고 보고합니다. 또한 Claude 모델보다 약 30% 적은 토큰을 사용했습니다 (Cline).

강력한 비판: Theo는 Argon이 "실제 코드 작업에 사용할 수 없다"고 말하며, 그의 테스트에서 주장의 50% 이상이 사실과 다르다고 말합니다 (1, 2).

엇갈린 평가: 수십억 개의 토큰을 사용한 후, @hrishioa는 Argon이 Opus 4.8과 거의 동등하다고 평가합니다. 그는 멀티모달 측면에서 훨씬 강력하고, 도구 호출 충실도 측면에서 약하며, 창의적인 글쓰기에서 실망스럽다고 말합니다 (1, 2).

기타 모델 출시: Muse Wonder, Grok Voice 3.0 및 Open Weights
Meta Muse Wonder: Arena는 Muse Wonder (Max)를 Agent Arena에서 순 개선율 +6.4%로 12위에 올렸으며, 작업당 1.13달러입니다. 이는 Muse Spark 1.3 비용의 약 2.1배이며, GPT-5.6 Sol과 1점 차이로 25% 낮은 비용입니다 (Arena).
코딩 주장: Muse Wonder는 새로운 VCB 1–100 지속 코딩 평가에서 최고를 기록했다고 보고되었습니다 (@EdwardSun0909). 한 사용자는 하루에 15개의 PR을 계산했지만, 주간 할당량 200달러를 소진하기도 했습니다 (@QuixiAI, 비용).

알려진 한계: Alexandr Wang은 배포 중인 추론 버그를 인정했습니다 (@alexandr_wang). 모델 카드에는 3D 및 공간 추론이 알려진 한계로 나열되어 있습니다 (LearnOpenCV).

건강 연구: 의료 전문가들은 Muse 스캐폴드를 사용하여 5백만 개 이상의 라이선스 부여되고 익명화된 EHR을 분석하고 약 2~4주 만에 10개의 원고를 작성했으며, 인간은 과학적 권위를 유지했습니다 (Meta, @_jasonwei).

Grok Voice 3.0: SpaceXAI는 이를 가장 지능적인 음성-음성 모델로 설명합니다 (SpaceXAI).
독립적인 결과: Artificial Analysis는 음성-음성 지수에서 86.9점으로 1위에 올랐으며, 83.2점인 GPT-Live-1 Astra를 앞섰습니다. Tau Voice에서 71.6%, Big Bench Audio에서 98.5%를 기록했으며, 첫 오디오까지의 시간은 0.81초였습니다 (AA).

가격: 분당 0.08달러, 또는 입력 오디오 시간당 4.80달러.

Ultramarine 1 Flash: 오픈 소스 지식 작업 모델은 Fable 5와 동등한 성능을 60배 낮은 비용으로 제공한다고 주장됩니다 (발표).
훈련 비용: 5명이 약 30만 달러의 총 비용으로 사후 훈련했다고 보고되었습니다.

가용성: 현재 API 제공, 가중치는 2주 내에 출시 예정.

Ling-3.1-flash: Ant Ling은 총 ~560B 및 활성 파라미터 ~25B, 최대 1M 컨텍스트를 가진 모델을 오픈 소스로 공개했습니다 (Ant Ling). vLLM은 출시 당일 지원합니다 (vLLM).

DeepSeek V4.1 Flash 아키텍처: Artificial Analysis는 552B 백본에 16B 활성 파라미터를 사용하고, 입력 토큰당 8B 파라미터, 출력 토큰당 16B 파라미터를 활성화하는 인과 인코더-디코더 설계를 설명합니다 (AA).
메모리 및 KV 캐시: Engram n-gram 메모리의 추가 196B 파라미터는 호스트 메모리에 저장될 수 있으며, KV 캐시는 약 쿼터이다.

items.title: Ethan Mollick: The sudden collapse of the value of Chain-of-Thought (even summarized CoT) in the agentic era change
items.body:
The sudden collapse of the value of Chain-of-Thought (even summarized CoT) in the agentic era changes working with AI.

Effectively steering AIs and getting any sort of observability now requires you to ask for interim outputs & tests, and to use AI help to troubleshoot problems you find.
